children.title: Scenario-Expanded Representations
children.top_down_role: Finite-scenario representations organized by stages, histories, paths, and replicated decisions.

children.title: Two-Stage Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Scenario-expanded two-stage recourse representations.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
All displayed functions and feasible sets are well-defined, and a common first-stage decision is required before the scenario is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic extensive form represents the two-stage stochastic program by one shared first-stage variable and scenario-specific recourse variables.

notation.meaning: First-stage feasible set and scenario-specific recourse feasible sets.
First-stage cost and scenario recourse costs.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the stochastic-programming extensive-form statement; a stochastic programming source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario deterministic equivalent with a shared first-stage decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a first-stage feasible set \(X\), recourse sets \(Y_s(x)\), first-stage cost \(f\), and scenario costs \(q_s\), the two-stage extensive form is
\[
\inf_{x,\,(y_s)_{s\in S}}\left\{f(x)+\sum_{s\in S}p_s q_s(x,y_s):x\in X,\ y_s\in Y_s(x)\ \text{for every }s\in S\right\}.
\]
The single variable \(x\) enforces first-stage nonanticipativity, while each \(y_s\) may depend on the realized scenario \(s\). Equivalently, scenario copies \(x_s\) may be introduced together with constraints \(x_s=x_{s'}\) for all \(s,s'\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-stage extensive form uses one common first-stage decision and a separate recourse decision for each scenario, weighting scenario costs by their probabilities.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Extensive Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the two-stage extensive-form container, but no citation is supplied. The deterministic-equivalent formula and the equivalence between a shared first-stage variable and scenario copies require an authoritative stochastic-programming source with a specific locator.

children.title: Multistage Extensive Forms
children.top_down_role: Scenario-expanded multistage representations with history-dependent decisions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T=(N,E)\) is a finite rooted scenario tree with stage map \(\tau:N\to\{1,\ldots,T\}\).
Each nonroot node has a unique parent, and each node has probability mass \(\pi_n>0\).
Feasibility at a node depends only on its decision and the decision at its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Indexing decisions by history nodes yields a finite deterministic extensive form whose feasible decisions are automatically nonanticipative.

notation.meaning: Finite rooted scenario tree, its nodes, and its arcs.
Decision and local cost at history node \(n\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports multistage stochastic extensive forms; a scenario-tree stochastic programming source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario-tree form with decisions adapted to observed histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\) be the root and \(a(n)\) the parent of each \(n\ne r\). A multistage extensive form has the form
\[
\inf_{(x_n)_{n\in N}}\left\{\sum_{n\in N}\pi_n c_n(x_n):x_r\in X_r,\ (x_{a(n)},x_n)\in K_n\ \text{for every }n\ne r\right\}.
\]
Because every node represents one observed history, the variable \(x_n\) is shared by all terminal scenarios passing through \(n\). Thus decisions at the same history coincide, while decisions following distinct histories may differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage extensive form assigns one decision to each scenario-tree history node and links each node only to its parent, thereby enforcing nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Extensive Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scenario-tree representation and content kind fit the multistage extensive-form container, but no citation supports the objective weighting, parent-local formulation, or nonanticipativity interpretation. A specific scenario-tree extensive-form source is required.

children.title: Scenario Path-Bundle Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Representations grouping complete paths or related collections of scenarios.

children.title: Scenario-Path Forms
children.top_down_role: Representations organized around complete trajectories through a scenario tree.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite set of root-to-leaf paths through a \(T\)-stage scenario tree.
Two paths have the same available information at stage \(t\) exactly when their histories through stage \(t\) coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The path-indexed model is nonanticipative exactly when all copies associated with a common history are equal.

notation.meaning: Decision copy at stage \(t\) on scenario path \(s\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports path-indexed scenario-tree formulations; a stochastic programming source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full path-copy representation with explicit nonanticipativity equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scenario-path form introduces a complete decision sequence \((x_1^s,\ldots,x_T^s)\) for every \(s\in S\) and writes scenario-local objectives and constraints separately. Its nonanticipativity system is
\[
x_t^s=x_t^{s'}\quad\text{whenever}\quad h_t(s)=h_t(s'),\qquad s,s'\in S,\quad t=1,\ldots,T.
\]
Consequently, an objective such as \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s F_s(x_1^s,\ldots,x_T^s)\), together with pathwise feasibility and these equalities, represents history-adapted decisions despite using path-specific copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-path form copies the entire decision sequence for each path and restores implementability by equating copies whenever the observed histories coincide.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Path Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The path-copy representation fits the Scenario-Path Forms leaf and is internally coherent, but no inspectable source supports the history-equivalence nonanticipativity system or its claimed representational equivalence.

children.title: Scenario-Bundle Forms
children.top_down_role: Representations organized around related collections of scenarios.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) is a partition of a finite scenario-path set \(S\).
Within every bundle, decisions sharing the same stagewise history must remain equal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bundle form preserves all within-bundle nonanticipativity and exposes any required cross-bundle history equalities as explicit coupling constraints.

notation.meaning: Partition of paths into nonempty bundles.
Stage-\(t\) decision copy for path \(s\) in bundle \(B\).

review_flags: The supplied sources do not establish scenario-bundle formulations or their coupling conventions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path partition retaining common-history equalities inside each bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(B\in\mathcal B\), a scenario-bundle form groups the pathwise variables and constraints for all \(s\in B\). It imposes
\[
x_t^{B,s}=x_t^{B,s'}\quad\text{if}\quad s,s'\in B\ \text{and}\ h_t(s)=h_t(s').
\]
If \(s\in B\) and \(s'\in B'\) with \(B\ne B'\) share history through stage \(t\), global nonanticipativity additionally requires \(x_t^{B,s}=x_t^{B',s'}\). These cross-bundle equalities form the coupling interface between otherwise separable bundle subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-bundle form groups path models, enforces common-history agreement inside each group, and leaves shared histories across groups as explicit coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Bundle Forms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and statement fit the Scenario-Bundle Forms leaf, but bundle formulations and the division between within-bundle and cross-bundle nonanticipativity are convention-dependent and have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Path-to-Bundle Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing how complete trajectories are collected into computational groups.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B\) partitions a finite scenario set \(S\), with \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each bundle has positive probability \(P_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Probability-weighted path objectives aggregate exactly into bundle objectives; feasibility is preserved when all original path constraints and nonanticipativity relations are retained.

notation.meaning: Conditional probability of scenario \(s\) within bundle \(B\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports exact path-to-bundle aggregation in stochastic programs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact regrouping by bundle, without scenario reduction or constraint deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every bundle \(B\in\mathcal B\), define \(P_B=\sum_{s\in B}p_s\) and \(p_{s\mid B}=p_s/P_B\). Then path contributions aggregate according to
\[
\sum_{s\in S}p_sF_s=\sum_{B\in\mathcal B}P_B\sum_{s\in B}p_{s\mid B}F_s.
\]
This regrouping is an exact representation, not an approximation. The bundled feasible set equals the path-form feasible set precisely when every pathwise constraint is retained and every common-history equality, including those crossing bundle boundaries, is either retained explicitly or represented by a shared variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path objectives can be regrouped exactly using bundle probabilities and conditional scenario probabilities, provided no path constraint or cross-bundle nonanticipativity relation is lost.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-to-Bundle Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The probability identity is algebraically standard and the representation kind fits the aggregation leaf, but the stronger feasible-set equivalence claim has no supporting stochastic-programming citation with a specific locator.

children.title: History Node-Path Indexing Pair
children.top_down_role: Node-based and path-based organizations of multistage information.

children.title: History-Node Indexing
children.top_down_role: Indexing organized by information histories represented as scenario-tree nodes.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T=(N,E)\) is a finite rooted scenario tree with stage map \(\tau\).
Each node represents one equivalence class of scenario paths having the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One decision per history node is equivalent to path copies satisfying all nonanticipativity equalities.

notation.meaning: Set of paths passing through node \(n\).
Unique node on path \(s\) at stage \(t\).

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the equivalence of history-node and path-copy indexing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision indexing by equivalence classes of indistinguishable path histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each node \(n\in N\), let \(S(n)\) contain exactly the root-to-leaf paths passing through \(n\), and assign one decision \(z_n\) to that history. The associated path decision is
\[
x_t^s=z_{n_t(s)},\qquad s\in S,
\]
where \(n_t(s)\) is the unique stage-\(t\) node on path \(s\). Hence paths with the same observed history use the same variable. Conversely, any path-indexed family satisfying nonanticipativity defines a unique \(z_n\) by selecting the common value on \(S(n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: History-node indexing assigns one decision to every distinct observed history; path decisions are obtained by selecting the node lying on each path at each stage.
knowledge_statements.title: History-Node Indexing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits History-Node Indexing and clearly relates node variables to path copies. However, the asserted two-way equivalence with the full path-indexed nonanticipativity system is unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Path Indexing
children.top_down_role: Indexing organized by complete scenario trajectories.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is the finite set of root-to-leaf paths of a \(T\)-stage scenario tree.
A path-indexed model contains one decision copy for each path and stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Path indexing separates scenario-local computations, while explicit equality constraints are necessary and sufficient to recover history-adapted decisions.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports scenario-tree path indexing and nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-local indexing with nonanticipativity represented as coupling equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Path indexing replaces each history-node decision by copies \(x_t^s\) for \(s\in S\) and \(t=1,\ldots,T\). Scenario-local objectives and constraints may then be written using only the variables of one path. The admissible path-indexed policies are exactly those satisfying
\[
x_t^s=x_t^{s'}\quad\text{for all }s,s'\in S\text{ such that }h_t(s)=h_t(s').
\]
Without these equalities, the formulation permits decisions to depend on future distinctions and therefore generally admits anticipative solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path indexing creates stagewise decision copies for every scenario path; equality constraints between copies with identical histories enforce nonanticipativity.
knowledge_statements.title: Path Indexing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits Path Indexing, and the variables and history equality are explicit. No source or inspectable locator supports the necessity-and-sufficiency claim or the anticipativity conclusion.

children.title: Node-to-Path Incidence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between shared history nodes and the paths containing them.

assumptions_latex: \(N\) is the node set and \(S\) the root-to-leaf path set of a finite scenario tree.
Every path contains exactly one node at each represented stage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incidence matrix maps node-indexed decisions and probabilities to their path-indexed counterparts and identifies every common-history coupling class.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports node-to-path incidence for scenario trees.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary incidence connecting history nodes to terminal scenario paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the node-to-path incidence matrix by
\[
A_{ns}=\begin{cases}1,&\text{if path }s\text{ passes through node }n,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\]
For path probabilities \(p_s\), the probability mass of node \(n\) is \(\pi_n=\sum_{s\in S}A_{ns}p_s\). If \(n\) is a stage-\(t\) node, the node decision \(z_n\) induces \(x_t^s=z_n\) for every \(s\) with \(A_{ns}=1\). Thus each row support identifies one nonanticipativity class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary incidence matrix records which history nodes lie on each scenario path, yielding node probabilities and the path-copy classes that must share decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-to-Path Incidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence construction fits the leaf, but no citation supports it. In addition, the conclusion says the matrix maps node-indexed decisions to path-indexed decisions, while the statement only defines incidence, node-probability aggregation, and row-support classes; the precise decision-map convention must be sourced before its mathematical version can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Scenario-Tree Block Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Stage and subtree partitions supporting nested or scenario-parallel computation.

children.title: Stagewise Blocks
children.top_down_role: Computational blocks partitioned according to decision stages.

assumptions_latex: \(N_t=\{n\in N:\tau(n)=t\}\) partitions the nodes of a finite scenario tree by stage.
Each nonroot constraint couples a node only with its parent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extensive form decomposes into stagewise blocks whose only interstage couplings follow parent-child arcs.

notation.meaning: Set of scenario-tree nodes at stage \(t\).

review_flags: The supplied decomposition references do not directly establish this scenario-tree block construction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Horizontal partition of a scenario-tree extensive form by decision stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each stage \(t\), the stagewise block contains variables \(x_{N_t}=(x_n)_{n\in N_t}\), node-local objective terms \(\sum_{n\in N_t}\pi_n c_n(x_n)\), and constraints assigned to nodes in \(N_t\). Under parent-local dynamics, every constraint in block \(t>1\) has the form
\[
(x_{a(n)},x_n)\in K_n,
\]
with \(a(n)\in N_{t-1}\) and \(n\in N_t\). Hence the block interface consists precisely of parent decisions entering from the preceding stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagewise blocks group all nodes at the same stage; their only cross-block data are parent decisions passed along scenario-tree arcs.
knowledge_statements.title: Stagewise Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stagewise representation fits the leaf under the stated parent-local coupling assumption, but no scenario-tree decomposition source supports the exact block-interface characterization.

children.title: Subtree Blocks
children.top_down_role: Computational blocks partitioned according to descendant scenario-tree regions.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T=(N,E)\) is a finite rooted tree, and \(r\in N\) is a chosen subtree root.
All model constraints are node-local or parent-child constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A rooted subtree is a decomposition block whose external primal interface consists only of the parent decision of its root.

notation.meaning: Parent of subtree root \(r\), when \(r\) is not the global root.
Tree edge boundary of the subtree.

review_flags: The supplied sources do not directly support rooted scenario-subtree decomposition blocks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertical block formed by a node and all of its descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a node \(r\), define \(D(r)=\{n\in N:r\text{ lies on the root-to-}n\text{ path}\}\). The subtree block rooted at \(r\) contains all variables, objective terms, and node-assigned constraints indexed by \(D(r)\). If \(r\) is not the global root, then
\[
\delta(D(r))=\{(a(r),r)\}.
\]
Consequently, under parent-child coupling, the block communicates with the remainder of the extensive form only through the root constraint involving \(x_{a(r)}\) and \(x_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subtree block contains a node and every descendant. With parent-child constraints, only the arc from the root's parent crosses its boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subtree-block representation fits the leaf, but no citation is supplied. The equality for the edge boundary also depends on whether the boundary denotes entering, outgoing, or undirected crossing edges; that convention is not explicitly defined and should be resolved from a source.

children.title: Nested Block Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Interfaces created where stage partitions meet nested subtree partitions.

assumptions_latex: Every block is the descendant set \(D(r)\) of some node \(r\) in a rooted tree.
Model coupling occurs only across tree edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rooted-subtree blocks have laminar node boundaries and single-edge external interfaces, permitting hierarchically nested decomposition.

notation.meaning: Tree-edge boundary of a node set.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports laminar scenario-tree block boundaries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laminar boundaries induced by blocks that are complete rooted subtrees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any two nodes \(r,q\), their descendant blocks satisfy exactly one of
\[
D(r)\cap D(q)=\varnothing,\qquad D(r)\subseteq D(q),\qquad D(q)\subseteq D(r).
\]
Thus the family of rooted-subtree blocks is laminar. Moreover, for every nonroot \(r\), the edge boundary is \(\delta(D(r))=\{(a(r),r)\}\). Nested blocks therefore exchange information only across their respective root interfaces; arbitrary overlapping blocks would destroy this laminar boundary structure and can create multiple cross-block coupling edges.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete rooted subtrees are either disjoint or nested, and each nonroot subtree has one entering edge, producing a hierarchical block interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Nested Block Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind correctly fits a leaf about nested block boundaries, and the laminarity claim is standard for descendant sets. Nevertheless, no source is cited, and the singleton boundary formula relies on an unstated edge-boundary convention.

children.title: Scenario Bundling Structure
children.top_down_role: Partitions that retain selected common-history coupling within scenario groups.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite set of scenario paths and \(\mathcal B\) is a partition of \(S\) into nonempty bundles.
Histories are compared stage by stage using the information available before each decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition defines a valid bundling structure when it preserves within-bundle common-history coupling and exposes all remaining common-history relations across bundles.

notation.meaning: Paths in bundle \(B\) sharing history \(h\) at stage \(t\).

review_flags: The supplied source hints do not directly define scenario bundling with retained common-history coupling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of scenario paths with explicitly retained history-based coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scenario bundling structure is a partition \(\mathcal B\) of \(S\) together with the within-bundle history classes
\[
C_{B,t,h}=\{s\in B:h_t(s)=h\},\qquad B\in\mathcal B.
\]
All decision copies indexed by paths in a nonempty class \(C_{B,t,h}\) are represented by one shared variable or constrained to be equal. If the global history class \(\{s\in S:h_t(s)=h\}\) intersects multiple bundles, the corresponding bundle variables remain linked by explicit cross-bundle nonanticipativity constraints. The partition changes decomposition granularity, not the underlying information structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario bundling structure partitions paths while retaining equality of decisions sharing a history inside bundles and explicitly coupling shared histories that cross bundles.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario Bundling Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is an appropriate content kind for Scenario Bundling Structure, and the statement matches the stated role. However, the proposed definition includes substantive coupling requirements and a decomposition-granularity claim without any authoritative source or locator establishing this bundling convention.

children.title: Explicit Nonanticipativity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Agreement represented through explicit cross-scenario coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Nonanticipativity Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite scenario-tree representation using equality constraints between decisions sharing the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set and let \(x_t^s\in\mathbb{R}^{n_t}\) denote the stage-\(t\) decision copied for scenario \(s\). For each stage \(t\), define \(s\sim_t r\) when scenarios \(s,r\in S\) have identical information histories through stage \(t\). Explicit nonanticipativity is represented by the linear coupling system
\[
x_t^s=x_t^r\quad\text{for every }t\text{ and every }s,r\in S\text{ with }s\sim_t r.
\]
Equivalently, after stacking all scenario decisions into \(x\), there exists an incidence-type matrix \(N\) such that the coupling system is \(Nx=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario copies must agree whenever their observed histories coincide; these equalities can be stacked into one homogeneous linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and all scenario copies at a given stage have the same dimension.
\(\sim_t\) is the equivalence relation induced by information histories through stage \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is nonanticipative}\iff x_t^s=x_t^r\text{ whenever }s\sim_t r\iff Nx=0.\)

notation.meaning: Stage-t decision copy for scenario s.
Scenarios s and r share their information history through stage t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-scenario equality and kernel representations are mathematically coherent and fit the representation container, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Nonanticipative Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Information-consistent decisions organized as a structured subspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative Subspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear subspace of finite scenario decisions consistent with a scenario-tree filtration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\prod_{s\in S}\prod_{t=0}^{T}\mathbb{R}^{n_t}\) be the space of stacked scenario decisions, and let \(\sim_t\) identify scenarios having the same information history through stage \(t\). The nonanticipative subspace is
\[
\mathcal N:=\{x\in X:x_t^s=x_t^r\text{ for every }t\text{ whenever }s\sim_t r\}.
\]
Because each defining relation is homogeneous and linear, \(\mathcal N\) is a linear subspace of \(X\). If \(N\) is any matrix whose rows encode all required scenario-copy differences, then \(\mathcal N=\ker N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonanticipative subspace contains exactly the scenario decision vectors that are constant on every information-history class.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and the horizon \(\{0,\ldots,T\}\) are finite.
Scenario copies belonging to one stage have a common Euclidean dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal N=\{x:x_t^s=x_t^r\text{ whenever }s\sim_t r\}=\ker N\text{ is a linear subspace of }X.\)

notation.meaning: Product space of all scenario-stage decision copies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise and fits the subspace container, but it has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Nonanticipativity Aggregation-Projection Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Nonanticipativity represented through information projection and policy aggregation.

children.title: Conditional-Expectation Views
children.top_down_role: Information-consistent policy organization through conditional aggregation.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Expectation Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hilbert-space representation of adapted decisions by conditional expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry a filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\), and let \(z_t\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P;\mathbb R^{n_t})\). The conditional expectation
\[
x_t:=\mathbb E[z_t\mid\mathcal F_t]
\]
is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and is the unique element of \(L^2(\mathcal F_t;\mathbb R^{n_t})\) satisfying
\[
\mathbb E\langle z_t-x_t,y_t\rangle=0\quad\text{for every }y_t\in L^2(\mathcal F_t;\mathbb R^{n_t}).
\]
Thus stagewise conditional expectation gives the orthogonal projection of an arbitrary square-integrable policy onto the nonanticipative policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditioning each stage decision on currently available information is exactly its orthogonal projection onto the square-integrable adapted decisions.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{T}\) is a filtration contained in \(\mathcal F\).
Each \(z_t\) is square-integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[z_t\mid\mathcal F_t]=P_{L^2(\mathcal F_t)}z_t\) for every stage \(t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-expectation characterization is standard and matches the container, but the Hilbert-space projection claim requires an authoritative cited source.

children.title: Nonanticipative Projection Views
children.top_down_role: Policy organization through projection onto information-consistent decision spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative Projection Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Euclidean projection onto finite-scenario nonanticipativity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let scenario weights satisfy \(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), and equip the scenario decision space with \(\langle x,z\rangle_p:=\sum_{s,t}p_s\langle x_t^s,z_t^s\rangle\). For the nonanticipative subspace \(\mathcal N\), the projection \(P_{\mathcal N}z\) is uniquely characterized by
\[
P_{\mathcal N}z\in\mathcal N,
\qquad
\langle z-P_{\mathcal N}z,y\rangle_p=0\quad	ext{for every }y\in\mathcal N.
\]
On each stage-\(t\) history class \(C\), its components are
\[
(P_{\mathcal N}z)_t^s=\frac{\sum_{r\in C}p_r z_t^r}{\sum_{r\in C}p_r},\qquad s\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto nonanticipativity replaces every history class of scenario copies by its probability-weighted average.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and every scenario weight is strictly positive.
\(\mathcal N\) is defined by equality within each information-history class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathcal N}z\) is obtained by probability-weighted averaging on every stagewise history class.

notation.meaning: Positive probability weight of scenario s.
Weighted orthogonal projection onto the nonanticipative subspace.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted class-average formula is internally consistent and appropriately presented as a representation, but no supporting source is cited.

children.title: Aggregation–Projection Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between conditional aggregation and nonanticipative projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation–Projection Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between history-class aggregation and weighted nonanticipative projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each stagewise information class \(C\), define the aggregation operator by
\[
(Az)_{t,C}:=\frac{\sum_{s\in C}p_s z_t^s}{\sum_{s\in C}p_s},
\]
and define the replication operator \(R\) by \((Ru)_t^s:=u_{t,C}\) whenever \(s\in C\). Then \(RA\) is the weighted orthogonal projector onto the nonanticipative subspace \(\mathcal N\):
\[
P_{\mathcal N}=RA,
\qquad A R=I,
\qquad (RA)^2=RA.
\]
Consequently, aggregation computes one decision per information class, while replication returns the corresponding nonanticipative scenario vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted aggregation followed by replication is precisely projection onto nonanticipativity; aggregating an already replicated policy changes nothing.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and the information classes partition the scenarios at every stage.
Aggregation uses normalized probability weights within each class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathcal N}=RA\), \(AR=I\), and \((RA)^2=RA\).

notation.meaning: Replication from class decisions to scenario copies.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identities are mathematically consistent when the class-decision space is understood as the domain of R, but the correspondence has no cited evidence.

children.title: Block-Angular Scenario Structure
children.top_down_role: Scenario blocks connected through shared decisions or linking constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Angular Scenario Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic-equivalent form with independent scenario blocks joined by first-stage variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-scenario two-stage linear program has block-angular form when it can be written as
\[
\min_{x,(y_s)} c^\top x+\sum_{s\in S}p_s q_s^\top y_s
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
Ax=b,
\quad T_sx+W_sy_s=h_s\ \ (s\in S),
\quad x\ge0,
\quad y_s\ge0.
\]
After fixing the shared vector \(x\), the variables \(y_s\) and the corresponding constraints separate by scenario. In the deterministic-equivalent constraint matrix, the matrices \(W_s\) occupy distinct diagonal blocks, while the matrices \(T_s\) form the linking column associated with \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario recourse blocks lie on the matrix diagonal and interact only through the common first-stage decision and its linking columns.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s\ge0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
All displayed matrices and vectors have compatible finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ fixed}\Longrightarrow\text{the subproblems in }y_s\text{ are mutually separable across }s.\)

children.title: Two-Block Linear Coupling
children.top_down_role: The canonical two-block separable interface for ADMM.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Block Linear Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex two-block form used by ADMM and related primal-dual splittings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb R^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper closed convex functions. The canonical two-block linearly coupled problem is
\[
\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,\,z\in\mathbb R^m} f(x)+g(z)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+Bz=c,
\]
where \(A\) and \(B\) are linear maps into a common finite-dimensional constraint space. Its objective is separable between \(x\) and \(z\); all interaction between the blocks occurs through the single affine constraint, whose augmented Lagrangian is
\[
L_\rho(x,z,y)=f(x)+g(z)+\langle y,Ax+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax+Bz-c\rVert^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two separable convex blocks interact only through one affine equality, yielding the canonical augmented-Lagrangian interface for ADMM.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\), \(B\), and \(c\) have compatible finite dimensions, and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)+g(z)\text{ is block-separable and }Ax+Bz=c\text{ is the complete coupling interface}.\)

notation.meaning: Augmented Lagrangian with penalty parameter rho.

children.title: Consensus Coupling
children.top_down_role: Local copies connected through agreement relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-copy formulation with agreement mediated by a shared global variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given proper functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), the centralized consensus formulation is
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i-z=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).
\]
The feasible set is the consensus subspace \(\{(x_1,\ldots,x_m):x_1=\cdots=x_m\}\), and eliminating the local copies gives the equivalent problem \(\min_z\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(z)\). For fixed \(z\) and multipliers, the local augmented-Lagrangian terms separate over \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each component receives a local decision copy, and equality to one global variable enforces agreement while preserving separable local objectives.
assumptions_latex: All local variables belong to the same finite-dimensional space.
The extended-real objectives have a common decision domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=z\ \forall i\Longrightarrow x_1=\cdots=x_m=z\), and eliminating \((x_i)\) yields \(\min_z\sum_i f_i(z)\).

notation.meaning: Local decision copy held by component i.

children.title: Aggregate Sharing Coupling
children.top_down_role: Local contributions connected through a shared aggregate quantity.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Sharing Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable local objectives coupled through a function or constraint of their aggregate contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), let \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^q\) be linear, and let \(g:\mathbb R^q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). An aggregate-sharing problem has the form
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_ix_i\right).
\]
Introducing \(z_i=A_ix_i\) and an aggregate variable \(u\) gives the equivalent constrained representation
\[
\min_{(x_i),(z_i),u}\sum_i f_i(x_i)+g(u)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad z_i=A_ix_i,\qquad u=\sum_i z_i.
\]
Thus local blocks communicate only through the aggregate \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local blocks contribute to one aggregate quantity; all cross-block interaction occurs through the function or constraint applied to that aggregate.
assumptions_latex: All maps \(A_i\) have the same finite-dimensional codomain.
The displayed extended-real objectives are well-defined on their respective spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u=\sum_iA_ix_i\) isolates the sole cross-block coupling in the aggregate variable \(u\).

notation.meaning: Contribution of local block i to the shared aggregate.
Objective or extended-real constraint applied to the aggregate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The aggregate-variable reformulation is mathematically coherent and fits the representation container, but no source supports the named aggregate-sharing pattern or equivalence.

children.title: Overlapping Partial-Separability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Intermediate structures containing local overlap or more than one coupling layer.

children.title: Partially Separable Structure
children.top_down_role: Problem structure whose components retain limited cross-block dependence.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Separable Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective decomposition in which each term depends on only a selected subset of global coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). A function \(F:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is partially separable with element sets \(J_1,\ldots,J_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) if there exist functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^{|J_i|}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that
\[
F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(E_i x),
\]
where \(E_i\) selects the coordinates indexed by \(J_i\). The sets may overlap; hence two element functions are coupled precisely through coordinates in \(J_i\cap J_j\). Full coordinate separability is the special case in which the sets \(J_i\) are pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially separable objective is a sum of element functions, each depending on only a selected, possibly overlapping subset of coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The number of coordinates and element functions is finite.
Each \(E_i\) is the coordinate-selection map associated with \(J_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_i f_i(E_ix)\), with coupling between terms \(i,j\) confined to \(J_i\cap J_j\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate set used by element function i.
Selection map extracting coordinates in J_i.
Element function on the selected local coordinates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed decomposition is a suitable definition, but no source is supplied. The assertion that terms are coupled precisely through every intersecting coordinate is stronger than the representation alone guarantees because an element function may not depend effectively on all selected coordinates.

children.title: Overlapping Block Structure
children.top_down_role: Block organizations in which variables or constraints belong to multiple local components.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlapping Block Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block organization characterized by a non-disjoint family of coordinate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the coordinates of \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(J_1,\ldots,J_m\subseteq V\) satisfy \(\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}J_i=V\). These sets define an overlapping block structure when
\[
J_i\cap J_j\ne\varnothing
\]
for at least one pair \(i\ne j\). With local copies \(x_i=E_ix\), consistency on an overlap requires
\[
R_{ij}x_i=R_{ji}x_j,
\]
where both restriction maps select the coordinates in \(J_i\cap J_j\). The overlap graph has one vertex per block and an edge \(\{i,j\}\) exactly when \(J_i\cap J_j\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocks overlap when some coordinate belongs to multiple blocks; local copies must agree on every shared coordinate.
assumptions_latex: The block family is finite and covers all global coordinates.
Local block coordinates retain an identifiable correspondence with global coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_i\cap J_j\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow R_{ij}x_i=R_{ji}x_j\text{ is the required pairwise consistency relation}.\)

notation.meaning: Global coordinate set belonging to block i.
Map selecting block i from the global vector.
Restriction of block i to its overlap with block j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The overlapping-set definition, restriction equalities, and overlap graph are coherent and fit the definition container, but they lack cited evidence.

children.title: Overlap-Coupling Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Coordination interfaces induced by shared content across partially separable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Coupling Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear consistency interface joining duplicated variables on intersections of overlapping blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let blocks \(J_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) have local variables \(x_i\in\mathbb R^{|J_i|}\), and let \(G=(\{1,ldots,m\},E)\) contain an edge \(\{i,j\}\) whenever \(J_i\cap J_j\ne\varnothing\). For each edge, let \(R_{ij}\) and \(R_{ji}\) restrict the adjacent local vectors to their common coordinates. The overlap-coupling interface is
\[
R_{ij}x_i-R_{ji}x_j=0\qquad(\{i,j\}\in E).
\]
Stacking these equalities yields \(Cx=0\). If the overlap graph induced by the blocks containing each global coordinate is connected, these edge equalities imply one common value for every duplicated coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping local blocks are joined by linear equalities on shared coordinates; connected overlap constraints enforce a unique common value for each duplicate.
assumptions_latex: Every restriction map uses the same ordering for the coordinates shared by its incident blocks.
For each global coordinate, the subgraph of blocks containing that coordinate is connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Cx=0\Longrightarrow\text{all local copies of each global coordinate agree}.\)

notation.meaning: Graph connecting blocks with nonempty intersections.
Restriction from block i to its overlap with block j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connectivity condition supports the agreement conclusion, but no source is cited. The graph vertex set also contains the malformed text \(\{1,ldots,m\}\), which should be \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

children.title: Two-Stage Nonanticipativity Duals
children.top_down_role: Dual scenario coordination for two-stage formulations.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set \(S\) is finite, with probabilities \(p_s>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Each \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^{m_s}\) is nonempty and convex, and each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex.
A primal-dual saddle point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[v_P=\max_{\lambda:\,\sum_s\lambda_s=0}q(\lambda).\]

notation.meaning: Multiplier for the equality between scenario copy and consensus decision.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario convex two-stage formulation with duplicated first-stage decisions.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Duplicate the first-stage decision as \(x_s\) and impose \(x_s=z\) for every \(s\in S\). For the primal value \[v_P=\inf_{z,(x_s,y_s)}\left\{\sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s,y_s):(x_s,y_s)\in X_s,\ x_s=z\right\},\] define \[q(\lambda)=\sum_{s\in S}\inf_{(x_s,y_s)\in X_s}\left(p_s f_s(x_s,y_s)+\langle\lambda_s,x_s\rangle\right).\] Minimization over \(z\) makes the Lagrangian finite exactly when \(\sum_s\lambda_s=0\). Under the stated saddle-point assumption, \(v_P=\max\{q(\lambda):\sum_s\lambda_s=0\}\), and evaluation of \(q\) separates by scenario.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing equality between scenario copies and the shared first-stage decision yields independent scenario subproblems, coupled only by the requirement that their multipliers sum to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Stage Nonanticipativity Duals

children.title: Multistage Nonanticipativity Duals
children.top_down_role: Dual scenario coordination across nested information structures.

assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and its history partitions are finite.
The scenario objective \(F\) is proper, closed, and convex on a nonempty closed convex product set \(C\).
The problem \(\inf_{x\in C\cap\mathcal N}F(x)\) has a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\inf_{x\in C\cap\mathcal N}F(x)=\max_{w\in\mathcal N^\perp}\inf_{x\in C}\bigl(F(x)+\langle w,x\rangle_P\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Subspace of policies constant on every information-history class.
Probability-weighted orthogonal complement of the nonanticipative subspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multistage scenario tree represented in a probability-weighted product space.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_{t,s})\) collect scenario-stage decisions and let \(\mathcal N\) contain exactly those policies satisfying \(x_{t,s}=x_{t,s'}\) whenever scenarios \(s\) and \(s'\) share the information available at stage \(t\). With the probability-weighted inner product, the annihilating prices are \(\mathcal N^\perp=\{w:\langle w,z\rangle_P=0\text{ for all }z\in\mathcal N\}\). The nonanticipativity dual is \[\sup_{w\in\mathcal N^\perp}\inf_{x\in C}\bigl(F(x)+\langle w,x\rangle_P\bigr).\] Under the saddle-point assumption, this value equals \(\inf_{x\in C\cap\mathcal N}F(x)\); the inner minimization separates whenever \(C\) and \(F\) are scenario-separable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite scenario tree, multistage nonanticipativity is a linear subspace constraint; its dual prices lie in the weighted orthogonal complement and coordinate otherwise separate scenario problems.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Nonanticipativity Duals

children.title: Nonsmooth Dual Coordination Families
children.top_down_role: Subgradient, bundle, and stabilized coordination of scenario dual variables.

assumptions_latex: The multiplier-feasible set \(D\) is closed and convex.
The concave dual function \(q:D\to\mathbb R\) is finite at every generated multiplier.
Each scenario solve returns a supergradient \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_D(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\quad\text{or}\quad \lambda^{k+1}\in\arg\max_{\lambda\in D}\{m_k(\lambda)-\tfrac{1}{2t_k}\|\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\|^2\}.\]

notation.meaning: Bundle cutting-plane model of the dual objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic coordination templates for a concave, typically nonsmooth, nonanticipativity dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\lambda^0\in D\), solve the scenario subproblems at iteration \(k\) and assemble a supergradient \(g^k\) from their nonanticipativity residuals. Projected supergradient coordination uses \(\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_D(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\). Bundle coordination stores triples \((\lambda^i,q(\lambda^i),g^i)\), forms \[m_k(\lambda)=\min_{i\in I_k}\{q(\lambda^i)+\langle g^i,\lambda-\lambda^i\rangle\},\] and maximizes \(m_k(\lambda)-(2t_k)^{-1}\|\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\|^2\) over \(D\). Stop when a prescribed dual-model gap and coordination residual are below their tolerances; output the incumbent multiplier and dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scenario residuals provide dual supergradients. Coordination may use projected supergradient ascent or a stabilized bundle model with an explicit dual-model gap stopping test.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Dual Coordination Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected-supergradient and proximal bundle templates are plausible and the algorithm kind fits, but no source is supplied for the bundle model, parameter rules, serious/null-step logic, or claimed dual-model-gap stopping test. Those choices materially determine the algorithmic statement.

children.title: Nonanticipative Policy Recovery Calculus
children.top_down_role: Recovery of information-consistent policies from scenario-dual solutions.

children.title: Primal Candidate Recovery
children.top_down_role: Construction of primal candidates from scenario-dual solution information.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\).
Scenario solutions \((x_s,y_s)\in X_s\) are available.
For every admissible common decision \(z\), each recourse completion set \(Y_s(z)=\{y:(z,y)\in X_s\}\) can be optimized or declared empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(z,(\widehat y_s)_s)\text{ is primal feasible whenever }z\in Z\text{ and }Y_s(z)\ne\varnothing\text{ for all }s.\]

notation.meaning: Admissible set for the shared first-stage decision.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-stage recovery by consensus projection followed by scenario recourse completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form the weighted consensus \(\bar x=\sum_{s\in S}p_s x_s\), choose \[z\in\arg\min_{u\in Z}\|u-\bar x\|_M^2,\] where \(M\) is positive definite, and for each scenario solve \[\widehat y_s\in\arg\min_{y\in Y_s(z)} f_s(z,y).\] If any \(Y_s(z)\) is empty, report recovery failure rather than a primal candidate. Otherwise output \((z,(\widehat y_s)_{s\in S})\). Because the same \(z\) is used in every scenario, the output satisfies first-stage nonanticipativity; membership of each \((z,\widehat y_s)\) in \(X_s\) establishes scenario feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average the scenario decisions, project the average onto admissible shared decisions, and reoptimize each scenario’s recourse. The result is feasible when every recourse-completion problem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Candidate Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits primal candidate recovery, and feasibility follows if every displayed recourse minimizer exists. No source supports the particular averaging, metric projection, or recourse-completion rule, while the assumptions do not explicitly ensure attainment of the displayed argmin problems.

children.title: Nonanticipative Policy Restoration
children.top_down_role: Restoration of information consistency across scenario-indexed decisions.

assumptions_latex: A finite scenario tree with probabilities \(p_s>0\) is given.
For each stage \(t\), scenarios are partitioned by their observed history.
The supplied scenario policy \(x=(x_{t,s})\) is square-integrable in the probability-weighted norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(P_{\mathcal N}x)_{t,s}=\frac{\sum_{r\in H_t(s)}p_r x_{t,r}}{\sum_{r\in H_t(s)}p_r}.\]

notation.meaning: History class containing scenario \(s\) at stage \(t\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal restoration under the probability-weighted Euclidean product norm.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Optimality Conditions and the Projection Theorem p. 210

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each stage \(t\) and scenario \(s\), let \(H_t(s)\) be the scenarios having the same observed history as \(s\). The probability-weighted orthogonal projection of a scenario policy \(x\) onto the nonanticipative subspace is given componentwise by \[(P_{\mathcal N}x)_{t,s}=\frac{\sum_{r\in H_t(s)}p_r x_{t,r}}{\sum_{r\in H_t(s)}p_r}.\] Thus all scenarios in one history class receive the same restored decision. This policy uniquely minimizes \(\sum_s p_s\sum_t\|z_{t,s}-x_{t,s}\|^2\) over \(z\in\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restore nonanticipativity by replacing each scenario-stage decision with the conditional probability-weighted average over scenarios sharing the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative Policy Restoration

children.title: Recovery Quality Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on feasibility or solution quality for recovered policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Quality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit feasibility and objective-quality limitations of aggregation without convexity or objective-scale regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasibility failure, consider two equally likely scenarios and the shared feasible set \(Z=\{0,1\}\). The individually feasible decisions \(x_1=0\) and \(x_2=1\) have aggregate \(\bar x=(x_1+x_2)/2=1/2\notin Z\). Thus averaging scenario-feasible decisions need not preserve feasibility when \(Z\) is nonconvex. For the absence of a disagreement-only objective bound, fix \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]\), let \(Z=[0,1]\), take \(x_1=0\), \(x_2=2\varepsilon\), and define \(\bar x=\varepsilon\) and \(d=\bigl(\tfrac12\sum_{s=1}^2|x_s-\bar x|^2\bigr)^{1/2}=\varepsilon\). For each \(L>0\), the objective \(f_L(z)=Lz\) satisfies \(f_L(\bar x)-\min_{z\in Z}f_L(z)=L\varepsilon\). Hence, for fixed disagreement \(d=\varepsilon\), the recovered objective gap is arbitrarily large as \(L\) varies; a bound depending only on disagreement requires additional objective-scale or stability assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging feasible binary decisions can yield an infeasible fractional decision. Even when the average is feasible, fixing the scenario disagreement does not bound its objective gap if the objective scale is unrestricted.
assumptions_latex: Both counterexamples use two scenarios with probabilities \(p_1=p_2=1/2\).
In the feasibility counterexample, the shared feasible set is \(Z=\{0,1\}\).
In the objective-quality counterexample, \(Z=[0,1]\), \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2]\), and \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_1=0,\ x_2=1\Longrightarrow \bar x=\tfrac12\notin\{0,1\},\qquad f_L(\varepsilon)-\min_{z\in[0,1]}f_L(z)=L\varepsilon.\]

notation.meaning: Equal-probability aggregate of the scenario decisions.
Objective with unrestricted positive scale parameter \(L\).

children.title: Scenario-Local Regularization
children.top_down_role: Scenario subproblem stabilization by a local proximal geometry.

assumptions_latex: Each scenario objective \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex on a nonempty closed convex set \(X_s\).
The local metric \(M_s\) is positive definite and \(\rho_s>0\).
A reference policy \(z_s^k\) and information price \(w_s^k\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho_s}{2}\|x-z_s^k\|_{M_s}^2\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex scenario subproblem regularized in a positive-definite local quadratic geometry.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), scenario \(s\) computes \[x_s^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in X_s}\left\{f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho_s}{2}\|x-z_s^k\|_{M_s}^2\right\},\qquad \|u\|_{M_s}^2=\langle u,M_su\rangle.\] The positive-definite quadratic term makes the minimized objective strongly convex whenever its remaining terms are convex, so the scenario decision is unique. All terms other than the supplied reference and price are scenario-local, and the subproblems can therefore be solved independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario minimizes its local objective plus its current information price and a positive-definite quadratic penalty measuring departure from the current consensus policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Local Regularization

children.title: Scenario-Policy Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Organization of scenario-local decisions into shared policy candidates.

assumptions_latex: The scenario set \(S\) is finite with probabilities \(p_s>0\).
At each stage, scenarios are grouped into finite information-history classes.
Scenario decisions have compatible dimensions within each history class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bar x_{t,H}=\frac{\sum_{s\in H}p_s x_{t,s}}{\sum_{s\in H}p_s}.\]

notation.meaning: Aggregated decision assigned to history class \(H\).

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Optimality Conditions and the Projection Theorem p. 210
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a stage \(t\) and information-history class \(H\), aggregate the scenario decisions by \[\bar x_{t,H}=\frac{\sum_{s\in H}p_s x_{t,s}}{\sum_{s\in H}p_s}.\] Assigning \(\bar x_{t,H}\) to every \(s\in H\) produces a policy constant on that history class. Performing this operation for every stage and history class yields a nonanticipative policy. The denominator is the probability of reaching \(H\), so the aggregate is the conditional expectation of the scenario decision given that history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within each information-history class, aggregate scenario decisions using normalized scenario probabilities. The resulting history-indexed decisions define a nonanticipative policy.

children.title: Nonanticipative Policy Projection
children.top_down_role: Projection of scenario decisions onto information-consistent policy spaces.

assumptions_latex: The scenario-policy space is finite-dimensional and carries the probability-weighted inner product.
The nonanticipative policy set \(\mathcal N\) is a closed linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{\mathcal N}x\in\mathcal N,\qquad x-P_{\mathcal N}x\in\mathcal N^\perp.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted orthogonal projection onto the linear nonanticipativity subspace.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Optimality Conditions and the Projection Theorem p. 210
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any scenario policy \(x\), the nonanticipative projection is the unique solution \[P_{\mathcal N}x=\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal N}\|z-x\|_P^2.\] It is characterized by \[P_{\mathcal N}x\in\mathcal N,\qquad \langle x-P_{\mathcal N}x,z\rangle_P=0\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal N.\] Consequently, \(x-P_{\mathcal N}x\in\mathcal N^\perp\), and the decomposition \(x=P_{\mathcal N}x+(I-P_{\mathcal N})x\) is orthogonal. On a finite scenario tree, the projector is computed by probability-weighted averaging within each information-history class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario policy decomposes uniquely into a nonanticipative projection and an orthogonal disagreement component. History-wise probability-weighted averaging computes the projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative Policy Projection

children.title: Aggregation Weighting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Weighting structures that shape policy aggregation across scenarios.

assumptions_latex: For every information class \(H\), weights satisfy \(a_{s,H}>0\) for \(s\in H\).
Scenario decisions have compatible dimensions within each class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_H(x)=\frac{\sum_{s\in H}a_{s,H}x_s}{\sum_{s\in H}a_{s,H}},\] with orthogonal projection obtained when the weights match the chosen inner product.

notation.meaning: Positive aggregation weight for scenario \(s\) in class \(H\).
Weighted aggregation operator on history class \(H\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive normalized weighting within each finite information-history class.

source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A valid classwise aggregation regime assigns weights \(a_{s,H}>0\) and uses \[A_H(x)=\frac{\sum_{s\in H}a_{s,H}x_s}{\sum_{s\in H}a_{s,H}}.\] Probability weighting takes \(a_{s,H}=p_s\) and represents conditional expectation. Uniform weighting takes \(a_{s,H}=1\). Metric weighting uses the coefficients defining a diagonal product-space inner product. The aggregation equals the orthogonal projection associated with that inner product exactly when its normalized weights agree with the inner-product weights on every class; arbitrary weights still produce classwise consensus but generally a different projection geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregation weights must be positive and normalized within each history class. Probability, uniform, and metric weights produce different averages, and only geometry-matched weights give the corresponding orthogonal projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Weighting Regimes

children.title: Information-Price Coordination
children.top_down_role: Dual coordination associated with scenario disagreement.

assumptions_latex: The nonanticipativity set \(\mathcal N\) is a closed linear subspace of a finite-dimensional weighted product space.
A penalty parameter \(\rho>0\) is fixed.
Scenario-local minimizers \(x^{k+1}\) and their projection \(z^{k+1}=P_{\mathcal N}x^{k+1}\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\in\mathcal N^\perp\quad\text{when }w^0\in\mathcal N^\perp.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Price update driven by the orthogonal scenario-disagreement residual.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After scenario-local decisions \(x^{k+1}\) are computed, set \(z^{k+1}=P_{\mathcal N}x^{k+1}\) and update the information prices by \[w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho\bigl(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\bigr).\] Because \(x^{k+1}-P_{\mathcal N}x^{k+1}\in\mathcal N^\perp\), initialization with \(w^0\in\mathcal N^\perp\) implies \(w^k\in\mathcal N^\perp\) for every \(k\). The price increment is therefore precisely the weighted-orthogonal scenario-disagreement component and vanishes exactly when the current scenario policy is nonanticipative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information prices accumulate scenario disagreement. Since projection residuals are orthogonal to all nonanticipative policies, correctly initialized prices remain in the nonanticipativity dual space.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Price Coordination

children.title: Progressive Hedging Problem Regimes

children.title: Convex Continuous Programs
children.top_down_role: The classical convergence setting for progressive hedging.

assumptions_latex: The scenario product space is finite-dimensional, and each scenario objective plus constraint indicator is proper, closed, and convex.
The nonanticipative feasible set is a nonempty closed linear subspace intersection, and an optimal solution exists.
Scenario subproblems are solved exactly with a fixed penalty \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|x^k-P_{\mathcal N}x^k\|_P\to0,\qquad F(P_{\mathcal N}x^k)\to v^*\] whenever the projected iterates are in the effective domain of \(F\).

notation.meaning: Closed proper convex scenario-separable objective, including constraint indicators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-dimensional convex continuous regime with exact scenario solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Apply progressive hedging to \(\min\{F(x):x\in\mathcal N\}\), using exact scenario-local proximal minimizations, probability-weighted projection onto \(\mathcal N\), and the associated information-price update. Under the stated assumptions, the primal disagreement satisfies \(\|x^k-P_{\mathcal N}x^k\|_P\to0\), every cluster point of the projected primal sequence is optimal, and the multiplier sequence converges to a dual solution when such a solution is uniquely selected by the iteration. If \(F\) is finite and continuous on the relevant projected iterates, then \(F(P_{\mathcal N}x^k)\to v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite-dimensional closed convex continuous models with exact subproblem solves and an attained solution, progressive hedging drives scenario disagreement to zero and its primal cluster points are optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Continuous Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the classical convex regime, but the stated assumptions do not explicitly ensure a primal-dual saddle point, and the multiplier-convergence qualification is not mathematically precise. Objective convergence of projected iterates also requires stronger domain and continuity control. An authoritative progressive-hedging convergence theorem is required before selecting the exact hypotheses and conclusions.

children.title: Multistage Scenario Trees
children.top_down_role: Progressive hedging across nested histories and repeated tree nodes.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T\) is a finite rooted scenario tree with leaf set \(S\) and probabilities \(p_s>0\).
Each leaf \(s\) carries a pathwise decision vector \(x_s=(x_{s,t})_{t=1}^T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal N\iff x_{s,t}=z_{n_t(s)}\) for some node decisions \(z_n\).

notation.meaning: Tree node reached by scenario s at stage t
Probability-weighted projection onto the nonanticipative subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-tree representation underlying multistage progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every stage \(t\), scenarios sharing the same history occupy the same node. The nonanticipativity subspace is \[\mathcal N=\{x:x_{s,t}=x_{s',t}\text{ whenever }n_t(s)=n_t(s')\}.\] Equivalently, \(x\in\mathcal N\) exactly when node variables \(z_n\) exist with \(x_{s,t}=z_{n_t(s)}\). The probability-weighted consensus is \[P_{\mathcal N}(x)_{s,t}=\frac{\sum_{r:n_t(r)=n_t(s)}p_r x_{r,t}}{\sum_{r:n_t(r)=n_t(s)}p_r}.\] Thus repeated tree nodes, rather than entire scenarios, determine the progressive-hedging consensus groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multistage scenario solution is nonanticipative exactly when decisions agree at every shared history; consensus averages are therefore computed separately at each tree node.
knowledge_statements.title: Multistage Scenario Trees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the multistage-tree container and its notation is coherent, but no source is supplied for the nodewise nonanticipativity representation or the probability-weighted projection formula. An authoritative progressive-hedging or multistage stochastic-programming locator is required.

children.title: Risk-Structured Programs
children.top_down_role: Progressive-hedging constructions for objectives with cross-scenario risk coupling.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, \(p_s>0\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Scenario loss is \(L_s(x_s)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(L)=\min_{\eta,\xi}\{\eta+(1-\alpha)^{-1}\sum_s p_s\xi_s:\xi_s\ge L_s(x_s)-\eta,\ \xi_s\ge0\}\).

notation.meaning: Nonanticipative subspace, including replicated risk variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: CVaR epigraph lifting as a scenario-separable progressive-hedging interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cross-scenario risk term has the lifted representation \[\operatorname{CVaR}_\alpha(L(x))=\min_{\eta,\,\xi_s\ge0}\left\{\eta+\frac{1}{1-\alpha}\sum_{s\in S}p_s\xi_s:\xi_s\ge L_s(x_s)-\eta\right\}.\] Scenario splitting replaces \(\eta\) by copies \(\eta_s\) and imposes \(\eta_s=\eta_r\) for all \(s,r\), together with the original nonanticipativity constraints on \(x_s\). The lifted objective and excess-loss constraints are scenario-separable; the replicated threshold supplies the additional consensus coordinate required by progressive hedging.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CVaR becomes scenario-separable after introducing scenario excess losses and replicated threshold variables, whose equality is enforced through the progressive-hedging consensus constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Risk-Structured Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The CVaR lifting is relevant to cross-scenario risk coupling and representation is the appropriate content kind, but there is no citation for either the epigraph formula or its replicated-threshold progressive-hedging construction.

children.title: Integer Programs
children.top_down_role: Progressive-hedging use for models containing discrete decision variables.

assumptions_latex: Each scenario feasible set \(X_s\) is nonempty and satisfies \(X_s\subseteq\mathbb Z^{I_s}\times\mathbb R^{n_s-|I_s|}\).
Scenario copies are coupled by a nonanticipativity subspace \(\mathcal N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_s\) is nonconvex whenever \(I_s\ne\varnothing\), so convex progressive-hedging convergence hypotheses do not apply directly.

notation.meaning: Indices constrained to take integer values in scenario s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-split integer-program regime, not a convergence assertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scenario-split integer program is an optimization problem of the form \[\min_{x}\ \sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_s\in X_s\subseteq\mathbb Z^{I_s}\times\mathbb R^{n_s-|I_s|},\qquad x\in\mathcal N,\] where at least one \(I_s\) is nonempty. Progressive hedging preserves the integrality restrictions inside each scenario subproblem, while its consensus projection acts on the scenario copies. Consequently, projected averages need not belong to the integer scenario sets and are coordination points rather than automatically feasible integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the integer regime, scenario subproblems retain integrality, but consensus averages may be fractional and are not automatically feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The regime definition fits the leaf, but the conclusion that every nonempty integer index set makes X_s nonconvex is false without further assumptions; an integer-restricted set can be empty, a singleton, or otherwise convex as a subset of Euclidean space. No source is supplied to establish the intended progressive-hedging boundary.

children.title: Nonconvex Continuous Programs
children.top_down_role: Progressive-hedging use for continuous models with nonconvex structure.

assumptions_latex: Every scenario variable lies in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
At least one scenario objective or feasible set is nonconvex, while all decision variables remain continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scenario-split model is continuous but nonconvex, and a progressive-hedging fixed point need not be globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Continuous feasible set for scenario s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous nonconvex scenario subproblems under progressive-hedging coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonconvex continuous scenario program has the form \[\min_x\ \sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_s\in X_s\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_s},\qquad x\in\mathcal N,\] with no discrete variables and with at least one \(f_s\) nonconvex on \(X_s\) or at least one \(X_s\) nonconvex. Scenario splitting still yields independent augmented subproblems, but those subproblems may have multiple local minimizers; therefore their solution rule must specify whether local or global minimization is intended.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime has only continuous variables but includes a nonconvex scenario objective or feasible set, so subproblem solutions and progressive-hedging limits may be local.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Continuous Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition of the continuous nonconvex regime fits the container. However, the claims about progressive-hedging fixed points and potentially local limits require a precise algorithm, subproblem selection rule, and supporting source; none is cited.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Nonconvex Programs
children.top_down_role: Regimes combining discrete decisions with nonconvex continuous structure.

assumptions_latex: At least one scenario has a nonempty integer index set and a nonconvex objective or constraint.
Scenario copies satisfy nonanticipativity constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model combines discrete nonconvexity with additional nonlinear nonconvexity, so convex progressive-hedging guarantees are unavailable without stronger structure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scenario-split models containing both integer restrictions and nonlinear nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer nonconvex scenario program has the form \[\min_x\ \sum_{s\in S}p_s f_s(x_s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_s\in X_s\subseteq\mathbb Z^{I_s}\times\mathbb R^{n_s-|I_s|},\qquad x\in\mathcal N,\] where some \(I_s\ne\varnothing\) and, beyond integrality, some \(f_s\) or continuous relaxation of \(X_s\) is nonconvex. A progressive-hedging subproblem must retain both the integer restrictions and nonlinear constraints. Its consensus point may violate integrality, nonconvex feasibility, or both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-integer nonconvex scenario programs combine discrete restrictions with nonlinear nonconvexity; their consensus averages can violate both integrality and nonlinear feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Nonconvex Programs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record appropriately distinguishes mixed-integer nonconvex programs from the two sibling regimes, but no source supports the progressive-hedging feasibility and guarantee-boundary claims. The conclusion also needs a cited statement of the convex guarantees being excluded.

children.title: Heuristic Guarantee Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Qualification limits separating heuristic performance from classical guarantees.

assumptions_latex: Progressive hedging is applied to scenario sets or objectives outside the closed proper convex regime.
Scenario subproblems may be solved locally or approximately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal-residual reduction alone certifies neither global optimality nor finite termination in the discrete-nonconvex regime.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of standard progressive-hedging guarantees beyond convex continuous models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When convexity is removed, the augmented scenario objectives can possess distinct local minimizers and the scenario update becomes set-valued unless a selection rule is fixed. When integrality is imposed, the consensus projection can be fractional. Hence \(r^k\to0\) only expresses asymptotic agreement of scenario copies; it does not by itself establish global optimality, an objective gap, or finite termination. Any such guarantee requires additional assumptions, such as globally solved subproblems, an exact penalty property, a valid lower-bounding mechanism, or a problem-specific finite-state argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside convex continuous models, declining nonanticipativity residuals do not by themselves certify global optimality, an objective bound, or finite termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Guarantee Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure_boundary is the correct content kind, and residual agreement alone does not encode an objective certificate. Nevertheless, the asserted boundary across nonconvex, integer, local, and approximate regimes needs an exact theorem, counterexample, or authoritative discussion; no source is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive hedging with joint subproblems for scenario bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a consensus vector \(z^0\in\mathcal N\) and bundle multipliers. For each \(B\in\mathcal B\), jointly solve \[x_B^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_B\in X_B}\left\{\sum_{s\in B}p_s f_s(x_s)+\langle w_B^k,x_B\rangle+\tfrac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_B-z_B^k\rVert^2\right\},\] where \(X_B\) retains the selected within-bundle constraints. Assemble the bundle solutions, project them onto global nonanticipativity to obtain \(z^{k+1}\), and update bundle multipliers by \(w_B^{k+1}=w_B^k+\rho(x_B^{k+1}-z_B^{k+1})\). Stop using prescribed residual tests.

children.title: Participation Coverage Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Participation Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient deterministic or random coverage conditions for partial scenario updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the finite scenario set be \(S=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a filtration, and let \(I_k\subseteq S\) be \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable. Participation has adequate coverage if either (i) there exists \(B<\infty\) such that \(\bigcup_{j=k}^{k+B-1}I_j=S\) for every \(k\), or (ii) for every \(s\in S\) there exists \(p_s>0\) such that \(\mathbb P(s\in I_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_s\) almost surely for every \(k\). In regime (i), every scenario participates infinitely often; in regime (ii), every scenario participates infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adequate coverage follows either from activation of every scenario in each uniformly bounded window or from a uniformly positive conditional activation probability for every scenario. The former gives deterministic infinite participation, and the latter gives almost-sure infinite participation.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite.
\((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0}\) is a filtration and \(I_k\) is \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall s\in S,\ s\in I_k\text{ infinitely often}\) deterministically in regime (i) and almost surely in regime (ii).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Subproblem Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progressive hedging with explicitly controlled errors in scenario proximal solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given scenario weights \(p_s>0\), penalty \(\rho>0\), initial consensus \(z^0\), and multipliers satisfying \(\sum_s p_s w_s^0=0\), iteration \(k\) computes each scenario point \(x_s^{k+1}\) within error \(\varepsilon_{s,k}\) of an exact minimizer of \(f_s(x)+\langle w_s^k,x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-z^k\rVert^2\).
