children.title: Aggregate Resource Sharing
children.top_down_role: Local contributions coupled through a shared aggregate objective or resource.

assumptions_latex: \(f_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, convex.
Each \(A_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to\mathbb{R}^p\) is linear.
The composite problem has a minimizer and a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate coupling \(g(\sum_iA_ix_i)\) is equivalently isolated by local contributions and one summation constraint.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex sharing through a sum of mapped local resource contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The aggregate sharing problem \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_N}\ \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N A_ix_i\right)\] is equivalently represented as \[\min_{(x_i),(r_i),s}\ \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+g(s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad r_i=A_ix_i,\quad s=\sum_{i=1}^N r_i.\] The local maps determine individual resource contributions, while the single variable \(s\) isolates the shared aggregate objective. Eliminating \(r_i\) and \(s\) recovers the original formulation exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local decisions produce resource contributions whose sum enters one shared convex objective; auxiliary variables isolate that aggregate coupling.
knowledge_statements.title: Aggregate Resource Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The auxiliary-variable aggregate representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but it has no source reference with an inspectable locator. An authoritative source for the sharing formulation is required.

children.title: Shared-Resource Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Sharing structures induced by common capacities, budgets, or network resources.

children.title: Capacity Sharing
children.top_down_role: Sharing formulations organized around common capacity limits.

assumptions_latex: Each allocation \(r_i\) lies in \(\mathbb{R}_+^p\).
The capacity vector \(c\) lies in \(\mathbb{R}_+^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Capacity feasibility is exactly the componentwise predicate \(\sum_{i=1}^N r_i\leq c\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative capacity consumption assigned to participant i
Available capacities for the p resources

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Divisible nonnegative resources with componentwise upper capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A collection of local resource allocations \((r_i)_{i=1}^N\) is capacity-feasible for capacity vector \(c\) precisely when \[r_i\in\mathbb{R}_+^p\quad(i=1,\ldots,N),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N r_i\leq c,\] where the inequality is componentwise. Equivalently, the aggregate \(s=\sum_i r_i\) belongs to the capacity set \(C=\{s\in\mathbb{R}_+^p:s\leq c\}\). In an objective formulation, the hard capacity restriction is represented by adding the indicator \(\delta_C(s)\) to the aggregate objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative local allocations share capacity when their componentwise sum does not exceed the available resource vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Capacity Sharing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise capacity predicate is precise, and condition is the correct content kind for this leaf. The record nevertheless lacks a cited source and exact locator.

children.title: Budget Sharing
children.top_down_role: Sharing formulations organized around common expenditure or resource budgets.

assumptions_latex: Each local decision belongs to a nonempty set \(X_i\).
Each cost function \(b_i:X_i\to\mathbb{R}_+\) is specified and the total budget satisfies \(B\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Budget feasibility is exactly \(x_i\in X_i\) for every \(i\) and \(\sum_i b_i(x_i)\leq B\).

notation.meaning: Budget consumed by local decision i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar additive budget shared by heterogeneous local decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A tuple of local decisions \((x_i)_{i=1}^N\) is budget-feasible precisely when \[x_i\in X_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,N),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N b_i(x_i)\leq B.\] Introducing expenditures \(r_i=b_i(x_i)\) and the aggregate \(s=\sum_i r_i\) yields the equivalent shared-resource condition \(s\in[0,B]\). If the functions \(b_i\) and sets \(X_i\) are convex, then the budget-feasible set is convex, so the coupling can be handled through an aggregate indicator or a nonnegative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local decisions share a budget when their nonnegative expenditures sum to no more than the available scalar amount.
knowledge_statements.title: Budget Sharing

children.title: Coupled Resource Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Resource Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary description for shared-resource feasible sets in finite-dimensional sharing models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent choose \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), let \(A_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a closed convex resource set. The coupled resource boundary is \[\mathcal B=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in\prod_{i=1}^N X_i:\ \sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i\in\operatorname{bd}C\right\}.\] For a componentwise capacity set \(C=\{z:z\le b\}\), membership means that the shared constraint is feasible and at least one component satisfies \(\left(\sum_iA_ix_i\right)_j=b_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupled boundary consists of feasible agent decisions whose aggregate resource use lies on the boundary of the shared capacity set.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) are nonempty closed convex sets.
Each \(A_i\) is linear.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\in\mathbb N\). For proper closed convex functions \(f_i:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), \(i=1,\ldots,N\), the convex exchange problem is \[\underset{x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\mathbb R^m}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N x_i=0.\] Positive and negative components of \(x_i\) represent net acquisition and disposition under a fixed sign convention. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Fenchel duality between aggregate sharing and agreement on a common dual variable.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\in\mathbb N\), let each \(X_i\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, and let \(A_i:X_i\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear. For proper closed convex functions \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), consider \[\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^N f_i(x_i)+g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^N A_i x_i\right)\right\}.\] If \(0\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g-\sum_{i=1}^N A_i\operatorname{dom}f_i)\), its Fenchel dual is \[\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{-g^*(y)-\sum_{i=1}^N f_i^*(-A_i^*y)\right\}.\] Replacing the common variable \(y\) by local copies \(y_1,\ldots,y_N\) requires the consensus constraints \(y_1=\cdots=y_N\). Thus aggregate coupling in the primal becomes consensus coupling in the dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a finite-dimensional Fenchel qualification, dualization converts a primal aggregate-sharing term into separable dual terms evaluated at one common dual variable; local copies of that variable must agree.
knowledge_statements.title: Sharing–Consensus Duality

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\), \(P\succeq0\), and \(Q\succeq0\), and initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|x-x^k\|_P^2,\] \[z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+\frac12\|z-z^k\|_Q^2,\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\] Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ADMM stabilized by general iteration-dependent convex regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\), initialize \((x^0,z^0,u^0)\), and select nonnegative convex regularizers \(R_k(\cdot,x^k)\) and \(S_k(\cdot,z^k)\) vanishing at their second arguments. Iterate \[x^{k+1}\in\arg\min_x f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+R_k(x,x^k),\] \[z^{k+1}\in\arg\min_z g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+S_k(z,z^k),\quad u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\] Output an iterate meeting specified residual tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized ADMM stabilizes alternating local solves using nonnegative convex regularizers, including quadratic proximal or Bregman choices.
assumptions_latex: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
Each regularized subproblem has a minimizer.
The regularizers are chosen so the resulting splitting remains convergent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheme generates regularized ADMM iterates and returns one satisfying the prescribed stopping test.

children.title: Regularization Geometry Choices

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Geometry Choices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified geometric representation of quadratic and Bregman stabilization in local ADMM models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local ADMM regularizer centered at \(x^k\) may be represented as either \[R_k(x,x^k)=\frac12\|x-x^k\|_{P_k}^2,\qquad P_k\succeq0,\] or \[R_k(x,x^k)=D_{h_k}(x,x^k)=h_k(x)-h_k(x^k)-\langle\nabla h_k(x^k),x-x^k\rangle,\] where \(h_k\) is differentiable and convex on the relevant domain. The Euclidean choice is recovered with \(h_k(x)=\frac12\langle x,P_kx\rangle\). Strongly convex generators provide coercive local geometry; diagonal or block metrics preserve separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM regularization can use quadratic metrics or Bregman divergences; Euclidean, diagonal, and block choices trade curvature against separability.
assumptions_latex: The center \(x^k\) lies in the differentiability domain of \(h_k\).
The metric \(P_k\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Quadratic proximal geometry is a special case of Bregman geometry generated by \(h_k(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,P_kx\rangle\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM permitting controlled optimality residuals in both local solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\), initialize \((z^0,u^0)\), and choose tolerances \(\varepsilon_k^x,\varepsilon_k^z\ge0\). Select \(x^{k+1}\) and \(z^{k+1}\) satisfying \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x^{k+1})+\rho A^*(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^k-c+u^k)\right)\le\varepsilon_k^x,\] \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial g(z^{k+1})+\rho B^*(Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c+u^k)\right)\le\varepsilon_k^z,\] then set \(u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). A standard absolute-error regime requires \(\sum_k(\varepsilon_k^x+\varepsilon_k^z)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact ADMM accepts approximate block minimizers whose computable optimality residuals obey a convergence-compatible error schedule.
assumptions_latex: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
A saddle point exists.
The optimality-error sequence is summable.

children.title: Linearization–Inexactness Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined regimes where local approximation and solve error occur together.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization–Inexactness Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined majorization and local-solve error condition for approximate linearized ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the linearized first-block model use a self-adjoint metric \(P_k\) and produce an approximate minimizer with optimality residual \(e_k\). A standard compatible regime is \[P_k-\rho A^*A\succeq\delta I\quad\text{for some }\delta>0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e_k\|_{P_k^{-1}}<\infty.\] The first inequality ensures that the linearized model majorizes the omitted quadratic curvature; the second prevents accumulated local-solve error from overwhelming the splitting iteration. With fixed scalar geometry \(P_k=\tau I\), compatibility reduces to \(\tau>\rho\|A\|^2\) plus summable weighted errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearization and inexact solution are compatible when the surrogate uniformly majorizes omitted curvature and the weighted optimality errors are summable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_k\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
The coupling map \(A\) is bounded and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k-\rho A^*A\succeq\delta I\) and \(\sum_k\|e_k\|_{P_k^{-1}}<\infty\) jointly control model and solve errors.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) denote a positive-definite metric used by a variable-metric ADMM step. knowledge_statements.title: Bregman ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM with Bregman proximal regularization of each local subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\), differentiable convex kernels \(\phi_x,\phi_z\), and weights \(\eta_x,\eta_z\geq0\). With \(D_\phi(v,w)=\phi(v)-\phi(w)-\langle\nabla\phi(w),v-w\rangle\), initialize \((z^0,u^0)\) and iterate
\[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2+\eta_xD_{\phi_x}(x,x^k)\right\},\]
\[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2+\eta_zD_{\phi_z}(z,z^k)\right\},\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\]
Any selected minimizers define the Bregman-regularized ADMM sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bregman ADMM adds geometry-dependent Bregman proximal terms to the two alternating augmented-Lagrangian subproblems, followed by the usual scaled-dual update.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions on finite-dimensional spaces.
The displayed subproblems attain minimizers.
\(\phi_x\) and \(\phi_z\) are differentiable on domains containing all iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x^{k+1},z^{k+1},u^{k+1})\) is generated by the displayed Bregman-regularized ADMM update.

notation.meaning: Bregman divergence generated by the convex kernel phi

Moreover, the first update uses x^0 although initialization supplies only (z^0,u^0). A direct source and corrected initialization are required.

children.title: Relaxed ADMM
children.top_down_role: Under-relaxed and over-relaxed ADMM families.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-block scaled ADMM with under-relaxation or over-relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), choose \(\rho>0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,2)\). Given \((z^0,u^0)\), compute
\[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c+u^k\|^2\right\},\qquad \bar a^{k+1}=\alpha Ax^{k+1}+(1-\alpha)(c-Bz^k),\]
\[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\left\{g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|\bar a^{k+1}+Bz-c+u^k\|^2\right\},\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+\bar a^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c.\]
Values \(0<\alpha<1\) give under-relaxation, \(\alpha=1\) ordinary ADMM, and \(1<\alpha<2\) over-relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed ADMM replaces the new first-block constraint contribution by an affine relaxation before updating the second block and scaled dual variable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions.
The two displayed minimization problems attain solutions.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recursion defines under-relaxed, ordinary, or over-relaxed ADMM according to \(\alpha\).

children.title: Multi-Block ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM extensions coordinating more than two primal blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Block ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Gauss–Seidel extension of scaled ADMM to finitely many primal blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i=b\), where \(m\geq2\). Choose \(\rho>0\), initialize \((x_1^0,\ldots,x_m^0,u^0)\), and for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) set
\[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|\sum_{j<i}A_jx_j^{k+1}+A_ix_i+\sum_{j>i}A_jx_j^k-b+u^k\right\|^2\right\}.\]
After the sweep, set
\[u^{k+1}=u^k+\sum_{i=1}^m A_i x_i^{k+1}-b.\]
This recursion is the direct sequential multi-block ADMM; its definition alone does not assert convergence for \(m\geq3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-block ADMM minimizes the augmented Lagrangian sequentially over every block, using newly updated earlier blocks, then performs one dual update.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper and closed.
Every displayed block subproblem attains a minimizer.
All spaces are finite-dimensional and the linear maps \(A_i\) have compatible ranges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gauss–Seidel sweep and residual update define the direct multi-block ADMM sequence.

children.title: Jacobi-Type ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using parallel block schedules based on stale shared states.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobi-Type ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel multi-block ADMM using the previous iterate in all cross-block residual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i=b\), choose \(\rho>0\) and positive-semidefinite operators \(P_i\). From \((x^k,u^k)\), compute all blocks in parallel by
\[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\|A_ix_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_jx_j^k-b+u^k\right\|^2+\frac12\|x_i-x_i^k\|_{P_i}^2\right\},\quad i=1,\ldots,m.\]
Then update
\[u^{k+1}=u^k+\gamma\left(\sum_{i=1}^mA_ix_i^{k+1}-b\right),\]
where \(\gamma>0\). Setting every \(P_i=0\) gives the unregularized Jacobi-type update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobi-type ADMM updates all primal blocks simultaneously from the same old iterate, optionally adds proximal stabilization, and then updates the dual variable.
assumptions_latex: Each parallel block subproblem attains a minimizer.
\(P_i\succeq0\) for every block.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The simultaneous block minimizations followed by the residual step define a Jacobi-type ADMM iteration.

notation.meaning: quadratic form induced by the positive-semidefinite operator

children.title: Multi-Block Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee limitations associated with additional blocks or parallel block schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Block Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unconditional convergence for the direct three-block Gauss–Seidel extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_1=f_2=f_3=0\), let each \(x_i\in\mathbb R\), and impose \(a_1x_1+a_2x_2+a_3x_3=0\), where
\[a_1=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T},\qquad a_2=(1,1,2)^{\mathsf T},\qquad a_3=(1,2,2)^{\mathsf T}.\]
The constraint matrix is nonsingular, so the unique feasible primal point is \(x=0\). Nevertheless, the linear iteration obtained by the direct sequential three-block ADMM has spectral radius strictly greater than \(1\). Hence some initial primal-dual states generate an unbounded sequence. Convexity, solvability, and exact block minimization therefore do not by themselves guarantee convergence of direct multi-block ADMM when \(m\geq3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular three-block linear feasibility problem makes direct sequential ADMM diverge, showing that ordinary two-block assumptions do not extend automatically.
assumptions_latex: The direct Gauss–Seidel three-block ADMM update is used with any fixed \(\rho>0\).
Block subproblems are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist initial states for which the three-block ADMM iterates diverge despite a unique primal solution.

notation.meaning: constraint column associated with scalar block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the constraint matrix is nonsingular, but the decisive claim that the induced ADMM iteration has spectral radius greater than one requires a direct, inspectable source. No citation is supplied.

children.title: Randomized ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM variants using randomized participant or block activation.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized coordinate activation of an ADMM fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W=W_1\times\cdots\times W_m\), and let \(T:W\to W\) be a fixed-point operator whose full update \(w^{k+1}=T(w^k)\) is an ADMM iteration. For a random nonempty subset \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define
\[w_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}(T(w^k))_i,&i\in S_k,\\w_i^k,&i\notin S_k.\end{cases}\]
Equivalently, \(w^{k+1}=w^k+P_{S_k}(T(w^k)-w^k)\), where \(P_{S_k}\) retains precisely the selected coordinates. The output after a prescribed stopping test is the current primal-dual state \(w^k\). Convergence requires additional operator and sampling hypotheses not contained in this algorithmic definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized ADMM applies only randomly selected coordinates of a full ADMM fixed-point update and leaves all other coordinates unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The state space has a specified finite block decomposition.
The full ADMM step admits a single-valued fixed-point representation \(T\).
Each sampled set \(S_k\) is measurable with respect to the sampling process.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^{k+1}=w^k+P_{S_k}(T(w^k)-w^k)\) defines the randomized coordinate-update ADMM sequence.

notation.meaning: random set of coordinates activated at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate realization of an ADMM fixed-point step under a prescribed activation schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:W_1\times\cdots\times W_m\to W_1\times\cdots\times W_m\) represent one full ADMM primal-dual update. Given \(w^0\) and a prescribed nonempty activation set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,
\ldots,m\}\), perform
\[w_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}(T(w^k))_i,&i\in S_k,\\w_i^k,&i\notin S_k,\end{cases}\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\]
The schedule may be cyclic, essentially cyclic, greedy, or otherwise deterministic. Stop when the chosen primal and dual residual tests are satisfied, and return the current primal-dual coordinates. This definition does not itself guarantee convergence for an arbitrary schedule or arbitrary ADMM operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate ADMM updates a prescribed subset of an ADMM state at each iteration while retaining all inactive coordinates.
assumptions_latex: The ADMM state has a finite block decomposition.
The full update operator \(T\) is single-valued on the iterates.
Each activation set \(S_k\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed partial fixed-point update defines coordinate ADMM for the schedule \((S_k)_{k\geq0}\).

notation.meaning: a primal or dual state block

children.title: Sampling Coverage Regimes
children.top_down_role: Activation patterns governing coverage of blocks or coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Activation conditions ensuring that randomized coordinate schedules do not permanently omit a block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_k\) be the random activation set and \(\mathcal F_k\) the history before iteration \(k\). Uniform conditional coverage holds when there is \(p_{\min}>0\) such that
\[\mathbb P(i\in S_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\geq p_{\min}\qquad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\text{ and every }k.\]
Essential coverage holds when
\[\mathbb P(i\in S_k\ \text{infinitely often})=1\qquad\text{for every }i.\]
Uniform conditional coverage implies essential coverage under the usual adapted sampling construction. Merely positive unconditional probabilities at isolated iterations do not constitute a uniform coverage regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampling schedule has coverage when every coordinate remains conditionally selectable with uniform positive probability, or at least is activated infinitely often almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \((S_k)_{k\geq0}\) is adapted to a filtration \((\mathcal F_{k+1})_{k\geq0}\).
The number of coordinate blocks \(m\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform conditional coverage is the predicate \(\inf_{i,k}\mathbb P(i\in S_k\mid\mathcal F_k)>0\); essential coverage is infinite activation almost surely.

notation.meaning: sampling and iteration history before step k
uniform lower bound on conditional activation probability

children.title: Asynchronous ADMM
children.top_down_role: ADMM families permitting participants to proceed without global synchronization.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lock-free coordinate ADMM using a possibly inconsistent stale snapshot of the shared state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:W\to W\) be a full ADMM fixed-point operator on \(W=W_1\times\cdots\times W_m\). At event \(k\), a worker selects \(i_k\), reads a snapshot \(\hat w^k\), and atomically writes
\[w_{i_k}^{k+1}=w_{i_k}^k+\eta_k\bigl((T(\hat w^k))_{i_k}-\hat w_{i_k}^k\bigr),\qquad w_j^{k+1}=w_j^k\quad(j\ne i_k),\]
where \(\eta_k>0\). The snapshot may combine coordinates from different earlier events. Initialization supplies \(w^0\); termination uses prescribed primal-dual residual or event-budget criteria. Sampling, stepsize, memory consistency, and delay restrictions are separate hypotheses required by convergence results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous ADMM lets workers compute coordinate corrections from stale shared states and commit those corrections without a global iteration barrier.
assumptions_latex: The shared state has finitely many atomically writable blocks.
The full ADMM update is represented by a single-valued operator \(T\).
Each event commits one selected coordinate correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The event recursion defines an asynchronous coordinate implementation of the ADMM fixed-point map.

notation.meaning: possibly inconsistent stale snapshot read at event k

children.title: Delayed-Information ADMM

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Information ADMM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise delay representation for stale reads in asynchronous ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w^k=(w_1^k,\ldots,w_m^k)\) denote the shared ADMM state after event \(k\). A delayed-information snapshot has the componentwise representation
\[\hat w^k=\bigl(w_1^{k-d_{k,1}},\ldots,w_m^{k-d_{k,m}}\bigr),\qquad 0\leq d_{k,j}\leq k.\]
An asynchronous coordinate update based on this information is
\[w^{k+1}=w^k+\eta_kP_{i_k}\bigl(T(\hat w^k)-\hat w^k\bigr).\]
Equal delays produce a consistent historical snapshot; unequal delays model an inconsistent read. Thus delayed-information ADMM is represented by an ADMM fixed-point correction evaluated at componentwise past states rather than at \(w^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed-information ADMM evaluates its update using state components read from possibly different past iterations, represented by coordinatewise delay indices.
assumptions_latex: The shared state is partitioned into finitely many blocks.
Every delay \(d_{k,j}\) is an integer satisfying \(0\leq d_{k,j}\leq k\).
The ADMM update admits a fixed-point operator \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat w_j^k=w_j^{k-d_{k,j}}\) gives the componentwise delayed-state representation used by the asynchronous update.

notation.meaning: age of coordinate j used at event k

children.title: Bounded-Staleness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes classified by limits on information age.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Staleness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform and eventual bounds on componentwise ages in delayed ADMM reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For component delays \(d_{k,j}\), uniform bounded staleness holds when there exists an integer \(\tau<\infty\) such that
\[0\leq d_{k,j}\leq\min\{\tau,k\}\qquad\text{for every event }k\text{ and coordinate }j.\]
An eventual bounded-staleness regime permits a finite transient: there exist \(K<\infty\) and \(\tau<\infty\) for which the same inequality holds whenever \(k\geq K\). A bound on average delay alone is not uniform bounded staleness. These predicates constrain information age but do not, without operator, stepsize, and activation assumptions, imply convergence of asynchronous ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded staleness requires every coordinate used by a worker to be at most a fixed finite number of update events old.
assumptions_latex: Each delayed read has component ages \(d_{k,j}\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\).
The coordinate set is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform bounded staleness is exactly the existence of \(\tau<\infty\) with \(\sup_{k,j}d_{k,j}\leq\tau\).

notation.meaning: end of a permitted finite transient

children.title: Unbounded-Delay Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Guarantee limitations arising when participant delays lack effective control.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Delay Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of fixed-point convergence when stale information may remain permanently old.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(T(x)=qx\) with \(0<q<1\), so \(T\) is a contraction with unique fixed point \(0\). Choose \(x^0\ne0\) and the admissible but unbounded delays \(d_k=k\). The delayed iteration
\[x^{k+1}=T(x^{k-d_k})\]
then satisfies \(x^{k+1}=qx^0\) for every \(k\geq0\), and therefore does not converge to the fixed point. Thus contraction of the synchronous operator does not ensure convergence when an asynchronous ADMM fixed-point analysis permits coordinates to read indefinitely old values; a freshness, bounded-delay, or comparable information condition is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a contraction can fail under delays that always reuse the initial state, so asynchronous convergence cannot allow permanently stale information without safeguards.
assumptions_latex: The delay sequence is \(d_k=k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The delayed iterates remain equal to \(qx^0\) after the first event and fail to approach the unique fixed point \(0\).

children.title: Classical Convex Two-Block Convergence
children.top_down_role: The baseline convex convergence family for canonical ADMM.

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Convex Two-Block Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, exact, canonical two-block ADMM with a fixed positive penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times m}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^p\). Starting from arbitrary \(z^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(y^0\in\mathbb{R}^p\), define \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(x)+\langle y^k,Ax+Bz^k-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax+Bz^k-c\|^2\right\},\] \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathbb{R}^m}\left\{g(z)+\langle y^k,Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|Ax^{k+1}+Bz-c\|^2\right\},\] and \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho r^{k+1}\), where \(r^{k+1}=Ax^{k+1}+Bz^{k+1}-c\). Then \(r^k\to0\), \(f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p^\star\), and \(y^k\to y^\star\) for some dual solution \(y^\star\). Every cluster point of \((x^k,z^k)\), when one exists, is primal optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite-dimensional exact two-block convex ADMM, feasibility residuals vanish, objective values approach the optimum, and dual iterates approach a dual solution. Any primal cluster point is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times m}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The problem \(\min\{f(x)+g(z):Ax+Bz=c\}\) has a saddle point, and each ADMM subproblem attains a minimizer.
The penalty satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^k\to0\), \(f(x^k)+g(z^k)\to p^\star\), and \(y^k\to y^\star\) for some dual solution \(y^\star\); every cluster point of \((x^k,z^k)\) is primal optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w^k=(x^k,z^k,y^k)\) be the ADMM primal-dual iterates and let \(\bar w^K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K}w^k\). The one-step variational inequality for ADMM telescopes under summation, yielding, for every saddle point \(w\), \[\mathcal{G}(\bar w^K;w)\le \frac{C(w)}{K},\] where \(C(w)<\infty\) depends on the initial primal-dual distance and \(\rho\), but not on \(K\). Thus an ergodic gap not exceeding \(\varepsilon>0\) is obtained after at most \(\lceil C(w)/\varepsilon\rceil\) iterations.

assumptions_latex: A reported convergence criterion is evaluated only at the Cesàro averages \(\bar u^K=K^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^{K}u^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convergence or a rate for \(\bar u^K\) alone does not imply convergence or the same rate for \(u^K\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary Cesaro-sequence counterexample separates averaged and last-iterate behavior
ADMM-specific sharpness source remains to be attached
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between ergodic guarantees and guarantees for actual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the scalar sequence \(u^k=(-1)^k\). Its Cesàro averages satisfy \[\bar u^K=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}(-1)^k\longrightarrow0,\] and indeed \(|\bar u^K|\le K^{-1}\), while \(u^k\) has no limit and \(|u^{k+1}-u^k|=2\). Hence an \(O(K^{-1})\) estimate for an averaged quantity cannot, without additional regularity or monotonicity, be transferred to the last iterate. In ADMM rate statements, the averaging operator and the quantity averaged must therefore be recorded explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast convergence of averaged iterates does not imply convergence of actual iterates; an alternating scalar sequence has vanishing averages but never converges.
knowledge_statements.title: Averaging Gap Regimes

children.title: Linear-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Linear-rate families under stronger convexity, smoothness, polyhedrality, or error-bound structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract local linear-rate criterion covering several stronger-structure ADMM regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\), and let \(N\) be an invariant neighborhood of \(S\). Suppose that for every \(u\in N\), \[\operatorname{dist}(Tu,S)^2\le\operatorname{dist}(u,S)^2-c\|u-Tu\|^2\] and \[\operatorname{dist}(u,S)\le\kappa\|u-Tu\|,\] where \(0<c\le\kappa^2\). If \(u^0\in N\) and \(u^{k+1}=Tu^k\), then, with \(q=1-c/\kappa^2\in[0,1)\), \[\operatorname{dist}(u^k,S)\le q^{k/2}\operatorname{dist}(u^0,S).\] Any residual bounded above by a fixed multiple of \(\operatorname{dist}(u^k,S)\) converges R-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An averaged ADMM fixed-point iteration converges locally and linearly in distance to its solution set when a fixed-point error bound and a compatible decrease inequality hold throughout an invariant neighborhood.
assumptions_latex: The ADMM state satisfies \(u^{k+1}=Tu^k\), and \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
There is an invariant neighborhood \(N\) of \(S\) containing \(u^0\).
For every \(u\in N\), \(\operatorname{dist}(Tu,S)^2\le\operatorname{dist}(u,S)^2-c\|u-Tu\|^2\).
For every \(u\in N\), \(\operatorname{dist}(u,S)\le\kappa\|u-Tu\|\), with \(0<c\le\kappa^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(u^k,S)\le q^{k/2}\operatorname{dist}(u^0,S)\), where \(q=1-c/\kappa^2\in[0,1)\).

notation.meaning: Invariant neighborhood on which the local estimates hold

children.title: Inexact ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence classifications permitting controlled local solution errors.

assumptions_latex: Exact ADMM is represented by an averaged map \(T\) with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
The computed update satisfies \(u^{k+1}=Tu^k+e^k\).
The deterministic errors are absolutely summable: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inexact states \(u^k\) converge to a point of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \(\|u^k-Tu^k\|\to0\).
review_flags: the conversion from subproblem optimality errors to the aggregate perturbation must be checked for each inexact ADMM formulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute-summability perturbation model for finite-dimensional inexact ADMM.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the inexact ADMM state obey \(u^{k+1}=Tu^k+e^k\), where \(T\) is averaged and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|e^k\|<\infty\). Then the perturbed iteration is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\), its fixed-point residual satisfies \[\|u^k-Tu^k\|\longrightarrow0,\] and, in finite dimensions, \(u^k\) converges to some \(u^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). Consequently, the associated primal-dual variables converge whenever the chosen ADMM state-to-solution correspondence is single-valued or continuous on the limit set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact ADMM retains fixed-point convergence when each computed update is an exact averaged-map update plus an absolutely summable error.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact ADMM Convergence

children.title: Variable-Metric ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence classifications permitting iteration-dependent or block-dependent metrics.

assumptions_latex: Each \(H_k\) is self-adjoint and uniformly coercive and bounded: \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) for fixed \(0<m\le M<\infty\).
Metric growth is summable: \(H_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)H_k\) with \(\eta_k\ge0\) and \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\).
The metric ADMM step is Fejér-decreasing up to the factor \(1+\eta_k\) and has the usual fixed-point demiclosedness property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The variable-metric ADMM state converges to a solution and its step residual vanishes.
review_flags: metric Fejer inequality must be instantiated for the selected variable-metric ADMM update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric convergence under uniform equivalence and summable metric variation.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the ADMM solution set. Suppose that for every \(u^\star\in S\), \[\|u^{k+1}-u^\star\|_{H_{k+1}}^2\le(1+\eta_k)\|u^k-u^\star\|_{H_k}^2-c\|u^{k+1}-u^k\|_{H_k}^2\] for some \(c>0\). Under uniform metric equivalence and \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), the distances have limits and \(\sum_k\|u^{k+1}-u^k\|_{H_k}^2<\infty\). If every cluster point with vanishing step residual lies in \(S\), then \(u^k\) converges to a point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-metric ADMM converges when metrics remain uniformly equivalent, change by a summable relative amount, and support a variable-metric Fejér decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric ADMM Convergence

children.title: Combined Error-Metric Regimes
children.top_down_role: Convergence regimes combining local inexactness with changing metrics.

assumptions_latex: The variable metrics satisfy the uniform-equivalence and summable-variation conditions of node \(\mathrm{A07.C04.BAL02.N2472CAEB4839.ANDB74244F98E}\).
The inexact update is \(u^{k+1}=T_k u^k+e^k\), where each \(T_k\) satisfies the required metric Fejér decrease.
The weighted perturbations are summable: \(\sum_k\|e^k\|_{H_{k+1}}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined variable-metric, inexact iteration converges to a common fixed point and has vanishing fixed-point residual.

notation.meaning: Exact update in the current metric

review_flags: a combined ADMM-specific theorem locator is needed to confirm the precise compatibility condition between metric change and subproblem errors

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(u^{k+1}=T_k u^k+e^k\), metric variation and computational error enter the quasi-Fejér estimate as separate summable perturbations. If \(H_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)H_k\), \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), and \(\sum_k\|e^k\|_{H_{k+1}}<\infty\), then the resulting perturbation remains summable. Provided the exact maps \(T_k\) share the ADMM solution set and satisfy a uniform metric decrease condition, \(u^k\) converges to a common fixed point and \(\|u^k-T_k u^k\|_{H_k}\to0\). Neither summability condition generally substitutes for the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADMM may combine varying metrics and inexact solves when metric drift and update errors are separately summable and exact metric updates share the same solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Combined Error-Metric Regimes

children.title: Stochastic-Asynchronous ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence under partial participation, randomization, and bounded delay models.

children.title: Randomized ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence classifications under randomized block or participant activation.

assumptions_latex: The ADMM fixed-point state is partitioned into finitely many blocks, and the full map \(T\) is averaged with \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
At iteration \(k\), block \(i_k\) is sampled independently with probabilities \(p_i\ge p_{\min}>0\).
Only the sampled block of \(u^k\) is replaced by the corresponding block of \(Tu^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^k\) converges almost surely to a point of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\), and \(\mathbb{E}\|u^k-Tu^k\|^2\to0\).
review_flags: requires an ADMM splitting whose randomized block replacement is a valid coordinate fixed-point iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent positive-probability coordinate activation of an averaged ADMM fixed-point map.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the randomized block update \[u^{k+1}=u^k+P_{i_k}(Tu^k-u^k),\qquad \mathbb{P}(i_k=i)=p_i.\] With the probability-weighted product norm, averagedness gives a conditional expected Fejér decrease proportional to \(\|u^k-Tu^k\|^2\). Because \(p_i\ge p_{\min}>0\), every block is activated infinitely often almost surely. Consequently, \(\|u^k-Tu^k\|\to0\) almost surely and in mean square, and in finite dimensions \(u^k\) converges almost surely to a point of \(\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized block ADMM converges almost surely when it is a coordinate update of an averaged fixed-point map and every block has uniformly positive sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized ADMM Convergence

children.title: Asynchronous ADMM Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence classifications under unsynchronized participant execution.

assumptions_latex: A worker update is computed from a delayed state \(u^{k-d_k}\) and committed to the current shared state.
Every block is activated infinitely often, delays are controlled, and conflicting writes obey a specified atomic or consistent-read model.
The relaxation is small enough to dominate the error caused by stale reads.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under a delay-aware quasi-Fejér inequality, the asynchronous residual vanishes and every cluster point is an ADMM solution.
review_flags: exact asynchronous ADMM theorem depends on the read-write model, activation law, delay model, and relaxation bound
provided locator concerns classical distributed iterations rather than a confirmed ADMM theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence interface for stale-read block ADMM; no universal delay-independent theorem is asserted.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Convergence Analysis of Classical Iterative Methods p. 143
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An asynchronous block update has the form \[u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha P_{i_k}\bigl(Tu^{k-d_k}-u^{k-d_k}\bigr).\] Convergence requires a Lyapunov function \(V_k\) for which, conditionally on the update history \(\mathcal{F}_k\), \[\mathbb{E}[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\le V_k-c\,\mathbb{E}[\|u^k-Tu^k\|^2\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\] with \(c>0\). This inequality must account for stale-read cross terms, activation probabilities, and write consistency. When it holds and the iterates are bounded, the residual vanishes and all cluster points belong to \(\operatorname{Fix}T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous ADMM convergence requires a delay-aware Lyapunov decrease, persistent block activation, a defined read-write model, and relaxation sufficient to absorb stale-read errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous ADMM Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Convergence Analysis of Classical Iterative Methods p. 143

children.title: Bounded-Delay Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence classifications under controlled information staleness.

assumptions_latex: The asynchronous update is \(u^{k+1}=u^k+\alpha P_{i_k}(Tu^{k-d_k}-u^{k-d_k})\).
There is a deterministic delay bound \(0\le d_k\le\tau<\infty\), and every block is activated persistently.
A delay-augmented Lyapunov inequality holds with a strictly positive residual coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The residual \(\|u^k-Tu^k\|\) converges to zero, and cluster points are fixed points of \(T\).
review_flags: a source giving an ADMM-specific admissible relaxation bound as a function of maximum delay is missing
provided source is indirect classical asynchronous-iteration support
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient bounded-delay predicate expressed through a delay-augmented descent inequality.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Convergence Analysis of Classical Iterative Methods p. 143
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bounded-delay convergence is certified when there exist weights \(a_1,\ldots,a_\tau\ge0\) and \(c_\tau>0\) such that \[V_k=\operatorname{dist}(u^k,S)^2+\sum_{j=1}^{\tau}a_j\|u^{k+1-j}-u^{k-j}\|^2\] satisfies \[\mathbb{E}[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_k]\le V_k-c_\tau\|u^k-Tu^k\|^2.\] Here \(S=\operatorname{Fix}T\), and the admissible relaxation must make \(c_\tau\) positive. Summation then yields residual convergence; boundedness and demiclosedness identify cluster points as fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite delay bound supports convergence when a Lyapunov function augmented by recent step differences decreases by a positive multiple of the current fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Delay Convergence

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Convergence Analysis of Classical Iterative Methods p. 143

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate for a bounded-delay predicate, but the decisive Lyapunov inequality is assumed rather than linked to checkable ADMM parameters. An ADMM-specific source must supply the read model and an admissible relaxation bound as a function of delay and sampling.

children.title: Sampling–Delay Interaction
children.top_down_role: Regimes where randomized participation interacts with delayed information.

assumptions_latex: Block \(i\) is sampled with probability \(p_i>0\) and may use information delayed by at most \(\tau_i\) commits.
Convergence analysis charges stale-read errors over the updates occurring during each block's delay window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interaction burden \(D=\max_i(\tau_i+1)/p_i\) increases when sampling becomes rarer or delays grow; convergence parameters must control their joint effect.
review_flags: the displayed exposure index is an interface quantity rather than a claimed universal sharp ADMM constant
an authoritative source for a precise sampling-delay theorem is missing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint exposure condition separating sampling frequency from block-specific delay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the blockwise sampling-delay exposure by \[D=\max_i\frac{\tau_i+1}{p_i}.\] Any convergence condition whose stale-read term is bounded by update opportunities over a delay window must depend jointly on \(p_i\) and \(\tau_i\), rather than on \(p_{\min}\) or \(\tau_{\max}\) alone. In particular, \(D=+\infty\) if some required block has \(p_i=0\) or unbounded delay, so no positive uniform descent coefficient can be inferred from this model. A finite \(D\), together with a theorem-specific relaxation restriction that preserves positive Lyapunov descent, is a sufficient interface requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling and delay interact blockwise: rare activation magnifies stale-information exposure, while zero activation or unbounded delay destroys any uniform descent guarantee based on this model.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling–Delay Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the interaction leaf, but D=max_i(τ_i+1)/p_i is introduced without evidence and is not a universal sampling-delay constant across asynchronous ADMM models. A precise theorem is required before this formula or its claimed sufficiency can be retained.

children.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualified stationarity and subsequential convergence families outside convex optimization.

assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper lower-semicontinuous functions, possibly nonconvex.
The ADMM sequence \(\{(x^k,z^k,y^k)\}\) is bounded, its primal residual converges to zero, and its subproblem optimality errors converge to zero.
The relevant limiting subdifferentials have closed graphs along convergent subsequences, and all displayed function values converge along those subsequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\) satisfies \(A\bar x+B\bar z=c\), \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\), and \(0\in\partial g(\bar z)+B^{\mathsf T}\bar y\).

notation.meaning: Limiting subdifferential of a proper lower-semicontinuous function.
A cluster point of the ADMM primal-dual sequence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional subsequential stationarity principle for finite-dimensional, possibly nonconvex two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\). Suppose an ADMM sequence \(\{(x^k,z^k,y^k)\}\) is bounded, \(Ax^k+Bz^k-c\to0\), and the errors in both block optimality inclusions converge to zero. If the limiting subdifferentials of \(f\) and \(g\) have closed graphs along convergent subsequences and the required function values converge, then every cluster point \((\bar x,\bar z,\bar y)\) is feasible and satisfies \(0\in\partial f(\bar x)+A^{\mathsf T}\bar y\) and \(0\in\partial g(\bar z)+B^{\mathsf T}\bar y\). This conclusion asserts qualified stationarity only, not global or local optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under boundedness, vanishing feasibility and subproblem errors, and subdifferential closedness, every ADMM cluster point satisfies the coupling constraint and limiting first-order stationarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the nonconvex subsequential-stationarity claim. In particular, “subproblem optimality errors” does not identify the inclusions or address the update-order defect needed to obtain stationarity at a common iterate.

children.title: Primal Feasibility Residuals

assumptions_latex: The coupling constraint is \(Ax+Bz=c\) in a finite-dimensional normed space.
The reported iterate is \((x^k,z^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\|r_p^k\|\leq\varepsilon_p\) certifies coupling feasibility to tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-coupled problem \(\min_{x,z} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), define the primal residual by \(r_p^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\). For any specified norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\geq0\), the check \(\|r_p^k\|\leq\varepsilon_p\) is a directly verifiable certificate that the current blocks satisfy the coupling relation within that tolerance. Exact primal feasibility is equivalent to \(r_p^k=0\). This residual alone does not certify stationarity, objective accuracy, or problem status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The norm of the coupling violation is a directly checkable certificate of approximate primal feasibility, but it does not establish optimality or problem status.

children.title: Dual Consistency Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence concerning consistency of dual-side coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Consistency Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard two-block ADMM dual-consistency residual for the stated update order and multiplier convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,z\in\mathbb R^m} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(A\) and \(B\) are compatible linear maps. For exact two-block ADMM with \(x\)-then-\(z\) updates and multiplier update \(y^k=y^{k-1}+\rho(Ax^k+Bz^k-c)\), define \(s^k=\rho A^{\mathsf T}B(z^k-z^{k-1})\). The \(x\)-subproblem optimality condition can then be rewritten as \(0\in\partial f(x^k)+A^{\mathsf T}y^k-s^k\). Hence \(\|s^k\|\leq\varepsilon_d\), for a specified norm and \(\varepsilon_d\geq0\), certifies approximate consistency between the current multiplier and the \(x\)-block stationarity condition. The signed formula depends on block order and multiplier scaling and must be transformed under another ADMM convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated update order and multiplier convention, the scaled change in the second block is the signed defect in current first-block stationarity; its norm measures dual consistency.
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,z\in\mathbb R^m} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with compatible linear maps \(A\) and \(B\).
ADMM updates \(x^k\), then \(z^k\), and then \(y^k=y^{k-1}+\rho(Ax^k+Bz^k-c)\), where \(\rho>0\).
The \(x\)-subproblem is solved exactly and its optimality inclusion uses the stated subdifferential \(\partial f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(s^k=\rho A^{\mathsf T}B(z^k-z^{k-1})\), the current inclusion is \(0\in\partial f(x^k)+A^{\mathsf T}y^k-s^k\), so \(\|s^k\|\) measures its dual-consistency defect.

children.title: Stationarity Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence concerning first-order stationarity of candidate solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex KKT-inclusion residuals for finite-dimensional equality-coupled composite optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,z\in\mathbb R^m} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions and \(A\) and \(B\) are compatible linear maps. At \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\), define \(\eta_x^k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(x^k)+A^{\mathsf T}y^k)\) and \(\eta_z^k=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial g(z^k)+B^{\mathsf T}y^k)\), using specified norms and the convex subdifferential. If \(\eta_x^k\leq\varepsilon_x\) and \(\eta_z^k\leq\varepsilon_z\), these checks certify approximate satisfaction of the two stationarity inclusions. Together with a small primal feasibility residual, they form an approximate convex KKT residual system. These residuals alone do not certify objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex equality-coupled problem, distances to the two KKT subdifferential inclusions measure block stationarity and, together with feasibility, form an approximate KKT certificate.
assumptions_latex: The problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,z\in\mathbb R^m} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with compatible linear maps \(A\) and \(B\).
The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions, and \(\partial\) denotes the convex subdifferential.
Distances are computed in specified finite-dimensional norms, with tolerances \(\varepsilon_x,\varepsilon_z\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\eta_x^k\leq\varepsilon_x\) and \(\eta_z^k\leq\varepsilon_z\) certify approximate satisfaction of the two convex stationarity inclusions at \((x^k,z^k,y^k)\).

notation.meaning: Distance from a point to a set in the specified norm.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite checks such as \(\|r_p^k\|\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\eta_x^k\leq\varepsilon_x\), and \(\eta_z^k\leq\varepsilon_z\) certify only the displayed approximate relations. Without convexity and a valid primal-dual bound, they do not bound objective suboptimality. Without an error bound, small residuals need not imply a nearby solution. Without a strict separating vector or a feasible negative-recession direction, residual growth or iterate divergence certifies neither infeasibility nor unboundedness. Thus residual thresholds must not be interpreted as complete problem-status certificates outside their stated regularity regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual thresholds certify only their defining approximate equations; stronger claims about distance, objective accuracy, infeasibility, or unboundedness require additional assumptions or rays.
