children.title: Objective-Value Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence concerning achieved or bounded objective values.

assumptions_latex: A feasible point \((\hat x,\hat z)\) is available with finite value \(U=f(\hat x)+g(\hat z)\).
A verified lower bound \(L\leq p^\star\) on the optimal value is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interval \(L\leq p^\star\leq U\) and gap \(U-L\) certify the objective value and suboptimality of the feasible point.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper objective bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective interval certificate from a feasible incumbent and a valid lower bound.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\hat x,\hat z)\) satisfy \(A\hat x+B\hat z=c\), and set \(U=f(\hat x)+g(\hat z)\). If an independently valid bound \(L\leq p^\star\) is available for the optimal value \(p^\star\), then \(L\leq p^\star\leq U\). Consequently, \(U-L\) is a verifiable upper bound on the incumbent suboptimality \(U-p^\star\). For a requested tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), feasibility together with \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. An objective value without a valid lower bound is not an objective-accuracy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent supplies an upper bound; paired with a verified lower bound, their difference certifies the incumbent's objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Certificates

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence concerning separation between compatible primal and dual values.

assumptions_latex: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions.
The point \((x,z)\) is primal feasible, and \(y\) gives finite conjugate values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable quantity \(G(x,z,y)=p(x,z)-q(y)\geq0\) certifies primal suboptimality by \(p(x,z)-p^\star\leq G(x,z,y)\).

notation.meaning: Primal objective at a feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-Lagrange gap certificate for convex equality-coupled problems.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper closed convex \(f\) and \(g\), let \((x,z)\) satisfy \(Ax+Bz=c\), and define \(p(x,z)=f(x)+g(z)\). For any \(y\) with finite conjugate terms, define \(q(y)=-f^*(-A^{\mathsf T}y)-g^*(-B^{\mathsf T}y)-c^{\mathsf T}y\). Weak duality gives \(q(y)\leq p^\star\leq p(x,z)\), so \(G(x,z,y)=p(x,z)-q(y)\geq0\) is computable and satisfies \(p(x,z)-p^\star\leq G(x,z,y)\). Therefore \(G(x,z,y)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality of the feasible primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex problems, a feasible primal point and finite dual point produce a nonnegative gap that upper-bounds primal objective error.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificates

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Gap Availability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Formulation regimes determining whether meaningful primal–dual gap evidence is available.

assumptions_latex: The equality-coupled objective is represented by proper closed convex functions \(f\) and \(g\).
The required function, conjugate, and feasibility quantities can be evaluated with certified numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite primal-dual gap certificate is available precisely when certified primal and dual bounds can both be evaluated at the reported points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Availability predicate for computable convex primal-dual gap certificates.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex problem \(\min f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), a finite primal-dual gap can be reported at \((x,z,y)\) when \(Ax+Bz=c\), \(f(x)+g(z)<+\infty\), and both \(f^*(-A^{\mathsf T}y)\) and \(g^*(-B^{\mathsf T}y)\) are finite and computable. Under these conditions, \(p(x,z)-q(y)\) is a certified gap. If primal feasibility is only approximate, conjugates are unavailable, or the model is nonconvex without another valid lower bound, the same expression is not automatically an objective-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified gap requires evaluable finite primal and dual bounds; approximate feasibility, unavailable conjugates, or nonconvexity can make the standard gap unavailable.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap Availability Regimes

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Problem-Status Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Problem-status evidence derived from divergent directions or embedding formulations.

children.title: Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Problem-status evidence supporting absence of primal or dual feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: The sets \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(Z\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) are nonempty closed convex sets.
Feasibility means finding \((x,z)\in X\times Z\) such that \(Ax+Bz=c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any \(y\) satisfying \(\sigma_X(A^{\mathsf T}y)+\sigma_Z(B^{\mathsf T}y)-c^{\mathsf T}y<0\) certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Support function of a closed convex set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation certificate for convex coupling feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Z\) be nonempty closed convex sets. If a vector \(y\) satisfies \(\sigma_X(A^{\mathsf T}y)+\sigma_Z(B^{\mathsf T}y)-c^{\mathsf T}y<0\), then every \((x,z)\in X\times Z\) obeys \(y^{\mathsf T}(Ax+Bz-c)<0\). Equality \(Ax+Bz=c\) would instead force this inner product to equal zero, which is impossible. Thus the displayed strict inequality is a directly checkable infeasibility certificate whenever both support-function values are rigorously evaluated. Mere multiplier growth without this separating inequality is not such a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector strictly separating the coupling target from all attainable coupled images certifies that no feasible pair exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-function inequality has the correct sufficient separation orientation, but no inspectable Farkas or separation source is supplied. The statement also includes proof-style explanatory steps that should be removed when a sourced candidate is resubmitted.

children.title: Unboundedness Certificates
children.top_down_role: Problem-status evidence supporting unbounded objective behavior.

assumptions_latex: The functions \(f\) and \(g\) are proper closed convex functions, and a feasible point \((x_0,z_0)\) exists.
Their recession functions \(f^\infty\) and \(g^\infty\) can be evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direction \((d_x,d_z)\) with \(Ad_x+Bd_z=0\) and \(f^\infty(d_x)+g^\infty(d_z)<0\) certifies \(p^\star=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-recession certificate for convex objective unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((x_0,z_0)\) is feasible for \(\min f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(Ax+Bz=c\), with proper closed convex \(f\) and \(g\). If a nonzero direction \((d_x,d_z)\) satisfies \(Ad_x+Bd_z=0\) and \(f^\infty(d_x)+g^\infty(d_z)<0\), then \((x_0+t d_x,z_0+t d_z)\) remains feasible for every \(t\geq0\), and its objective tends to \(-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\). The direction and strict recession inequality therefore certify that the primal optimal value is \(p^\star=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction preserving the coupling and having strictly negative total recession cost certifies that the convex objective is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Unboundedness Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-recession certificate is standard for proper closed convex functions, but it lacks a theorem or section citation. The assumptions should also explicitly require the feasible base point to have finite objective value.

children.title: Divergent-Direction Evidence
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic direction evidence used to distinguish problem-status outcomes.

assumptions_latex: A sequence of ADMM differences has normalized accumulation direction \((d_x,d_z)\neq(0,0)\).
The original convex problem has a verified feasible base point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting direction is an unboundedness certificate only after verifying \(Ad_x+Bd_z=0\) and \(f^\infty(d_x)+g^\infty(d_z)<0\).

notation.meaning: Normalized accumulation direction of iterate differences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of divergent iterate directions into rigorous recession certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose along a subsequence \((x^{k+1}-x^k,z^{k+1}-z^k)/\tau_k\to(d_x,d_z)\) for positive \(\tau_k\), with \((d_x,d_z)\neq(0,0)\). This limit is only divergent-direction evidence until its model implications are checked. If one additionally verifies \(Ad_x+Bd_z=0\), a feasible base point exists, and \(f^\infty(d_x)+g^\infty(d_z)<0\), then the direction becomes a rigorous certificate of primal unboundedness below. Without these checks, even stable normalized divergence does not distinguish unboundedness from infeasibility, nonconvergence, or poor scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized divergent direction becomes an unboundedness certificate only after it is shown to preserve feasibility and strictly decrease the recession objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Divergent-Direction Evidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the conversion of an ADMM difference limit into model-level directional evidence. Moreover, the leaf concerns evidence and the record emphasizes that the raw limit is not a certificate; a condition or failure-boundary role would fit better than certificate unless the verified recession conditions are made the record's primary object.

children.title: Status Ambiguity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where observed divergence does not uniquely identify infeasibility or unboundedness.

assumptions_latex: Only residual histories, multiplier growth, or iterate divergence are observed.
No strict separation inequality or feasible negative-recession direction has been verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The observed behavior alone cannot determine whether the model is infeasible, unbounded, feasible but nonconvergent, or merely poorly scaled.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between numerical warning signals and mathematically valid status certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Iterate divergence, multiplier growth, or failure of residuals to decrease is not by itself a problem-status certificate. Infeasibility requires a verified alternative such as a strict separating vector \(y\); unboundedness below requires a feasible recession direction \(d\) with strictly negative recession objective. If neither alternative is checked, the same qualitative numerical behavior may also arise from an inappropriate penalty, ill-conditioning, inexact subproblem solves, or failure of convergence assumptions. A certificate-control system must therefore report status as unresolved rather than infer infeasibility or unboundedness from divergence alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divergence and residual stagnation are warning signals, not status certificates; without a separating or negative-recession ray, the cause remains mathematically ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Ambiguity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the claims about indistinguishable causes of divergence and residual stagnation require an inspectable convergence or solver-status source with a specific locator.

children.title: ADMM Termination-Penalty Control
children.top_down_role: Implementation-level families for tolerances, scaling, and adaptive penalty selection.

children.title: Scale-Aware Stopping Calculus
children.top_down_role: Scale-aware termination organizations based on residual evidence.

children.title: Absolute Stopping Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Termination controls based on fixed residual tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Stopping Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute residual floors for finite-dimensional ADMM termination tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the primal and dual residuals at iteration \(k\) be \(r^k\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\) and \(s^k\in\mathbb{R}^{q}\). For an absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge 0\), define the dimension-adjusted absolute thresholds by \[\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri,abs}}=\sqrt{p}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{{dual,abs}}}=\sqrt{q}\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}.\] The absolute-only stopping condition is \(\lVert r^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri,abs}}\) and \(\lVert s^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual,abs}}\). The square-root factors make the tolerance correspond to a common root-mean-square residual allowance per coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute stopping scales a per-coordinate tolerance by the square root of each residual dimension and requires both residual norms to lie below their floors.
assumptions_latex: \(r^k\in\mathbb{R}^{p},\ s^k\in\mathbb{R}^{q}\)
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge 0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r^k\rVert_2\le\sqrt p\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\) and \(\lVert s^k\rVert_2\le\sqrt q\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}\).

notation.meaning: Dimensions of the primal and dual residual vectors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard dimension-scaled ADMM residual tolerance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dimension-adjusted absolute thresholds are mathematically standard and fit the definition container, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Relative Stopping Thresholds
children.top_down_role: Termination controls scaled to iterate, data, or residual magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Stopping Thresholds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative ADMM thresholds normalized by current primal and dual scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\), let \(y^k\) be the unscaled multiplier and let \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\). Define the relative primal and dual threshold components by \[\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri,rel}}^k=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{\lVert Ax^k\rVert_2,\lVert Bz^k\rVert_2,\lVert c\rVert_2\},\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual,rel}}^k=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\lVert A^{\mathsf T}y^k\rVert_2.\] These terms scale the admissible residuals with the magnitudes of the current primal constraint quantities and dual stationarity quantity, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative thresholds multiply a dimensionless tolerance by current primal constraint and dual stationarity scales.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax+Bz=c\) with compatible finite-dimensional spaces
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri,rel}}^k\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual,rel}}^k\) are homogeneous under consistent rescaling of their associated quantities.

notation.meaning: Linear constraint data in the two-block ADMM formulation.
Current primal variables and unscaled multiplier.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard scaled ADMM residual test
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-threshold formulas are standard and fit the container, but the record has no inspectable source supporting the precise ADMM convention.

children.title: Scale-Aware Threshold Composition
children.top_down_role: Organizations combining fixed tolerance floors with magnitude-sensitive stopping controls.

knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Aware Threshold Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined absolute-relative termination condition for two-block ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r^k=Ax^k+Bz^k-c\) and dual residual \(s^k\), compose the absolute and relative components additively: \[\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri}}^k=\sqrt p\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{\lVert Ax^k\rVert_2,\lVert Bz^k\rVert_2,\lVert c\rVert_2\},\] \[\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual}}^k=\sqrt q\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\lVert A^{\mathsf T}y^k\rVert_2.\] Terminate at iteration \(k\) exactly when \(\lVert r^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri}}^k\) and \(\lVert s^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual}}^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stopping test adds absolute residual floors to scale-dependent relative allowances and accepts only when both residual tests pass.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\)
\(r^k\in\mathbb R^p,\ s^k\in\mathbb R^q\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pri}}^k\) and \(\lVert s^k\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{dual}}^k\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional absolute-plus-relative ADMM stopping rule
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly composes the stated absolute and relative components, but the exact stopping convention lacks a cited source.

children.title: Residual-Balancing Penalty Families
children.top_down_role: Adaptive penalty families guided by relative residual behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Balancing Penalty Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative ADMM penalty adaptation driven by unequal normalized residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\rho_0>0\), imbalance factor \(\mu>1\), multiplier \(\tau>1\), and bounds \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}\). After computing residuals, set \[\widetilde\rho_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\tau\rho_k,&\lVert r^k\rVert_2>\mu\lVert s^k\rVert_2,\\ \rho_k/\tau,&\lVert s^k\rVert_2>\mu\lVert r^k\rVert_2,\\ \rho_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad \rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{\max},\max\{\rho_{\min},\widetilde\rho_{k+1}\}\}.\] If the scaled multiplier is \(u^k=y^k/\rho_k\), replace it after a penalty change by \(u^k\leftarrow(\rho_k/\rho_{k+1})u^k\), preserving \(y^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the penalty when primal residual dominates, decrease it when dual residual dominates, clip it, and rescale the scaled multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\) and the unscaled multiplier is unchanged by penalty rescaling.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional residual-balancing ADMM heuristic with multiplier rescaling
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm container is appropriate, but the scope promises normalized residual balancing while the formula compares raw residual norms, whose units and scaling may differ. A source is needed to fix the intended variant.

children.title: Geometry-Informed Penalty Family
children.top_down_role: Penalty-selection families informed by local spectral or curvature information.

children.title: Spectral Penalty Selection
children.top_down_role: Penalty choices informed by local spectral estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Penalty Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded secant-based penalty proposal for adaptive ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an update iteration, form accepted primal and dual secant pairs \((a_k,b_k)\) and \((c_k,d_k)\) from consecutive iterates and associated operator values. When \(\langle a_k,b_k\rangle>0\) and \(\langle c_k,d_k\rangle>0\), compute \[\alpha_k=\frac{\langle a_k,b_k\rangle}{\langle a_k,a_k\rangle},\qquad \beta_k=\frac{\langle c_k,d_k\rangle}{\langle c_k,c_k\rangle},\qquad \widehat\rho_{k+1}=\sqrt{\alpha_k\beta_k}.\] Set \(\rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{\max},\max\{\rho_{\min},\widehat\rho_{k+1}\}\}\). If either curvature test fails or a denominator vanishes, retain \(\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive secant curvatures produce a geometric-mean penalty proposal; invalid estimates are rejected and accepted proposals are clipped.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{[1mmax}\)
Secant pairs belong to compatible real inner-product spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\), with no update when the spectral estimate is inadmissible.
review_flags: Exact ADMM secant-pair convention and geometric-mean formula require an authoritative adaptive-ADMM source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The secant-pair definitions and geometric-mean rule depend on the particular spectral ADMM method and cannot be validated without a source. The assumption also contains corrupted LaTeX in the upper-bound symbol.

children.title: Curvature-Informed Penalty Selection
children.top_down_role: Penalty choices informed by local curvature behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Informed Penalty Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty selection from positive local curvature estimates on both ADMM blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric local Hessian or model matrices \(H_x^k\) and \(H_z^k\), choose nonzero directions \(d_x^k\) and \(d_z^k\) and form Rayleigh estimates \[\kappa_x^k=\frac{\langle d_x^k,H_x^kd_x^k\rangle}{\lVert d_x^k\rVert_2^2},\qquad \kappa_z^k=\frac{\langle d_z^k,H_z^kd_z^k\rangle}{\lVert d_z^k\rVert_2^2}.\] If both estimates are positive, propose \(\widehat\rho_{k+1}=\sqrt{\kappa_x^k\kappa_z^k}\) and clip it to \([\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\). Otherwise reject the proposal and keep \(\rho_{k+1}=\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate curvature in each block, use their geometric mean as the penalty, and reject nonpositive or invalid estimates.
assumptions_latex: \(H_x^k\) and \(H_z^k\) are symmetric local models.
\(d_x^k\ne0,\ d_z^k\ne0\)
\(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted penalty satisfies \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\).
review_flags: The intended curvature model and penalty-optimality criterion are not fixed by the supplied locator hints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed geometric mean of block Rayleigh curvatures is a specific heuristic, not a generally determined ADMM rule. Its intended model and justification require an authoritative source.

children.title: Hybrid Local-Geometry Penalties
children.top_down_role: Penalty families combining multiple local geometric signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Local-Geometry Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded interpolation of residual-based and local-geometry penalty proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho_{R,k}>0\) be a residual-balancing proposal and \(\rho_{G,k}>0\) an accepted spectral or curvature proposal. For a trust weight \(\theta_k\in[0,1]\), define the log-scale hybrid proposal \[\widehat\rho_{k+1}=\exp\bigl((1-\theta_k)\log\rho_{R,k}+\theta_k\log\rho_{G,k}\bigr).\] Output \(\rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{\max},\max\{\rho_{\min},\widehat\rho_{k+1}\}\}\). If the geometry proposal fails its positivity or reliability test, set \(\theta_k=0\); if both proposals are admissible, \(\theta_k\) may increase with the geometry estimate's reliability score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend residual and geometry proposals multiplicatively, reduce geometry weight when unreliable, and clip the resulting penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_{R,k}>0\) and every used \(\rho_{G,k}>0\)
\(\theta_k\in[0,1]\)
\(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\), and an rejected geometry estimate has no influence.

notation.meaning: Reliability weight assigned to local geometry.

review_flags: The hybrid interpolation and reliability rule require a specific adaptive-penalty source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logarithmic interpolation is mathematically well-defined, but neither it nor the unspecified reliability weighting is established by supplied evidence.

children.title: Geometry-Estimate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where noisy or unstable local geometry weakens penalty selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Estimate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidity and rejection conditions for geometric-mean secant or curvature penalty proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be local geometry estimates, let \(\Gamma\ge 1\) be a prescribed anisotropy limit, and define \(\widehat\rho=\sqrt{\alpha\beta}\). The proposal is admissible only if \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are finite and strictly positive and \(\max\{\alpha/\beta,\beta/\alpha\}\le\Gamma\). A zero secant denominator, a nonpositive or nonfinite estimate, or violation of the anisotropy limit requires rejection of the proposal. An admissible proposal may be projected onto prescribed bounds \([\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\), where \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\), before the next ADMM update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject geometry-based penalty proposals with zero denominators, nonpositive or nonfinite estimates, or anisotropy exceeding a prescribed limit; admissible proposals may then be clipped to positive finite bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat\rho=\sqrt{\alpha\beta}\) is the candidate geometry rule.
\(\Gamma\ge1\) is a prescribed anisotropy limit.
\(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A proposal is used only when \(0<\alpha,\beta<\infty\) and \(\max\{\alpha/\beta,\beta/\alpha\}\le\Gamma\), after optional projection onto \([\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algebraic domain restrictions for a geometric-mean proposal
An authoritative adaptive-ADMM source is still required for the controller-specific anisotropy and clipping safeguards.

children.title: Adaptive-Penalty Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Stability and convergence restrictions associated with changing penalty parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Penalty Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundedness, controlled variation, and multiplier consistency for changing ADMM penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive scalar penalty sequence is safeguarded when \[0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_k\le\rho_{\max}<\infty\quad\text{for every }k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\left|\frac{\rho_{k+1}}{\rho_k}-1\right|<\infty.\] Whenever the scaled multiplier is \(u^k=y^k/\rho_k\), a penalty-only change must use \(u^k\leftarrow(\rho_k/\rho_{k+1})u^k\), so the unscaled multiplier \(y^k\) is preserved. A controller may enforce the variation condition through finitely many updates, summable update magnitudes, or eventual freezing of \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep penalties positive and bounded, control their cumulative relative variation, and rescale the scaled multiplier whenever the penalty changes.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_k>0\) for every \(k\)
\(u^k=y^k/\rho_k\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty sequence remains nondegenerate and penalty changes do not alter the represented unscaled multiplier.
review_flags: A convergence theorem tying this safeguard to a specific variable-penalty ADMM variant is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positivity, boundedness, and multiplier consistency are appropriate safeguards, but summable relative penalty variation is variant-specific and requires a source identifying the ADMM convergence setting it supports.

children.title: Coordinator-Based Architectures
children.top_down_role: Central consensus, server-worker, and parameter-server organizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinator-Based Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous server-worker realization of consensus ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent \(\min_x\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x)\) as \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\sum_i f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\). With penalty \(\rho>0\), worker \(i\) computes \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left(f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_i-z^k+u_i^k\rVert_2^2\right).\] The coordinator receives the worker states and sets \(z^{k+1}=m^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k)\); each worker then sets \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\). Thus only the coordinator performs the global aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve local proximal subproblems, a coordinator averages their shifted states, and workers update local multipliers against the shared consensus variable.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Communication is synchronous and reliable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture realizes consensus ADMM for \(\min_x\sum_i f_i(x)\).

notation.meaning: Worker-local copy of the decision vector.

children.title: Decentralized Graph Architectures
children.top_down_role: Peer-to-peer coordination using local graph communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Decentralized Graph Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peer-to-peer consensus representation over a connected communication graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph, let each vertex \(i\) hold \(f_i\), and stack local decisions as \(X=(x_i)_{i\in V}\). For an oriented incidence matrix \(D\), decentralized consensus is represented by \[(D\otimes I_d)X=0.\] Connectivity implies that this constraint holds exactly when \(x_i=x_j\) for all vertices. Splitting the edge constraints assigns each update only local objectives, incident-edge multipliers, and neighbor messages; no vertex requires a globally maintained consensus variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph incidence constraints encode global consensus on a connected network while allowing every node to update using only local data and neighbor messages.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is connected and undirected.
\(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\) for every \(i\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D\otimes I_d)X=0\) if and only if \(x_i=x_j\) for all \(i,j\in V\).

children.title: Data-Partitioned Architectures
children.top_down_role: Distributed organizations based on observations, samples, or data shards.

knowledge_statements.title: Data-Partitioned Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-partitioned empirical objectives realized through local consensus subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(N\) observations into disjoint sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_m\) and define \[F(x)=R(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x),\qquad f_i(x)=\sum_{j\in I_i}\ell_j(x).\] Introduce worker copies \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) and a shared variable \(z\). Then minimizing \(F\) is equivalent to \[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\;R(z)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for every }i.\] Worker \(i\) stores and evaluates only observations indexed by \(I_i\); coordination occurs through the consensus variables and the shared regularizer \(R(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition observations among workers, express the loss as a sum of worker-local objectives, and couple local model copies to a shared variable on which the common regularizer is evaluated.
assumptions_latex: \(I_i\cap I_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\) and \(\bigcup_{i=1}^{m}I_i=\{1,\ldots,N\}\).
Each \(f_i\) and \(R\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing \(F(x)=R(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x)\) is equivalent to minimizing \(R(z)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: Observation indices stored by worker i.
Worker-local decision copy and shared consensus variable.
Regularizer evaluated on the shared consensus variable.

children.title: Feature-Partitioned Architectures
children.top_down_role: Distributed organizations based on variables, coordinates, or feature groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Partitioned Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-partitioned convex models represented through local predictors and a global aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\geq 1\), let \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and let \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,p\). With \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_p]\) and \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\), consider
\[\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_p}\;\ell\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^p A_i x_i\right)+\sum_{i=1}^p r_i(x_i).\]
Introducing \(z_i\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) gives the equivalent constrained representation
\[\min_{x_1,ldots,x_p,z_1,ldots,z_p,z}\;\ell(z)+\sum_{i=1}^p r_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z_i=A_i x_i\ \text{for all }i,\qquad z=\sum_{i=1}^p z_i.\]
Thus local feature blocks produce local prediction vectors, while coordination acts on their aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Features and variables are partitioned by columns. Each worker forms a local prediction, and the constrained formulation coordinates the sum of those predictions through a shared aggregate vector.
assumptions_latex: \(p\geq1\), \(A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n_i}\), and \(x_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\).
\(\ell:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(r_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original objective is equivalent to minimizing \(\ell(z)+\sum_{i=1}^p r_i(x_i)\) subject to \(z_i=A_i x_i\) and \(z=sum_{i=1}^p z_i\).

notation.meaning: Feature block stored by worker i.
Local prediction contributed by worker i.

children.title: Hybrid Partition Layouts
children.top_down_role: Execution layouts combining observation-based partitions with variable-based partitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Partition Layouts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-dimensional row-and-column partitioning of a convex linear-prediction model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) into blocks \(A_{ij}\), with row groups \(i=1,\ldots,q\) and feature groups \(j=1,\ldots,p\), and write \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\). For
\[\min_x\;\sum_{i=1}^q \ell_i((Ax)_i)+\sum_{j=1}^p r_j(x_j),\]
define \(z_{ij}=A_{ij}x_j\) and \(z_i=\sum_{j=1}^p z_{ij}\). The resulting constraints separate computations over matrix blocks while requiring reductions across feature groups for each row group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid layout partitions both samples and features, computes blockwise predictions, and reduces feature contributions within each sample group.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\) and \(r_j\) are proper, closed, and convex.
The blocks \(A_{ij}\) form a disjoint two-dimensional partition of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Ax)_i=\sum_{j=1}^p A_{ij}x_j=\sum_{j=1}^p z_{ij}\) for every row group \(i\).

notation.meaning: Matrix block for row group i and feature group j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-dimensional block representation is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports its characterization as a hybrid ADMM partition architecture.

children.title: Partition-Balance Constraints
children.top_down_role: Workload, storage, plus coupling effects induced by partition granularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Balance Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A load-balance predicate for heterogeneous ADMM partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c_i>0\) be the estimated work assigned to partition \(i\), and let \(s_i>0\) be its processing rate. For imbalance tolerance \(\beta\geq 1\), the partition is \(\beta\)-balanced when
\[\max_{1\leq i\leq p}\frac{c_i}{s_i}\leq \beta\,\frac{\sum_{i=1}^p c_i}{\sum_{i=1}^p s_i}.\]
For identical processing rates this reduces to bounding the largest partition cost by \(\beta\) times the mean partition cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition is balanced when its slowest normalized workload is at most a prescribed multiple of the system-wide average normalized workload.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is the partition-balance constraint.

notation.meaning: Estimated computational work of partition i.
Processing rate assigned to partition i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed inequality is a possible heterogeneous-load predicate, not a canonical balance constraint without a stated scheduling model. Moreover, the ratio of total work to total processing rate is not generally the average of the individual normalized workloads, as the plain statement suggests.

children.title: Shared-Memory Realizations
children.top_down_role: Multicore realizations using common address spaces for block coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Memory Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous consensus ADMM using parallel workers and shared arrays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x_i,z}\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)+g(z)\) subject to \(x_i=z\), initialize shared \(z^0\) and local \(u_i^0\). At iteration \(k\), parallel workers compute
\[x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f_i/\rho}(z^k-u_i^k).\]
After a barrier, a shared reduction forms \(\bar x^{k+1}=p^{-1}\sum_i x_i^{k+1}\) and \(\bar u^k=p^{-1}\sum_i u_i^k\), then sets \(z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/(p\rho)}(\bar x^{k+1}+\bar u^k)\). Workers update \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\) and stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers execute local proximal updates in parallel, reduce through shared memory, update the consensus variable, and synchronize before the next iteration.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\), and shared reductions are race-free.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The updates realize synchronous consensus ADMM in a shared-memory execution model.

children.title: Message-Passing Realizations
children.top_down_role: Cluster realizations using explicit interprocess communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Message-Passing Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous consensus ADMM with private process memory and collective communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x_i,z}\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)+g(z)\) subject to \(x_i=z\), process \(i\) stores \(x_i^k,u_i^k\) and a replica of \(z^k\). It computes \(x_i^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{f_i/\rho}(z^k-u_i^k)\), then an all-reduce obtains \(\bar x^{k+1}=p^{-1}\sum_i x_i^{k+1}\) and \(\bar u^k=p^{-1}\sum_i u_i^k\). Every process evaluates \(z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/(p\rho)}(\bar x^{k+1}+\bar u^k)\), updates \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\), and terminates after a collective residual test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each process keeps private local state and uses collective reductions to reproduce the global consensus and stopping computations.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f_i\) and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\rho>0\), and collectives return exact mathematical sums.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The collective reductions realize the coordination step without shared writable memory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The collective implementation is mathematically consistent with synchronous consensus ADMM and fits the algorithm container, but it has no cited source or locator supporting the message-passing realization.

children.title: Hybrid-Memory Realizations
children.top_down_role: Multilevel realizations combining node-local memory sharing with network messaging.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid-Memory Realizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hierarchical consensus ADMM across shared-memory process groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition workers into process groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_q\). Each group computes its local proximal updates in shared memory and forms \(S_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}x_i^{k+1}\) and \(T_g=\sum_{i\in G_g}u_i^k\). One representative per group performs message-passing all-reductions of \(S_g\) and \(T_g\). The resulting global averages determine the replicated update \(z^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/(p\rho)}(p^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k))\); each group broadcasts \(z^{k+1}\) locally, updates its dual variables, and applies a hierarchical residual test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers reduce locally within shared-memory groups, representatives reduce across groups, and the consensus result is broadcast down the hierarchy.
assumptions_latex: The groups \(G_g\) form a disjoint partition of \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\).
All local and intergroup reductions compute the required sums consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two-level reductions equal \(\sum_{g=1}^q\sum_{i\in G_g}(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k)=\sum_{i=1}^p(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k)\).

notation.meaning: Group sum of scaled dual iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hierarchical reduction identity is plausible, but the record does not introduce the underlying consensus problem, the function g, the penalty parameter, or the local proximal updates. An authoritative hybrid-memory ADMM source is also absent.

children.title: Execution-Model Portability
children.top_down_role: Transfer of decomposition layouts across multicore, multinode, plus heterogeneous systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution-Model Portability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration equivalence across shared, distributed, and hierarchical reduction implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{X}\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and consider two deterministic implementations \(A\) and \(B\) of the same synchronous consensus-ADMM update graph, with \(x_i^k,z^k,u_i^k\in\mathcal{X}\). If the implementations start from identical states, use the same penalty \(\rho>0\), evaluate identical local proximal maps, and return identical reduction values before every dependent update, then
\[(x_A^k,z_A^k,u_A^k)=(x_B^k,z_B^k,u_B^k)\quad\text{for every iteration }k\text{ executed by both implementations}.\]
Hence the mathematical iteration is portable across execution models under identical update semantics. Finite-precision reassociation, asynchronous reads, or different stopping reductions need not preserve bitwise equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared-memory, message-passing, and hierarchical implementations produce the same mathematical iterates when they use identical initialization, local operators, reduction values, update ordering, and stopping semantics.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{X}\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space and both realizations execute the same deterministic synchronous update graph.
Corresponding initial states, penalty parameters, local maps, reduction results, and stopping rules are identical.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_A^k,z_A^k,u_A^k)=(x_B^k,z_B^k,u_B^k)\) for every iteration \(k\) executed by both realizations.

children.title: Local Proximal Work
children.top_down_role: Per-participant cost attributable to proximal subproblem computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Proximal Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-iteration work for independent local proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose one ADMM iteration evaluates local maps \(x_i^+=\operatorname{prox}_{f_i/\rho}(v_i)\), and evaluation on partition \(i\) costs \(T_i\) arithmetic operations. The aggregate local work is
\[W_{\mathrm{prox}}=\sum_{i=1}^p T_i.\]
With one concurrently executing worker per partition and no resource contention, the local-computation span is \(S_{\mathrm{prox}}=\max_i T_i\). Coordination, communication, and barrier time are excluded from both quantities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local proximal work sums across partitions, while ideal parallel elapsed work is governed by the most expensive partition.
assumptions_latex: Partition \(i\)'s proximal evaluation costs \(T_i\geq0\).
Local evaluations are independent within the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{prox}}=\sum_iT_i\) and, under ideal concurrency, \(S_{\mathrm{prox}}=\max_iT_i\).

notation.meaning: Arithmetic cost of partition i's proximal map.

children.title: Factorization Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense direct-solve cost for a local symmetric positive-definite system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a local ADMM subproblem require solving \(H_i x=b_i^k\), where \(H_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}\) is dense, symmetric, positive definite, and constant during the solve. Computing a Cholesky factorization \(H_i=L_iL_i^{\mathsf T}\) requires \(n_i^3/3+O(n_i^2)\) floating-point operations and \(O(n_i^2)\) storage. Given \(L_i\), the two triangular solves for one right-hand side require \(2n_i^2+O(n_i)\) floating-point operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense local Cholesky factorization costs cubic work and quadratic storage; each subsequent solve costs quadratic work.
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\) is dense, symmetric, positive definite, and of order \(n_i\).
The complexity model counts scalar floating-point operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization cost is \(n_i^3/3+O(n_i^2)\), storage is \(O(n_i^2)\), and each factored solve costs \(2n_i^2+O(n_i)\).

children.title: Iterative Local-Solve Complexity
children.top_down_role: Per-iteration effort arising from approximate local linear-system solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Local-Solve Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate-gradient complexity for an inexact local positive-definite solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(b_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), and let \(x_*=H_i^{-1}b_i\). Define \(\kappa_i=\lambda_{\max}(H_i)/\lambda_{\min}(H_i)>1\) and \(\lVert v\rVert_{H_i}=\sqrt{v^{\mathsf T}H_i v}\). Starting conjugate gradients from \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\), the condition
\[t\geq\left\lceil\frac{\log(2/\varepsilon)}{\log((\sqrt{\kappa_i}+1)/(\sqrt{\kappa_i}-1))}\right\rceil\]
is sufficient for \(\lVert x_t-x_*\rVert_{H_i}\leq\varepsilon\lVert x_0-x_*\rVert_{H_i}\), where \(0<\varepsilon<1\). Consequently, the required iteration count is \(O(\sqrt{\kappa_i}\log(1/\varepsilon))\), and the arithmetic cost is that count times the cost of one multiplication by \(H_i\), plus vector operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric positive-definite local system, conjugate gradients requires on the order of the square root of the condition number times the logarithm of inverse relative energy-norm accuracy in matrix-vector products.
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i\times n_i}\) is symmetric positive definite with \(\kappa_i>1\).
\(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sufficient iteration count is \(O(\sqrt{\kappa_i}\log(1/\varepsilon))\).

notation.meaning: Exact solution of the local linear system.
Spectral condition number of the local system matrix.
Energy norm induced by the local system matrix.

children.title: Linear-Algebra Reuse Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Algebra Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Amortization when local system matrices remain fixed across ADMM iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose partition \(i\) solves \(H_i x_i^{k+1}=b_i^k\) for \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\), where \(H_i\) is unchanged because the local model, penalty \(\rho\), and active linear constraints are fixed. If factorization costs \(F_i\) and each factored solve costs \(S_i\), then reuse gives total cost
\[F_i+KS_i\]
instead of \(K(F_i+S_i)\). If \(H_i\) changes, this exact reuse guarantee does not apply, although structured updates or preconditioner reuse may remain possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed local system matrix is factored once and reused, reducing repeated-solve cost from repeated factorizations to one factorization plus solves.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient matrix \(H_i\) is identical in all \(K\) local solves.
The stored factorization remains available and numerically acceptable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact factor reuse changes the modeled cost from \(K(F_i+S_i)\) to \(F_i+KS_i\).

notation.meaning: Cost of one solve using stored factors.

children.title: Message-Volume Complexity
children.top_down_role: Communication cost measured through transferred data volume.

knowledge_statements.title: Message-Volume Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication cost of a tree-based dense-vector all-reduce.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\) processes perform a synchronous all-reduce of a dense vector containing \(d\) scalar words by a balanced reduce tree followed by a broadcast tree. Along the critical path, the operation uses \(2\lceil\log_2 p\rceil\) messages and transmits \(2d\lceil\log_2 p\rceil\) words. Over all network links, it transmits \(2d(p-1)\) words. Under the \(\alpha\)-\(\beta\) model, the critical-path communication time is bounded by
\[2\lceil\log_2p\rceil(\alpha+\beta d),\]
excluding contention and local reduction work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced tree all-reduce has logarithmic message depth, logarithmic critical-path word volume, and linear total network word volume.
assumptions_latex: Messages carry \(d\) scalar words without segmentation or compression.
The collective uses balanced reduction and broadcast trees.
The \(\alpha\)-\(\beta\) model excludes contention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Critical-path volume is \(2d\lceil\log_2p\rceil\) words and total network volume is \(2d(p-1)\) words.

notation.meaning: Number of scalar words in the reduced vector.
Per-message latency and per-word transfer cost.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounds are plausible for the specified reduce-tree-plus-broadcast implementation, but they are collective-algorithm-specific and uncited. A source should also clarify whether the stated critical-path message count is exact for all process counts or an upper bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R^k\geq 0\) be the prescribed primal-dual residual after synchronous ADMM round \(k\), let \(\varepsilon\geq 0\), and define \(K_\varepsilon=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:R^k\leq\varepsilon\}\). Assume \(K_\varepsilon<\infty\) and that exactly one global barrier completes each round. Then the synchronization count before termination is \(S_\varepsilon=K_\varepsilon\). If the barrier completing round \(k\) has duration \(b_k\geq 0\), the cumulative synchronization time is \[C_{\mathrm{sync}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K_\varepsilon-1}b_k.\] Thus the stopping index determines the barrier count but does not determine elapsed synchronization time without timing information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When synchronous ADMM terminates after a finite number of rounds and every round ends with one global barrier, the barrier count equals the stopping-round index. Elapsed synchronization time is the sum of the individual barrier durations.

children.title: Network-Latency Costs
children.top_down_role: Execution sensitivity to message startup time plus network delay.

assumptions_latex: The execution has \(K\in\mathbb N_0\) sequential coordination rounds.
For each round \(k\), communication dependencies form a finite directed acyclic graph \(G_k\).
Independent transmissions may overlap without resource contention, and every transmission starts as soon as its predecessors finish.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The latency-only makespan of round \(k\) is \(L_k=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(G_k)}\sum_{e\in P}\ell_e\), and the total over \(K\) sequential rounds is \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}L_k\).

nonnegative duration assigned to transmission edge e
set of directed paths in the dependency graph

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\in\mathbb N_0\). For each synchronous distributed ADMM round \(k\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}\), let \(G_k=(V_k,E_k)\) be a finite directed acyclic graph whose edges represent message transmissions and whose directed paths encode transmission dependencies. Assign a duration \(\ell_e\geq0\) to every \(e\in E_k\), and let \(\mathcal P(G_k)\) denote the set of directed paths in \(G_k\). If independent transmissions overlap without resource contention and every transmission starts when its predecessors finish, the latency-only makespan is \[L_k=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(G_k)}\sum_{e\in P}\ell_e.\] Because the coordination rounds are sequential, their latency-only makespans add: \[C_{\mathrm{lat}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}L_k.\] Summing all edge durations generally exceeds this ideal-overlap makespan because independent transmissions may execute concurrently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an ideal execution model with unlimited overlap, no resource contention, and immediate scheduling, a round's network makespan is its longest weighted dependency path. The latency-only makespans add across sequential coordination rounds.

children.title: Barrier-Waiting Costs
children.top_down_role: Idle-time costs caused by collective coordination points plus participant imbalance.

assumptions_latex: The number of workers satisfies \(m\in\mathbb N\).
All workers start each synchronous round at a common time origin and enter one barrier after completing their work.
The execution contains \(K\in\mathbb N_0\) rounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For round \(k\), \(T_k=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}t_{ik}\), \(W_k=\sum_{i=1}^{m}(T_k-t_{ik})\), and the maximum individual waiting time is \(B_k=T_k-\min_{1\leq i\leq m}t_{ik}\).

notation.meaning: barrier-arrival time of worker i in round k, measured from the common round start
barrier release time in round k
aggregate worker waiting time in round k
maximum individual barrier-waiting time in round k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates aggregate idle worker-time from the maximum individual barrier wait caused by completion-time imbalance.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.2 Asynchronous Algorithms and the Reduction of the Synchronization Penalty p. 95
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) workers start synchronous round \(k\) at a common time origin, and let worker \(i\) reach the barrier at time \(t_{ik}\geq0\). The barrier releases at \(T_k=\max_{1\leq i\leq m}t_{ik}\). Worker \(i\) waits \(T_k-t_{ik}\), so the aggregate idle worker-time is \[W_k=\sum_{i=1}^{m}(T_k-t_{ik}).\] The maximum individual waiting time is \[B_k=T_k-\min_{1\leq i\leq m}t_{ik}.\] For \(K\in\mathbb N_0\) rounds, aggregate waiting is \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}W_k\). It is zero exactly when every worker has the same barrier-arrival time in every round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous barrier releases when the slowest worker arrives. Aggregate waiting sums every worker's idle time, while the slowest-minus-fastest arrival time is the maximum individual barrier wait, not the round's full critical-path duration.
knowledge_statements.title: Barrier-Waiting Costs

children.title: ADMM Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Known boundaries where convergence, certification, or computational advantage may fail.

children.title: Naive Multi-Block Divergence
children.top_down_role: Failure of unrestricted direct extensions beyond protected two-block structures.

assumptions_latex: At least three primal blocks are updated sequentially by direct Gauss-Seidel ADMM.
Objectives are allowed to be closed proper convex functions without additional strong-convexity or rank safeguards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct multi-block ADMM has no universal convergence guarantee; admissible convex instances exist for which its iterate sequence diverges.

notation.meaning: linear constraint operator for block i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Gauss-Seidel extension to three or more convex blocks without protective assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^{p}f_i(x_i):\sum_{i=1}^{p}A_ix_i=b\}\) with \(p\geq3\), closed proper convex \(f_i\), and a nonempty solution set. The naive extension of two-block ADMM minimizes the augmented Lagrangian successively in \(x_1,\ldots,x_p\) and then performs one multiplier update with fixed \(\rho>0\). Under only these assumptions, convergence is not guaranteed: there exist finite-dimensional convex quadratic instances with a consistent linear constraint for which the resulting primal-dual iteration matrix has spectral radius greater than one, so some initializations produce unbounded or nonconvergent iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequentially extending two-block ADMM to three or more convex blocks can diverge unless additional structure, proximal regularization, or another convergence safeguard is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Naive Multi-Block Divergence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and mathematical claim are appropriate, but the existence of a convex quadratic multi-block ADMM instance with iteration-matrix spectral radius greater than one is a nontrivial literature claim. An exact theorem or counterexample locator is required before its hypotheses and conclusion can be trusted at candidate-review level.

children.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Limitations
children.top_down_role: Stationary outcomes without global optimality or desirable local structure.

assumptions_latex: A nonconvex method returns only a first-order stationary point.
No convexity, second-order condition, or global certificate is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order stationarity does not imply local minimality or global optimality.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed polynomial directly separates stationarity from local and global minimality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete unconstrained counterexample to interpreting an ADMM stationary limit as an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the smooth nonconvex problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}f(x)\) with \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\), the point \(x^\star=0\) satisfies the first-order stationarity condition \(f'(x^\star)=0\). Nevertheless, \(f(0)=1\), while \(f(1)=f(-1)=0\), and \(f''(0)=-4<0\); hence \(x^\star\) is a strict local maximizer rather than a local or global minimizer. Consequently, a nonconvex ADMM theorem concluding only that every accumulation point is stationary cannot, without additional assumptions, guarantee global optimality or even desirable local structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polynomial objective has a stationary point at zero that is a strict local maximum, showing that nonconvex stationarity alone guarantees neither local nor global optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Stationarity Limitations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The polynomial calculation is correct and the counterexample kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no inspectable citation. Standard-field rationale may support candidate construction, yet this statement-review layer requires a source locator for acceptance.

children.title: Scaling-Penalty Failure Coupling
children.top_down_role: Slow progress or instability caused by imbalanced block geometry.

children.title: Block-Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Slow or unstable progress associated with imbalanced block magnitudes or geometry.

assumptions_latex: The variables satisfy \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), and the residual lies in \(\mathbb R^m\).
The matrix \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular and the penalty satisfies \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(r=0\) by \(Dr=0\) changes the scalar quadratic penalty metric from \(\rho I_m\) to \(\rho D^{\mathsf T}D\); an ill-conditioned \(D^{\mathsf T}D\) assigns highly unequal weights to residual directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic effect of nonsingular row scaling on the augmented residual metric.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z\in\mathbb R^p\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(r=Ax+Bz-c\). Replace the constraint \(r=0\) by \(Dr=0\), where \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular. For \(\rho>0\), the quadratic augmentation becomes \[\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Dr\rVert_2^2=\frac12r^{\mathsf T}(\rho D^{\mathsf T}D)r.\] Thus the scaling preserves the feasible set but changes the scalar penalty metric from \(\rho I_m\) to \(\rho D^{\mathsf T}D\). If \(D^{\mathsf T}D\) is ill-conditioned, the augmentation weights residual directions very unequally and may consequently worsen conditioning or produce strongly direction-dependent progress. Equivalence of the resulting ADMM iterates requires corresponding transformations of the penalty metric and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonsingular row scaling preserves the feasible set but changes scalar-penalty ADMM into a weighted-penalty formulation. Ill-conditioned scaling weights residual directions very unequally and may degrade numerical behavior.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Scaling Pathologies

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Penalty-Sensitivity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Performance regimes dominated by narrow or unstable penalty choices.

assumptions_latex: Standard two-block scaled ADMM is applied exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linear contraction factor is \(q(\rho)=(\rho^2+ab)/((a+\rho)(b+\rho))\), minimized at \(\rho=\sqrt{ab}\), and tends to one at both penalty extremes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct elimination of the displayed scalar ADMM updates yields the stated eigenvalue
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar quadratic model exhibiting slow convergence for very small or very large penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x,z\in\mathbb R}\frac a2x^2+\frac b2z^2\) subject to \(x-z=0\), where \(a,b>0\). Exact scaled ADMM with penalty \(\rho>0\) is a linear iteration whose only nonzero eigenvalue is \[q(\rho)=\frac{\rho^2+ab}{(a+\rho)(b+\rho)}.\] Hence the asymptotic contraction factor satisfies \(0<q(\rho)<1\), is minimized at \(\rho=\sqrt{ab}\), and obeys \(q(\rho)\to1\) as either \(\rho\downarrow0\) or \(\rho\to\infty\). Convergence therefore remains valid here but becomes arbitrarily slow in both extreme-penalty regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a scalar quadratic consensus problem, ADMM's exact contraction factor approaches one for penalties near zero or infinity and is best at the geometric mean of the curvatures.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalty-Sensitivity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar quadratic factor, its minimizer, and its limiting behavior are mathematically consistent, and property is the correct content kind. However, the exact eigenvalue formula is unsupported by an inspectable source, so the record requires a specific derivation or theorem locator.

children.title: Scaling-Penalty Interactions
children.top_down_role: Coupled effects of block normalization plus penalty selection.

assumptions_latex: An equality constraint is multiplied by a nonzero scalar \(\alpha\).
The scaled formulation uses scalar penalty \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal augmented term depends on \(\rho\alpha^2\); preserving it requires \(\rho'=\rho/\alpha^2\) after scaling by \(\alpha\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality follows immediately from the displayed augmented term
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar constraint scaling and the compensating transformation of the ADMM penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x,z)=Ax+Bz-c\). Replacing \(r(x,z)=0\) by the equivalent constraint \(\alpha r(x,z)=0\), with \(\alpha\neq0\), changes the quadratic augmentation from \(\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r\rVert_2^2\) to \[\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert\alpha r\rVert_2^2=\frac{\rho\alpha^2}{2}\lVert r\rVert_2^2.\] Thus the effective primal penalty is \(\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}=\rho\alpha^2\). To preserve the original augmented term after scaling the constraint by \(\alpha\), one must use \(\rho'=\rho/\alpha^2\) and transform the scaled dual variable consistently. Holding \(\rho\) fixed confounds physical scaling with algorithmic tuning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying a constraint by alpha multiplies ADMM's effective penalty by alpha squared. Dividing the penalty by alpha squared preserves the original augmented residual weighting.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Penalty Interactions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primal augmented-term scaling by alpha squared is correct. The additional claim about preserving the ADMM formulation depends on the convention for scaled or unscaled dual variables, which is not specified or sourced. A citation and an explicit dual-variable transformation are required.

children.title: Preconditioning Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where available rescaling or preconditioning does not restore balanced progress.

assumptions_latex: A weighted augmentation \(\frac12\lVert r\rVert_P^2\) is used.
The weight \(P\) may be singular on attainable residual directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive definiteness on the residual range is a boundary for residual control; without it, infeasibility can be invisible to the augmentation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed one-dimensional instance directly exhibits loss of residual control
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by a penalty metric that is singular on feasible-residual directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a preconditioned ADMM augmentation uses \(\frac12\lVert r\rVert_P^2=\frac12r^{\mathsf T}Pr\) with \(P\succeq0\). Residual control requires \(r^{\mathsf T}Pr>0\) for every nonzero attainable residual \(r\). If some nonzero attainable \(v\) satisfies \(Pv=0\), the augmentation cannot distinguish residuals differing along \(v\). In the scalar problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}0\) subject to \(x=0\), choosing \(P=0\) makes every \(x\) minimize the augmented primal subproblem, including infeasible values. Hence semidefinite preconditioning without positivity on the residual range can destroy uniqueness and residual convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty metric singular along an attainable residual direction cannot detect infeasibility there. Even the constraint x equals zero becomes uncontrolled when the metric is zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioning Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A singular metric indeed fails to penalize nullspace residual directions, but the scalar example specifies only an augmented primal subproblem and not a complete preconditioned ADMM iteration or dual update. Nonuniqueness of that subproblem alone does not establish failure of residual convergence for every implementation. A sourced, fully specified algorithm and failure result are needed.

children.title: Uncontrolled Inexactness
children.top_down_role: Loss of convergence when local solution errors are insufficiently controlled.

assumptions_latex: An exact fixed-point step is contractive with factor \(q\in(0,1)\).
Every step contains an uncontrolled additive error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A persistent nonsummable error can shift the limit away from the exact fixed point, so vanishing residuals are not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent-error counterexample for inexact fixed-point realizations of splitting iterations.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact splitting iteration on \(\mathbb R\) be \(x^{k+1}=qx^k\), where \(0<q<1\), so its unique fixed point is \(0\). If each local solve introduces the same nonzero error \(e\), the realized iteration becomes \(x^{k+1}=qx^k+e\). It converges to \(e/(1-q)\neq0\), and the error sequence satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|e|=\infty\). Thus contractivity of the exact ADMM or splitting map does not ensure convergence to its solution under uncontrolled inexactness; standard guarantees require quantitative error control such as summability or a suitable relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent local-solve error can move an otherwise contractive splitting iteration to the wrong limit. Exact-method convergence therefore does not survive arbitrary inexact updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Inexactness

children.title: Asynchrony-Participation Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Breakdown outside supported asynchronous or randomized execution models.

children.title: Delay Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns caused by unsupported communication or computation delays.

assumptions_latex: A worker applies a one-step-delayed gradient update.
The synchronous step size is stable for the underlying scalar quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Delay can turn a stable synchronous iteration into a divergent recurrence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar delayed-update example isolating instability caused by one iteration of delay.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.2 Asynchronous Algorithms and the Reduction of the Synchronization Penalty p. 95
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\frac12x^2\), synchronous gradient iteration is \(x^{k+1}=(1-\gamma)x^k\), which converges to \(0\) whenever \(0<\gamma<2\). With one-step-delayed information, the update is \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\gamma x^{k-1}\), whose characteristic equation is \(r^2-r+\gamma=0\). Taking \(\gamma=3/2\), the synchronous factor is \(-1/2\), but the delayed roots are complex with modulus \(\sqrt{3/2}>1\). Except for exceptional initial conditions, the delayed iterates therefore diverge. Delay bounds and delay-dependent step restrictions are essential in asynchronous coordination guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step size that contracts a synchronous scalar quadratic iteration can diverge with only one iteration of delay, demonstrating the need for delay-dependent parameter bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Delay Failures

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4.2 Asynchronous Algorithms and the Reduction of the Synchronization Penalty p. 95
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The delayed-gradient recurrence and root calculation are correct, and counterexample is the right role for that recurrence. However, it is a gradient-descent example rather than an ADMM or ADMM fixed-point iteration, so it does not establish the claimed failure phenomenon in this ADMM failure-regime container. The generic asynchronous-computation citation does not repair that mismatch.

children.title: Staleness Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns caused by obsolete local states or coordination information.

assumptions_latex: The exact update map is the contraction \(T(x)=x/2\).
A worker may repeatedly use an indefinitely stale initial read.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a finite-staleness or fresh-information condition, repeated stale writes need not approach the fixed point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indefinitely stale-read counterexample, distinct from instability under a fixed finite delay.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.2 Asynchronous Algorithms and the Reduction of the Synchronization Penalty p. 95
source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(T(x)=x/2\), whose unique fixed point is \(0\). Suppose \(x^0\neq0\) and an asynchronous worker indefinitely reads the stale value \(x^0\), then overwrites shared memory with \(T(x^0)=x^0/2\) at every event. The recorded sequence satisfies \(x^k=x^0/2\) for all \(k\geq1\), so it never reaches the fixed point despite the contraction of \(T\). Therefore convergence cannot follow from contractivity alone when information age is unbounded; a bounded-staleness or eventual-freshness condition is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a contraction can fail when a worker always reads the initial value: repeated stale writes remain away from the fixed point. Some freshness condition is indispensable.
knowledge_statements.title: Staleness Failures

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4.2 Asynchronous Algorithms and the Reduction of the Synchronization Penalty p. 95
source_witnesses.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indefinitely stale-write example correctly shows that contractivity alone is insufficient under the stated shared-memory schedule. It is nevertheless a generic contraction example with no demonstrated connection to ADMM, so it does not fit the exact ADMM failure-regime path. An ADMM-specific stale-information result or explicitly derived ADMM instance is required.

children.title: Participation Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdowns caused by missing, intermittent, or persistently inactive participants.

knowledge_statements.title: Participation Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A worker omitted forever can make asynchronous consensus ADMM solve a truncated scenario problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider 
\[\min_{x_1,x_2,z}\ \frac12x_1^2+\frac12(x_2-1)^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1=z,\ x_2=z.\]
Its unique solution is \(x_1=x_2=z=\tfrac12\). If worker \(2\) never participates, while worker \(1\) and the coordinator repeatedly apply their scaled-ADMM updates from \(z^0=u_1^0=0\), the participating subsystem remains at \(x_1^k=z^k=u_1^k=0\). Thus its limit is not the solution of the full problem. Any convergence guarantee must therefore impose recurrent participation of every constraint-bearing worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent omission of one scenario can make the active workers converge to the optimizer of a truncated problem rather than the full consensus problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho>0\) is fixed.
Worker \(2\) is never selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_1^k,z^k)\to(0,0)\neq(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)\), so full-problem convergence fails.

notation.meaning: scaled consensus multiplier for worker i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample fits Participation Failures, but the coordinator behavior when worker 2 is omitted is not defined. Whether the coordinator drops that block, retains a stale value, or renormalizes its update changes the iteration. A source and a fully specified asynchronous-consensus ADMM variant are required.

children.title: Combined Asynchrony Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure regions created by interacting delay, staleness, plus participation effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined Asynchrony Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint delay and participation boundary for worker-coordinator ADMM schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For worker \(i\), let \(\tau_i(k)\le k\) be the iteration of the value used at coordinator step \(k\), and let \(p_i(k)\le k\) be its most recent update. A bounded-asynchrony schedule satisfies
\[\sup_{i,k}(k-\tau_i(k))<\infty,\qquad \sup_{i,k}(k-p_i(k))<\infty.\]
The first bound excludes arbitrarily stale reads and the second gives essential cyclic participation. If either supremum is infinite, convex consensus instances and admissible schedules exist for which asynchronous ADMM does not converge to a full-problem solution; boundedness is a boundary condition, not by itself a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded message age and participation gaps delimit the usual asynchronous regime; losing either permits failure, though satisfying both alone does not guarantee convergence.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many workers.
Each coordinator step uses the indexed worker values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If either displayed supremum is infinite, no universal full-problem convergence guarantee follows.

notation.meaning: timestamp of worker i's value used at step k
most recent participation time of worker i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic fit, but the existential failure claim for either unbounded delay or unbounded participation gaps depends on the precise asynchronous ADMM protocol and admissible schedule model. No source fixes those details or supports the stated boundary.

children.title: ADMM Degeneracy Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Degenerate coupling and subproblem structures that weaken convergence or interpretation.

children.title: Rank-Deficiency Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Degenerate coupling structures associated with deficient constraint or operator rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficiency Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular curvature in an ADMM block can destroy uniqueness or existence of its update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an ADMM block update minimizes
\[\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2,\]
where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\rho>0\). Set \(H=Q+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A\) and \(g=c-\rho A^{\mathsf T}b\). Then \(\ker H=\ker Q\cap\ker A\). If \(g\notin\operatorname{range}H\), equivalently if \(g^{\mathsf T}d\ne0\) for some \(d\in\ker H\), the objective is unbounded below along one orientation of \(d\). If \(g\in\operatorname{range}H\), minimizers exist and form \(x_0+\ker H\), where \(Hx_0=-g\); consequently the update is nonunique exactly when \(H\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block update is unbounded when its linear term has a component along a zero-curvature direction; otherwise it is solvable, and it is nonunique precisely when a zero-curvature direction remains.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is unbounded if \(g\notin\operatorname{range}H\); if \(g\in\operatorname{range}H\), its solution set is \(x_0+\ker H\).

notation.meaning: quadratic Hessian of the ADMM block subproblem
effective linear coefficient of the quadratic subproblem
