children.title: Subproblem Solvability Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where local subproblems lack suitable solutions or stable computational resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solvability Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proper convex block objective need not attain its ADMM subproblem infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the convex problem
\[\min_{x,z}\ e^x+\delta_{\{0\}}(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z=0.\]
Written as \(Ax+Bz=c\), it has \(A=0\), \(B=1\), and \(c=0\). For every multiplier and every \(\rho>0\), the ADMM \(x\)-update is
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R} e^x,\]
which is empty because the infimum \(0\) is approached only as \(x\to-\infty\). Hence the ADMM iteration is not well-defined without an attainment or coercivity assumption on each block subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a proper closed convex objective can yield an empty ADMM update when the penalty does not control a nonattaining direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta_{\{0\}}\) denotes the indicator of \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The \(x\)-subproblem has no minimizer, so ADMM cannot perform its first complete iteration.

notation.meaning: zero-set indicator, equal to zero at 0 and infinity elsewhere

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

children.title: Nonunique-Solution Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Interpretive or convergence complications arising from nonunique local or global solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Solution Pathologies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued block updates can preserve residual convergence while preventing iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,x_2)\) and consider
\[\min_{x,z}\ 0+\delta_{\{0\}}(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+z=0.\]
The augmented term is independent of \(x_2\), so every \(x\)-update permits an arbitrary second component. Starting with zero multiplier and \(z^0=0\), select \(x_1^{k+1}=0\) and \(x_2^{k+1}=(-1)^k\). Then the primal and dual residuals are identically zero, but \((x^k,z^k)\) does not converge. Thus residual convergence does not select a solution when block minimizers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary choices among nonunique block minimizers can make ADMM iterates oscillate even while all standard residuals vanish.
assumptions_latex: The block solver may return any exact minimizer.
The multiplier and \(z^0\) are zero.

children.title: Degeneracy Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where rank loss, solvability issues, plus nonuniqueness reinforce one another.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing curvature connects instability, nonuniqueness, and loss of subproblem solvability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\varepsilon\ge0\), consider the block objective
\[q_{\varepsilon,b}(x)=\frac12x_1^2+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}x_2^2-bx_2.\]
For \(\varepsilon>0\), its unique minimizer is \((0,b/\varepsilon)\), whose norm diverges as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\) when \(b\ne0\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), every \((0,t)\) is a minimizer if \(b=0\), whereas no minimizer exists if \(b\ne0\). Thus the same degenerating direction produces ill-conditioning before singularity and either nonuniqueness or nonsolvability at the singular boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As curvature vanishes, unique block solutions become unstable; at singularity the same direction yields either infinitely many minimizers or no minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
\(b\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit \(\varepsilon=0\) separates nonuniqueness at \(b=0\) from nonsolvability at \(b\ne0\).

children.title: Communication-Dominated Execution
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which coordination costs overwhelm decomposed local computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Dominated Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A wall-clock criterion for when coordination overwhelms parallel scenario solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For one nonoverlapped synchronous round with \(P\ge1\) workers, let \(T_i^{\mathrm{comp}}\ge0\) be worker \(i\)'s computation time, \(T^{\mathrm{lat}}\ge0\) the communication latency, \(V^{\mathrm{comm}}\ge0\) the communicated volume, \(B^{\mathrm{eff}}>0\) the effective bandwidth, and \(T^{\mathrm{coord}}\ge0\) the remaining coordination time. Define
\[M=\max_{1\le i\le P}T_i^{\mathrm{comp}},\qquad C=T^{\mathrm{lat}}+\frac{V^{\mathrm{comm}}}{B^{\mathrm{eff}}}+T^{\mathrm{coord}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{iter}}=M+C.\]
Execution is communication dominated when \(C\ge M\). In that regime \(C/T_{\mathrm{iter}}\ge1/2\), and reducing computation from \(M\) to \(M'\ge0\) while holding \(C\) fixed reduces the round time by only \(M-M'\le M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonoverlapped synchronous round is communication dominated when latency, transfer, and coordination time together are at least the slowest worker's computation time; communication then accounts for at least half of the round time.
assumptions_latex: All time components are nonnegative.
Communication and coordination do not overlap local computation.
\(B^{\mathrm{eff}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C\ge M\), then \(C/T_{\mathrm{iter}}\ge1/2\).

notation.meaning: maximum local computation time in the synchronous round
combined latency, transfer, and coordination time

children.title: Nonanticipativity–Consensus Correspondence

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipativity–Consensus Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario nonanticipativity is consensus among decisions sharing the same observed history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with probabilities \(p_s>0\), let \(\mathcal T=\{0,\ldots,T\}\) be the stage set, and let \(x_{t,s}\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\) be the stage-\(t\) decision copy for scenario \(s\). For \(t\in\mathcal T\), write \(s\sim_t s'\) when \(s\) and \(s'\) have identical information histories through stage \(t\). The nonanticipative policy subspace is
\[\mathcal N=\{x:x_{t,s}=x_{t,s'}\ \text{for every}\ t\in\mathcal T\ \text{and all}\ s\sim_t s'\}.\]
For each stage-history class \(h\), introduce \(z_{t,h}\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\). Then \(x\in\mathcal N\) if and only if
\[x_{t,s}=z_{t,[s]_t}\qquad\text{for every}\ t\in\mathcal T\ \text{and}\ s\in S.\]
Thus scenario splitting represents information consistency as structured consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-scenario decisions are nonanticipative exactly when all decision copies sharing a stage history equal one history-indexed consensus variable.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(\mathcal T\) are finite.
\(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
For each \(t\in\mathcal T\), the relation \(\sim_t\) partitions \(S\) into history classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathcal N\) if and only if there exists \(z\) satisfying \(x_{t,s}=z_{t,[s]_t}\) for every \((t,s)\in\mathcal T\times S\).

notation.meaning: scenarios share the same information history through stage t
stage-t history class containing scenario s
consensus decision associated with stage-history class h

children.title: Policy-Projection Role
children.top_down_role: Policy-space coordination viewed through scenario-wise projection.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Projection Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted projection converts scenario-wise decisions into a nonanticipative policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be a finite scenario set with \(p_s>0\), let \(\mathcal T=\{0,\ldots,T\}\), and let each scenario policy be \(x_s=(x_{t,s})_{t\in\mathcal T}\) with \(x_{t,s}\in\mathbb R^{n_t}\). Equip the policy space with
\[\langle x,y\rangle_p=\sum_{s\in S}p_s\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\langle x_{t,s},y_{t,s}\rangle,\]
and let \(\mathcal N\) be the nonanticipative subspace. The policy projection is
\[P_{\mathcal N}^{p}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathcal N}\frac12\sum_{s\in S}p_s\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\lVert y_{t,s}-x_{t,s}\rVert^2.\]
For \(h=[s]_t\), its components are
\[\bigl(P_{\mathcal N}^{p}x\bigr)_{t,s}=\frac{\sum_{r\in h}p_r x_{t,r}}{\sum_{r\in h}p_r}.\]
Thus projection replaces the scenario copies in each history class by their probability-weighted average and produces the nearest nonanticipative policy in this metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Policy projection replaces decisions sharing a stage history by their probability-weighted average, yielding the unique nearest nonanticipative policy.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(\mathcal T\) are finite.
\(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
\(\mathcal N\) is the linear nonanticipative subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_{\mathcal N}^{p}x\in\mathcal N\) is the unique weighted least-squares nonanticipative approximation to \(x\).

notation.meaning: probability-weighted orthogonal projection onto the nonanticipative subspace
history class of scenario s at stage t
strictly positive probability of scenario s

children.title: Proximal-Regularization Role
children.top_down_role: Scenario coordination viewed through proximal stabilization.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Regularization Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The progressive-hedging scenario solve is a proximal augmented-Lagrangian block update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be finite with \(p_s>0\), let \(\mathcal N\) be the nonanticipative subspace in the probability-weighted policy space, and choose \(\rho>0\), \(z^0\in\mathcal N\), and \(w^0\in\mathcal N^{\perp_p}\). Given proper closed convex scenario functions \(f_s\), compute independently
\[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_s}\left\{f_s(x_s)+\langle w_s^k,x_s-z_s^k\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_s-z_s^k\rVert^2\right\}.\]
Equivalently,
\[x_s^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_s}\left\{f_s(x_s)+\frac{\rho}{2}\left\lVert x_s-\left(z_s^k-\frac{w_s^k}{\rho}\right)\right\rVert^2\right\}.\]
Then set
\[z^{k+1}=P_{\mathcal N}^{p}x^{k+1},\qquad w_s^{k+1}=w_s^k+\rho(x_s^{k+1}-z_s^{k+1}).\]
Because \(w^k\in\mathcal N^{\perp_p}\), the general consensus projection \(P_{\mathcal N}^{p}(x^{k+1}+w^k/\rho)\) equals \(P_{\mathcal N}^{p}x^{k+1}\). Thus each scenario solve is a proximal step centered at the dual-shifted policy \(z_s^k-w_s^k/\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario performs a proximal solve around a multiplier-shifted implementable policy; weighted projection then restores nonanticipativity and the multiplier update prices disagreement.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Every displayed scenario subproblem attains a minimizer.
\(z^0\in\mathcal N\) and \(w^0\in\mathcal N^{\perp_p}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scenario update is a proximal augmented-Lagrangian step centered at \(z_s^k-w_s^k/\rho\).

notation.meaning: weighted orthogonal complement of the nonanticipative subspace

children.title: Projection-Proximal Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Shared structural roles connecting policy projection with proximal regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Proximal Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric projection is exactly the proximal mapping of a closed convex set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be self-adjoint and positive definite on \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. With \(\delta_C\) denoting the indicator of \(C\),
\[\operatorname{prox}^{H}_{\delta_C}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\delta_C(y)+\frac12\lVert y-x\rVert_H^2\right\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\frac12\lVert y-x\rVert_H^2=P_C^H(x).\]
Consequently, the progressive-hedging policy-projection step is the proximal step for the nonanticipativity indicator in the probability-weighted metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty closed convex policy set equals the proximal mapping of that set's indicator in the same positive-definite metric.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(H\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}^{H}_{\delta_C}=P_C^H\), and in particular \(\operatorname{prox}^{p}_{\delta_{\mathcal N}}=P_{\mathcal N}^{p}\).

notation.meaning: quadratic metric induced by the positive-definite operator H

children.title: Projection-Proximal Scope Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Proximal Scope Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The projection-as-proximal identity depends on using the same indicator and metric, while existence and uniqueness require additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and positive-definite metric operator \(H\), the set-valued expressions
\[P_C^H(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in C}\frac12\lVert y-x\rVert_H^2\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{prox}_{\delta_C}^H(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\delta_C(y)+\frac12\lVert y-x\rVert_H^2\right\}\]
are identical because they define the same minimization problem. If \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, this common mapping is everywhere single-valued. Without convexity it may be multivalued; for \(C=\{-1,1\}\subset\mathbb R\), both mappings send \(0\) to \(\{-1,1\}\). Without closedness it may be empty; for \(C=(0,1)\) and \(x=0\), the infimum is not attained. If \(H\) is only positive semidefinite, uniqueness may fail even for closed convex \(C\). A projection generated by a different metric or by a nonquadratic Bregman divergence is generally not the same proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the same set indicator and quadratic metric makes projection and the proximal map identical as set-valued minimizers; closed convexity and a positive-definite metric additionally guarantee existence and uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: Projection and proximal regularization are compared on the same ambient space.
The indicator and projection use the same set \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The identity persists set-valuedly when the minimization problems match, while nonempty closed convex \(C\) and positive-definite \(H\) ensure an everywhere unique value; incompatible metrics define different mappings in general.

notation.meaning: quadratic metric operator used by both mappings

children.title: Information-Price Interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Price Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-scenario progressive hedging with nonanticipativity enforced through scenario prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be finite, let \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\), and let \(N\subseteq\prod_{s\in S}X_s\) be the nonanticipativity subspace. A vector \(w=(w_s)_{s\in S}\in N^{\perp}\) is an information-price system: each \(w_s\) prices the scenario copy's deviation from implementable information. For every information set \(I\) whose scenarios share a decision component, orthogonality gives \[\sum_{s\in I}p_s w_s=0.\] Thus prices redistribute incentives within each information set without changing the probability-weighted value of a common feasible decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information prices are dual variables for nonanticipativity; within every information set, their probability-weighted sum is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite and \(p_s>0\) for every \(s\in S\).
\(N\) is a linear nonanticipativity subspace of the probability-weighted product space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in N^{\perp}\Longrightarrow \sum_{s\in I}p_s w_s=0\) on every information set \(I\).

children.title: Dual-Consensus Interpretation

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Consensus Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-subspace formulation of nonanticipativity and its orthogonal dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the probability-weighted product Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\), impose nonanticipativity by \(x\in N\), equivalently by adding the indicator \(\delta_N(x)\). Its convex conjugate is \[\delta_N^*(w)=\delta_{N^{\perp}}(w).\] Hence the dual variable associated with consensus lies in \(N^{\perp}\). The primal projection residual \(x-P_Nx\in N^{\perp}\) is therefore a valid dual-consensus direction, while \(P_Nx\) is the closest nonanticipative decision in the chosen Hilbert metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity is primal consensus in a subspace, while its dual variables and projection residuals lie in the orthogonal complement.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(N\subseteq\mathcal H\) is a closed linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_N^*=\delta_{N^{\perp}}\), \(P_Nx\in N\), and \(x-P_Nx\in N^{\perp}\).

children.title: Price-Dual Mapping
children.top_down_role: Structural alignment between scenario information prices plus consensus dual quantities.

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Dual Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mapping between progressive-hedging prices and scaled or unscaled ADMM multipliers under explicitly matched updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(N\subseteq\mathcal H\) be a closed linear subspace, and consider the split constraint \(x-z=0\) with \(z\in N\) and penalty \(\rho>0\). Suppose the unscaled ADMM multiplier satisfies \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\), and define the progressive-hedging price by the same update \(w^{k+1}=w^k+\rho(x^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\) with \(w^0=y^0\). Then \[w^k=y^k=\rho u^k\] for every \(k\geq0\), where \(u^k=y^k/\rho\) is the scaled ADMM dual variable. If \(z^{k+1}=P_N(x^{k+1}+u^k)\) and \(u^0\in N^{\perp}\), then \(u^k\in N^{\perp}\) and \(z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1}\) for every \(k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the two methods use the same constraint orientation, residual update, penalty, and initial multiplier, the progressive-hedging price equals the unscaled ADMM multiplier and equals the scaled dual multiplied by the penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(N\subseteq\mathcal H\) is a closed linear subspace.
\(\rho>0\), and both methods use the constraint orientation \(x-z=0\) and the same residual multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w^k=y^k=\rho u^k\) and \(z^{k+1}=P_Nx^{k+1}\) for every \(k\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Dual Correspondence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which the price–dual identification changes or ceases to be literal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identity \(w=y=\rho u\) is convention-dependent. Reversing the split constraint from \(x-z=0\) to \(z-x=0\) changes the mapping to \(w=-y\). With iteration-dependent penalties \(\rho_k\), the unscaled relation remains \(w^k=y^k\), but \(w^k=\rho_k u^k\) requires rescaling the stored scaled dual whenever \(\rho_k\) changes. For a general constraint \(Ax+Bz=c\), multipliers act through \(A^*y\) in the scenario stationarity equations, so a scenario price is \(A^*y\), not necessarily \(y\) itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The price–dual identity depends on constraint orientation, scaling, and the constraint operator; outside identity consensus, prices may be adjoint-transformed multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The compared algorithms use equivalent primal subproblems and multiplier updates.
Adjoints are taken in the declared primal and dual metrics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w=y\) holds only for matched orientation, scaling, metric, and identity-form consensus conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Conditioning Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable-metric preconditioning of the consensus residual in scenario splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) be bounded, self-adjoint, and uniformly positive definite. Replacing the Euclidean quadratic by \[\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x-z\rVert_M^2=\frac{\rho}{2}\langle M(x-z),x-z\rangle\] changes the geometry of the proximal and projection steps. If \(mI\preceq M\preceq LI\), then \[\rho m\lVert r\rVert^2\leq \rho\lVert r\rVert_M^2\leq \rho L\lVert r\rVert^2.\] Thus \(M\) supplies directional conditioning while preserving the zero-residual set \(x=z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric weights residual directions differently, improving or worsening conditioning without changing the consensus solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(M=M^*\) and \(0<mI\preceq M\preceq LI\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert r\rVert_M=0\iff r=0\), with spectral bounds \(m\lVert r\rVert^2\leq\lVert r\rVert_M^2\leq L\lVert r\rVert^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Penalty Conditioning Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar penalty control of primal regularization and dual response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed metric \(M\succ0\), the penalty \(\rho>0\) multiplies every residual direction uniformly. The augmented-Lagrangian curvature contributed in the residual coordinates is \(\rho M\), and the unscaled multiplier update is \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho M r^{k+1}.\] Increasing \(\rho\) strengthens primal agreement regularization and amplifies the unscaled dual response to the same residual; decreasing it has the opposite effect. The feasible set and exact saddle points are unchanged when only \(\rho\) changes, although iteration trajectories and numerical conditioning generally change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar penalty uniformly controls consensus curvature and multiplier response, affecting trajectories but not the exact feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is fixed, self-adjoint, and positive definite.
An exact augmented-Lagrangian formulation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty curvature is \(\rho M\), while \(\{r:r=0\}\) is independent of \(\rho\).

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Penalty Scaling Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence class of metric and penalty pairs with identical quadratic weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(\alpha>0\), define \(\widetilde M=\alpha M\) and \(\widetilde\rho=\rho/\alpha\). Then \[\widetilde\rho\,\widetilde M=\rho M\] and, for every residual \(r\), \[\frac{\widetilde\rho}{2}\lVert r\rVert_{\widetilde M}^2=\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert r\rVert_M^2.\] Consequently, algorithms whose proximal, projection, and unscaled multiplier updates depend only on the product \(\rho M\) generate identical primal and unscaled-dual iterates from identical initial states. Scaled-dual coordinates must be transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocally scaling the metric and scalar penalty preserves their product and hence preserves methods depending only on that product.
assumptions_latex: \(M\succ0\), \(\rho>0\), and \(\alpha>0\).
All metric-dependent algorithmic operations use only \(\rho M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M,\rho)\sim(\alpha M,\rho/\alpha)\) whenever the algorithm depends only on \(\rho M\).

children.title: Conditioning Correspondence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where metric scaling does not translate cleanly into penalty behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Correspondence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of treating metric choice and scalar penalty choice as interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar penalty cannot reproduce an anisotropic metric unless the metric is proportional to the identity on the residual space. Indeed, if \(\rho M=\widehat\rho I\), then necessarily \(M=(\widehat\rho/\rho)I\). Moreover, reciprocal scaling preserves iterates only when every affected operation depends on \(\rho M\); separate use of \(M\), adaptive rules for \(\rho\), inexact stopping tests, or metric-dependent adjoints can break the correspondence. If \(M\) is singular, \(\lVert r\rVert_M=0\) may hold for nonzero residuals, so the penalized zero set need not equal consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar penalties cannot mimic directional metrics, and equivalence fails under separate parameter use or singular metrics.
assumptions_latex: The residual space has dimension at least two.
\(\rho>0\) and \(\widehat\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric–penalty interchangeability requires proportional metrics and consistent use of the product \(\rho M\).

notation.meaning: residual metric, possibly singular at the boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Pathwise Operator Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-sum representation with one local operator block per root-to-leaf scenario path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite set of root-to-leaf paths. For each \(p\in\mathcal P\), let \(X_p\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(\pi_p>0\), and let \(f_p:X_p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Equip \(X=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}X_p\) with its standard product Hilbert structure and define \(F(x)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\pi_p f_p(x_p)\). Then \[\partial F(x)=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}\pi_p\partial f_p(x_p).\] Thus \(A=\partial F\) is the direct sum \(A=\bigoplus_{p\in\mathcal P}A_p\), where \(A_p=\pi_p\partial f_p\), and its resolvent acts pathwise as \[J_A(x)=\bigl(J_{A_p}(x_p)\bigr)_{p\in\mathcal P}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the standard product of the path Hilbert spaces, a finite separable convex objective has a direct-sum subdifferential whose resolvent is evaluated independently on each path.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is finite, each \(X_p\) is a real Hilbert space, and \(X=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}X_p\) has the standard product inner product.
\(\pi_p>0\) for every \(p\in\mathcal P\).
Each \(f_p:X_p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigoplus_{p\in\mathcal P}A_p\) and \(J_A(x)=\bigl(J_{A_p}(x_p)\bigr)_{p\in\mathcal P}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle Operator Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct-sum representation obtained by grouping scenario paths into disjoint bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak B\) be a partition of the finite path set \(\mathcal P\). For each bundle \(B\in\mathfrak B\), define \(X_B=\prod_{p\in B}X_p\) and \(A_B=\bigoplus_{p\in B}A_p\). Then the pathwise operator can be regrouped as \[A=\bigoplus_{B\in\mathfrak B}A_B.\] Consequently, \(J_A=\prod_{B\in\mathfrak B}J_{A_B}\), so the bundle blocks can be processed independently whenever no represented objective or constraint term couples distinct bundles. Internal bundle blocks may be evaluated jointly without changing the represented operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partition of scenario paths regroups path operators into independent bundle blocks, provided no represented model term couples distinct bundles.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak B\) is a disjoint partition of the finite set \(\mathcal P\).
\(A=\bigoplus_{p\in\mathcal P}A_p\), and no represented operator term couples paths in distinct bundles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigoplus_{B\in\mathfrak B}A_B\) with \(A_B=\bigoplus_{p\in B}A_p\).

children.title: Path-Bundle Granularity Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coordination, locality, plus block-size consequences of choosing path or bundle granularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-Bundle Granularity Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural tradeoff between block parallelism and within-block coupling under path bundling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak B\) be a partition of the path set \(\mathcal P\), and let \(c(B)\geq0\) denote the cost of evaluating the resolvent for bundle \(B\in\mathfrak B\) under a fixed implementation. If all bundle evaluations can run concurrently with enough processors and communication overhead is ignored, one block sweep has idealized critical-path cost \[T_{\mathrm{par}}(\mathfrak B)=\max_{B\in\mathfrak B}c(B),\] while its total local work is \[T_{\mathrm{work}}(\mathfrak B)=\sum_{B\in\mathfrak B}c(B).\] Finer partitions expose more independent tasks and use smaller blocks, whereas coarser partitions permit joint treatment of more within-bundle coupling and may reduce coordination. No granularity uniformly dominates because local solution costs and coordination overhead are model- and implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fine bundles expose more parallel tasks, while coarse bundles internalize more coupling. Under the idealized model, parallel cost is the largest bundle cost and total work is the sum of bundle costs, so no granularity is uniformly best.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathfrak B\) is a disjoint partition whose bundle blocks can be processed independently.
\(c(B)\geq0\) is the cost of one bundle-resolvent evaluation under a fixed implementation.
The critical-path formula assumes enough processors and ignores communication and scheduling overhead.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{par}}(\mathfrak B)=\max_{B\in\mathfrak B}c(B)\) and \(T_{\mathrm{work}}(\mathfrak B)=\sum_{B\in\mathfrak B}c(B)\), with no model-independent optimal granularity.

notation.meaning: computational cost of evaluating bundle B

children.title: Bundle-Formation Sensitivity

knowledge_statements.title: Bundle-Formation Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of exact block separability and computational balance on the selected path partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak B\) be a partition of the finite path set \(\mathcal P\), and let \(G=(\mathcal P,E)\) be the coupling graph in which \((p,q)\in E\) whenever an unsplit represented operator term depends jointly on \(x_p\) and \(x_q\). Exact bundle separability requires every coupling edge to lie within a bundle: \[(p,q)\in E\Longrightarrow\exists B\in\mathfrak B\text{ such that }\{p,q\}\subseteq B.\] If an edge crosses two bundles, the asserted direct-sum representation fails unless the crossing term is separately split or dualized. Even a valid partition can be computationally sensitive because unequal bundle costs create load imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bundle partition is exactly separable only when every unsplit pairwise coupling lies within one bundle; a crossing coupling requires an additional representation such as splitting or dualization.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(\mathcal P,E)\) records every unsplit pairwise cross-path coupling in the represented operator.
\(\mathfrak B\) is a disjoint partition of \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A coupling edge crossing two members of \(\mathfrak B\) invalidates \(A=\bigoplus_{B\in\mathfrak B}A_B\) unless the crossing term is represented separately.

notation.meaning: set of unsplit pairwise coupling edges

knowledge_statements.title: History-Node Operator Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block representation on a finite scenario-tree product space indexed by information histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H\) be the history nodes of a finite scenario tree and let \(X=\bigoplus_{h\in\mathcal H}X_h\). Denote the canonical injection and projection by \(I_h:X_h\to X\) and \(P_h:X\to X_h\). Every bounded linear operator \(L:X\to X\) has history-node blocks \(L_{hk}=P_hLI_k\) and the representation
\[
Lx=\sum_{h\in\mathcal H}I_h\!\left(\sum_{k\in\mathcal H}L_{hk}x_k\right).
\]
It is history-node block diagonal precisely when \(L_{hk}=0\) for all \(h\ne k\); then each block can be evaluated using only variables attached to its information node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scenario-tree operator decomposes into blocks mapping variables between history nodes; block diagonality means every node can evaluate its block locally.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is finite.
\(X_h\) are Hilbert spaces.
\(L:X\to X\) is bounded and linear.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=(L_{hk})_{h,k\in\mathcal H}\), where \(L_{hk}=P_hLI_k\).

canonical injection and projection for node h

children.title: Nonanticipative-Subspace Operators
children.top_down_role: Operator representations of information-consistency geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonanticipative-Subspace Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted projection and normal-cone operators for information-consistent scenario decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be the leaves of a finite scenario tree with probabilities \(p_s>0\), and let \(h_t(s)\) denote the history of leaf \(s\) at stage \(t\). In the weighted product space, the nonanticipative subspace is
\[
N=\{x:x_{s,t}=x_{s',t}\text{ whenever }h_t(s)=h_t(s')\}.
\]
Its orthogonal projector averages scenario copies within each history class:
\[
(P_Nx)_{s,t}=\frac{\sum_{r:h_t(r)=h_t(s)}p_r x_{r,t}}{\sum_{r:h_t(r)=h_t(s)}p_r}.
\]
Moreover, the normal-cone operator satisfies \(N_N(x)=N^\perp\) for \(x\in N\) and \(N_N(x)=\varnothing\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonanticipativity is a linear subspace; its projector averages decisions sharing a history, and its normal cone represents consistency multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and the stage set are finite.
\(p_s>0\) and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
Scenario copies at a fixed stage share a common Hilbert decision space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_N\) is weighted history-class averaging, and \(N_N(x)=N^\perp\) on \(N\).

notation.meaning: history node reached by scenario s at stage t

children.title: Scenario-Wise versus Stage-Wise Orientation
children.top_down_role: Selection between path-oriented coordination and recourse-stage master decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Scenario-Wise versus Stage-Wise Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural selection rule for path decomposition versus recursive recourse decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a finite multistage stochastic convex program. A scenario-wise orientation is structurally compatible when its objective and local constraints admit \(F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sF_s(x_s)\) and the cross-scenario restriction is \(x\in N\), because fixing coordination variables separates the leaf problems. A stage-wise orientation is structurally compatible when the continuation problem depends on the past through a state \(u_t\) and admits the recursion
\[
Q_t(u_t)=\mathbb E\!\left[\inf_{x_t\in C_t(u_t,\xi_t)}\{f_t(x_t,\xi_t)+Q_{t+1}(T_t(x_t,\xi_t))\}\mid u_t\right].
\]
Choose the orientation whose interface—history consensus or state value function—has the smaller tractable representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use scenario-wise splitting for path-separable models with nonanticipativity coupling; use stage-wise decomposition when low-dimensional states support tractable recourse recursion.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and horizon are finite.
All displayed infima and conditional expectations are well-defined.
Local feasible sets and costs are convex in decision variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scenario-wise decomposition exposes \(N\); stage-wise decomposition exposes the recourse functions \(Q_t\).

notation.meaning: state summarizing information relevant to future recourse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the container, but no source is cited. The displayed conditional recourse recursion and the asserted selection criterion depend on information structure, measurability, state sufficiency, and interchange conditions that cannot be validated from the record alone.

children.title: Consensus versus Sharing Orientation
children.top_down_role: Selection between agreement coupling and aggregate-resource coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus versus Sharing Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic selection rule distinguishing replicated-variable agreement from aggregate-resource coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For separable convex functions \(f_i\), consensus orientation applies to
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_i=z\ \text{for every }i,
\]
so coordination acts on disagreement among replicated copies. Sharing orientation applies to
\[
\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m}\ \sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^m B_ix_i=b,
\]
so coordination acts on an aggregate resource residual. The formulation should be classified by its coupling equation: equality of copies selects consensus splitting, whereas a summed linear image selects sharing splitting. Either form may be converted to the other by introducing auxiliary variables, but this can enlarge the interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consensus coordinates equal local copies; sharing coordinates an aggregate constraint. Auxiliary reformulations can exchange the forms but may increase coupling dimension.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The displayed coupling constraints are feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Use consensus for \(x_i=z\) coupling and sharing for \(\sum_iB_ix_i=b\) coupling.

notation.meaning: local contribution to the aggregate coupling map

children.title: Coupling-Dimension Burden

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Dimension Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-round storage and arithmetic burden induced by a dense linear coupling interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(m\) blocks coupled by \(\sum_{i=1}^mB_ix_i=b\in\mathbb R^q\), where \(B_i\in\mathbb R^{q\times n_i}\). In a dense arithmetic model, explicitly forming the coupling residual requires at most
\[
\sum_{i=1}^m O(qn_i)
\]
scalar operations and storing an unrestricted interface multiplier requires \(O(q)\) scalars. If only \(r=\operatorname{rank}[B_1\ \cdots\ B_m]\) independent coupling directions are retained, an equivalent reduced interface uses \(O(r)\) multiplier storage and residual dimension \(r\). Thus raw row dimension governs an unreduced implementation, whereas rank governs its minimal linear interface dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense unreduced coupling uses a q-dimensional residual and multiplier; rank compression reduces the independent interface dimension to rank r.
assumptions_latex: All spaces are finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
Dense matrix-vector multiplication is used.
Redundant coupling equations are consistent with \(b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unreduced residual cost is \(O(\sum_i qn_i)\), while the minimal independent interface dimension is \(r=\operatorname{rank}B\).

notation.meaning: rank of the aggregate coupling matrix

children.title: Coupling-Rank Structure
children.top_down_role: Selection implications of full-rank, deficient-rank, or redundant coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Rank Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-revealing reduction of a linear coupling interface to independent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B=[B_1\ \cdots\ B_m]\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{q\times r}\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}B\). If \(b\in\operatorname{range}B\), then
\[
Bx=b\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U^{\mathsf T}Bx=U^{\mathsf T}b.
\]
Hence \(U^{\mathsf T}B\) supplies exactly \(r\) independent coupling equations. Any multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^q\) decomposes as \(y=UU^{\mathsf T}y+(I-UU^{\mathsf T})y\), and the second component satisfies \(B^{\mathsf T}(I-UU^{\mathsf T})y=0\); it therefore has no effect on stationarity through the coupling map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthonormal basis of the coupling range reduces the constraints to rank-many equations; multipliers orthogonal to that range do not affect stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is a finite-dimensional real matrix.
\(b\in\operatorname{range}B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Bx=b\) is equivalently represented by \(U^{\mathsf T}Bx=U^{\mathsf T}b\) in \(\mathbb R^r\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis matrix for the range of B
orthogonal projector onto the range of B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral condition number of the coupling Schur operator on its effective range.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\). The interface Schur operator is \(S=BH^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\). On its effective space \(\operatorname{range}B\), define
\[
\kappa_{\mathrm{int}}=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(S|_{\operatorname{range}B})}{\lambda_{\min}^{+}(S|_{\operatorname{range}B})},
\]
where \(\lambda_{\min}^{+}\) is the smallest positive eigenvalue. The interface is spectrally well-conditioned at level \(K\ge1\) exactly when \(\kappa_{\mathrm{int}}\le K\). Equivalently, all nonzero singular values of \(BH^{-1/2}\) lie in an interval \([\alpha,\beta]\) with \((\beta/\alpha)^2\le K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interface conditioning is the positive spectral condition number of the Schur operator, equivalently the squared singular-value ratio of the scaled coupling map.

children.title: Dimension-Conditioning Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Conditioning Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface compression and preconditioning address distinct geometric costs of coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a coupling matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\) of rank \(r\), orthogonal compression by a range basis \(U\in\mathbb R^{q\times r}\) replaces \(Bx=b\) by \(U^{\mathsf T}Bx=U^{\mathsf T}b\), reducing interface dimension from \(q\) to \(r\) without changing the positive singular values of \(B\). An invertible row scaling \(D\) preserves feasibility through \(DBx=Db\) but can change the positive singular-value ratio and hence the conditioning of the coordination operator. Interface design should therefore first remove redundant directions and then select scaling or a metric to control conditioning; minimizing dimension alone does not guarantee favorable conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank compression removes redundant coordinates without harming nonzero singular values; scaling preserves feasibility but changes conditioning, so both goals require separate design choices.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}B\).
\(D\) is invertible on the coupling space.
\(b\in\operatorname{range}B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compression controls interface dimension, whereas row scaling or metric selection controls its spectral conditioning.

notation.meaning: orthonormal range basis used for compression

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose coordination round \(k\) invokes local solver \(i\) to tolerance \(\varepsilon_{i,k}\), requiring at most \(C_i(\varepsilon_{i,k})\) elementary operations. With serial execution, the local-solve work per round is bounded by
\[
W_k^{\mathrm{ser}}\le\sum_{i=1}^m C_i(\varepsilon_{i,k}).
\]
With one unit-rate processor per block, no contention, and negligible launch overhead, the normalized local-solve wall time is bounded by
\[
T_k^{\mathrm{par}}\le\max_{1\le i\le m}C_i(\varepsilon_{i,k}).
\]
Communication, synchronization, and coordinator work must be added separately; they are not included in these local-solver bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Per-round local work sums under serial execution, while normalized wall time is governed by the slowest block under ideal unit-rate parallel execution; communication costs are additional.

children.title: Local-Solver Accuracy
children.top_down_role: Quality levels for exact or inexact local subproblem resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Solver Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for an approximate local convex subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For local block \(i\), let \(A_i\) be a maximal monotone operator and let the current coordination data define \(v_{i,k}\). A computed point \(x_{i,k}\) is an \(\varepsilon_{i,k}\)-accurate local solution when there exists a residual \(e_{i,k}\) such that
\[
v_{i,k}-x_{i,k}-e_{i,k}\in A_i(x_{i,k}),\qquad \|e_{i,k}\|\le\varepsilon_{i,k}.
\]
Equivalently, \(x_{i,k}\) is an inexact evaluation of the resolvent \(J_{A_i}=(I+A_i)^{-1}\). The pair \((x_{i,k},e_{i,k})\) is directly checkable whenever membership in the graph of \(A_i\) is checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local solve is certified by a bounded residual in its monotone inclusion, equivalently by an inexact resolvent evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\) is maximal monotone on a Hilbert space.
The graph-membership test for \(A_i\) is available.
\(\varepsilon_{i,k}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|e_{i,k}\|\le\varepsilon_{i,k}\) certifies the stated inexact resolvent evaluation.

children.title: Effort-Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Method-selection implications of exchanging local computational effort for solution accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Effort-Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-work criterion for choosing local tolerances across coordination rounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K(\delta;\varepsilon)\) be the number of coordination rounds required to reach global accuracy \(\delta\) under a local tolerance schedule \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_{i,k})\). With serial local execution, choose the schedule by the total-work criterion
\[
\min_{\varepsilon}\ \sum_{k=0}^{K(\delta;\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{i=1}^m C_i(\varepsilon_{i,k}),
\]
subject to the inexactness condition required by the outer method. For outer iterations stable under summable errors, \(\sum_k\max_i\varepsilon_{i,k}<\infty\) is an admissible accuracy condition. Solving local problems more accurately is justified only when its reduction of coordination rounds or terminal error offsets the increased local cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose local tolerances to minimize total work, while satisfying the outer method’s error condition; excessive local accuracy can waste computation.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i(\varepsilon)\) is nonincreasing as tolerance \(\varepsilon\) increases.
The outer method has a specified inexactness condition.
\(K(\delta;\varepsilon)\) is finite for admissible schedules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An admissible tolerance schedule should minimize cumulative local cost rather than per-round error alone.

notation.meaning: coordination rounds needed for global accuracy delta
local tolerance for block i in round k

children.title: Coordination-Frequency Consequences
children.top_down_role: Effects of local solve quality on the required frequency of global coordination.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination-Frequency Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error propagation and communication count under periodic inexact coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose one exact coordination step is contractive about a solution \(z^\star\) with factor \(q\in(0,1)\), while round \(k\) incurs aggregate local error \(\eta_k\ge0\). If
\[
\|z^{k+1}-z^\star\|\le q\|z^k-z^\star\|+\eta_k,
\]
then after \(K\) coordination rounds,
\[
\|z^K-z^\star\|\le q^K\|z^0-z^\star\|+\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}q^{K-1-j}\eta_j.
\]
If coordination occurs once every \(\tau\) local-update sweeps, \(K\) rounds entail \(K\tau\) sweeps and \(K\) communication events. Increasing \(\tau\) reduces communication per sweep but is beneficial only if the induced errors do not negate the saved rounds or messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Less frequent coordination reduces messages per local sweep but can enlarge accumulated disagreement; a contraction recurrence quantifies the resulting error.
assumptions_latex: The exact coordination map is contractive with factor \(q\in(0,1)\).
Each inexact round has bounded aggregate error \(\eta_k\).
Coordination occurs periodically every \(\tau\ge1\) local sweeps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The terminal error is bounded by \(q^K\|z^0-z^\star\|+\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}q^{K-1-j}\eta_j\), with \(K\) communications over \(K\tau\) sweeps.

notation.meaning: aggregate error introduced in coordination round k
number of local sweeps between coordination events

children.title: Distributed-Execution Constraint Taxonomy

children.title: Compute-Architecture Constraints
children.top_down_role: Decomposition restrictions arising from processor organization, memory locality, or accelerator access.

knowledge_statements.title: Compute-Architecture Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worker eligibility, memory, and load conditions for assigning scenario subproblems to heterogeneous compute resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let scenario set \(S\) be assigned to workers \(W\) by binary variables \(z_{sw}\). Worker \(w\) has memory capacity \(M_w\), processing budget \(C_w\), and eligibility set \(E_w\subseteq S\); scenario \(s\) requires memory \(m_s\) and work \(c_s\). The assignment is compute-architecture feasible exactly when
\[\sum_{w\in W}z_{sw}=1,\qquad z_{sw}=0\ \text{if }s\notin E_w,\qquad \sum_{s\in S}m_sz_{sw}\le M_w,\qquad \sum_{s\in S}c_sz_{sw}\le C_w\]
for every \(s\in S\) and \(w\in W\). Replication, when required, replaces the first equality by the prescribed replication count and charges every replica against its worker capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each scenario must be assigned only to eligible workers, with every worker respecting its memory and computational budgets; required replicas consume capacity separately.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) and \(W\) are finite.
\(m_s,c_s,M_w,C_w\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[z\ \text{is feasible precisely when all assignment, eligibility, memory, and processing inequalities hold.}\]

notation.meaning: Indicator that worker w executes scenario s.
Memory and processing capacities of worker w.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite assignment and capacity constraints are the standard mathematical model for heterogeneous task placement
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the asserted architecture-feasibility model and replication convention require a direct distributed-decomposition or heterogeneous-scheduling source.

children.title: Communication-Topology Constraints
children.top_down_role: Decomposition restrictions arising from network connectivity, bandwidth, or routing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Topology Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity and capacity conditions for transmitting quantities coupled by scenario-consensus constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(W,E)\) be the directed communication graph and let \(D\subseteq W\times W\) contain every worker pair that must exchange data during one decomposition iteration. For each \((i,j)\in D\), choose a directed path \(P_{ij}\) in \(G\), and let \(b_{ij}\ge0\) be its required traffic. Given link capacities \(B_e\), the communication topology is feasible when every required pair has such a path and
\[\sum_{(i,j)\in D:\,e\in P_{ij}}b_{ij}\le B_e\qquad(e\in E).\]
If direct neighbor-only averaging is used, feasibility additionally requires the induced worker graph on each coupled scenario group to be connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every required data exchange must have a route, link traffic must remain within capacity, and neighbor-only consensus groups must induce connected worker subgraphs.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(D\) are finite.
Communication routes remain fixed during the iteration under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{All coupling messages are routable without exceeding any link capacity.}\]

notation.meaning: Route selected for exchange from i to j.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multicommodity routing and connected-subgraph conditions are standard communication-feasibility predicates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Routing capacity is standard, but the required connectivity notion for directed neighbor-only averaging depends on the consensus protocol and cannot be validated from the supplied rationale alone.

children.title: Synchronization Constraints
children.top_down_role: Method-selection effects of barriers, coordination cadence, plus asynchronous execution support.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay and fairness requirements for asynchronous scenario-block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Index accepted block updates by \(k\). If worker \(w\) updates at index \(k\), let \(d_{wv}(k)\le k\) be the version of worker \(v\)'s state read by \(w\). Execution satisfies bounded asynchronous synchronization with delay \(\tau\in\mathbb N\) when
\[0\le k-d_{wv}(k)\le\tau\]
for every state actually read, and when every worker performs at least one accepted update in each window \(\{k,k+1,\ldots,k+L-1\}\) for some finite \(L\). A barrier-synchronous execution is the special case \(\tau=0\) in which all workers complete iteration \(k\) before any begins iteration \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asynchronous reads may be stale only by a bounded amount, every worker must update within each finite window, and barrier synchronization corresponds to zero delay.
assumptions_latex: Accepted updates admit a common logical ordering.
\(\tau\) and \(L\) are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{No consumed state is older than }\tau\text{ updates, and no worker is indefinitely starved.}\]

notation.meaning: Version of v's state read by w at logical update k.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded staleness and essentially cyclic activation are standard asynchronous-iteration assumptions
convergence implications depend on the selected decomposition method
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-delay and fairness assumptions fit the leaf, but their precise indexing and the characterization of barrier execution require a source tied to the asynchronous iteration model.

children.title: Failure-Tolerance Constraints
children.top_down_role: Method-selection effects of participant loss, unreliable links, or intermittent availability.

knowledge_statements.title: Failure-Tolerance Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crash-failure survivability conditions for replicated scenario state and post-failure communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose at most \(f\) workers may crash, each scenario state has a checkpointed replica set \(R_s\subseteq W\), and \(G[W\setminus F]\) denotes the surviving communication graph after failures \(F\). The execution architecture is \(f\)-crash-tolerant for scenario recovery when, for every \(F\subseteq W\) with \(|F|\le f\),
\[R_s\setminus F\ne\varnothing\quad(s\in S),\qquad G[W\setminus F]\ \text{connects every surviving worker pair required by the coupling interface}.\]
The first condition is ensured by \(|R_s|\ge f+1\). Recovery additionally requires that a surviving replica contain either the latest committed state or a checkpoint from which omitted updates can be replayed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After any allowed crash set, each scenario must retain recoverable state and all surviving workers required for coupling must remain mutually reachable.
assumptions_latex: Failures are crash-stop and satisfy \(|F|\le f\).
Checkpoint or replay metadata is stored with each counted replica.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{Every scenario state remains recoverable and every required surviving exchange remains possible.}\]

notation.meaning: Workers storing recoverable replicas of scenario s.
Communication graph induced by surviving workers.

fault model and recovery protocol require chapter-specific sourcing

children.title: Decomposition Assurance Requirement System

children.title: Certificate Requirements
children.top_down_role: Method-selection needs associated with residual, gap, or bound-based evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori primal-dual certificate for convex scenario decomposition with linear nonanticipativity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and \(K\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(X\subseteq H\) be nonempty and convex, let \(F:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and convex, and let \(A:H\to K\) be linear. Define \(p^*=\inf\{F(x):x\in X,\ Ax=0\}\) and, for \(y\in K\),
\[q(y)=\inf_{z\in X}\bigl(F(z)+\langle y,Az\rangle\bigr).\]
For declared tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\rm feas},\varepsilon_{\rm gap}\ge0\), a pair \((x,y)\in H\times K\) is an \((\varepsilon_{\rm feas},\varepsilon_{\rm gap})\)-certificate when \(x\in X\cap\operatorname{dom}F\), \(\|Ax\|\le\varepsilon_{\rm feas}\), \(q(y)>-\infty\), and
\[F(x)-q(y)\le\varepsilon_{\rm gap}.\]
The certificate is independently checkable when local membership and objective terms, the aggregate \(Ax\), and the dual lower bound \(q(y)\) can be evaluated or rigorously bounded. If \(\varepsilon_{\rm feas}=0\), weak duality yields \(q(y)\le p^*\le F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate provides a locally admissible policy, a bounded coupling residual, and a valid dual lower bound whose difference from the reported objective does not exceed the declared gap tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(K\) are finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces.
\(X\) is nonempty and convex, \(F\) is proper and convex, and \(A:H\to K\) is linear.
\(\varepsilon_{\rm feas},\varepsilon_{\rm gap}\ge0\), and \(q(y)\) can be evaluated or rigorously lower-bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|Ax\|\le\varepsilon_{\rm feas},\qquad F(x)-q(y)\le\varepsilon_{\rm gap}.\]

notation.meaning: Lagrangian dual lower-bound function for multiplier y.
Nonnegative feasibility and primal-dual gap tolerances.

children.title: Convergence-Guarantee Requirements
children.top_down_role: Method-selection needs associated with the required strength or applicability of convergence claims.

knowledge_statements.title: Convergence-Guarantee Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum global convergence contract for a scenario-decomposition method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex problem \(p^*=\inf\{F(x):x\in X,\ Ax=0\}\) with nonempty solution set \(X^*\), a decomposition method satisfies the global convergence requirement if every admissible initialization and execution allowed by its synchronization model generate iterates \(x^k\) such that
\[\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^*)\to0,\qquad \|Ax^k\|\to0,\qquad F(x^k)\to p^*.\]
If the method claims an ergodic or expected guarantee, the reported contract must replace \(x^k\) by the declared averaged iterate or place the declared quantities under expectation. Any rate claim must identify the residual, the iterate convention, and constants independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An acceptable guarantee must specify which iterates converge, drive coupling violations to zero, attain the optimal value, and state whether conclusions are pointwise, ergodic, or expected.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and convex, and \(X^*\ne\varnothing\).
The execution obeys the method's stated synchronization and error assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{dist}(x^k,X^*)\to0,\quad \|Ax^k\|\to0,\quad F(x^k)\to p^*.\]

children.title: Policy-Feasibility Requirements
children.top_down_role: Method-selection needs associated with nonanticipative or implementable policy outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Policy-Feasibility Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local admissibility and nonanticipativity requirements for policies represented on a finite scenario tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be the leaves of a finite scenario tree, and let \(h_t(s)\) denote the node reached by scenario \(s\) at decision stage \(t\). A scenario-indexed policy \(x=(x_{s,t})\) is feasible exactly when
\[x_s\in X_s\quad(s\in S),\qquad x_{s,t}=x_{s',t}\quad\text{whenever }h_t(s)=h_t(s').\]
The first predicate enforces every scenario's deterministic dynamics, control restrictions, and boundary conditions. The second is nonanticipativity: decisions made before scenarios separate depend only on the observed history. Equivalently, after stacking all scenario decisions, policy feasibility is \(x\in\prod_{s\in S}X_s\) and \(Ax=0\) for a node-incidence nonanticipativity operator \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible policy satisfies every scenario's local constraints and assigns identical stage decisions to scenarios sharing the same observed history.
assumptions_latex: The scenario tree and its stage-node map \(h_t\) are fixed.
Each \(X_s\) contains the complete local constraints for scenario \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x\in\prod_{s\in S}X_s\quad\text{and}\quad Ax=0.\]

notation.meaning: History node of scenario s at stage t.
Locally feasible policy set for scenario s.

children.title: Requirement-Driven Method Selection
children.top_down_role: Decomposition choices shaped by the combined evidentiary, feasibility, plus guarantee requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Requirement-Driven Method Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of a decomposition method by assurance predicates before performance ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a finite set of candidate methods. For each mandatory requirement \(j\in J\), let \(R_j(m)\in\{0,1\}\) state whether method \(m\) satisfies the required certificate, convergence, policy-feasibility, architecture, communication, synchronization, and failure model. Define the eligible set
\[\mathcal M_{\rm elig}=\{m\in\mathcal M:R_j(m)=1\ \text{for every }j\in J\}.\]
Requirement-driven selection first rejects every method outside \(\mathcal M_{\rm elig}\), then chooses
\[m^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\in\mathcal M_{\rm elig}} C(m),\]
where \(C\) is a declared resource or performance criterion. If \(\mathcal M_{\rm elig}=\varnothing\), the requirements are incompatible with the candidate set and no method may be selected without relaxing an identified requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter methods by all mandatory assurance and execution requirements, then optimize performance only among eligible methods; an empty eligible set requires explicit requirement revision.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) and \(J\) are finite.
Every predicate \(R_j\) is evaluated under the same problem and execution model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[m^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{m\in\mathcal M:\,R_j(m)=1\ \forall j\in J}C(m),\]
provided the feasible method set is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Indicator that method m meets mandatory requirement j.

performance criterion and mandatory requirement set are application-dependent

children.title: Decomposition-Specific Operator Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition-Specific Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus-ADMM representation exposing scenario-local proximal maps and the nonanticipativity projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\) be finite, let each \(H_s\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, and equip \(H=\prod_{s\in S}H_s\) with its declared product inner product. Let \(F:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be defined by \(F(x)=\sum_{s\in S}p_sf_s(x_s)\), where \(p_s>0\), and let \(A:H\to K\) be linear with nonanticipative subspace \(N=\ker A\). The problem \(\min_{x\in H}F(x)+\delta_N(x)\) is equivalently
\[\min_{x,z\in H}F(x)+\delta_N(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad x=z.\]
For \(\rho>0\), its scaled ADMM interface is
\[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{F/\rho}(z^k-u^k),\qquad z^{k+1}=\Pi_N(x^{k+1}+u^k),\qquad u^{k+1}=u^k+x^{k+1}-z^{k+1}.\]
The first map separates into the scenario maps \(\operatorname{prox}_{p_sf_s/\rho}\), while \(\Pi_N\) is the orthogonal projection, in the declared product inner product, onto the scenario-tree nonanticipativity subspace. The vector \(\rho u^k\) is the multiplier estimate for \(x=z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the declared product Hilbert space, consensus ADMM alternates separable scenario proximal solves, orthogonal projection onto the nonanticipative subspace, and a scaled multiplier update.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is finite, and every \(H_s\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
Each \(f_s\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(p_s>0\), and \(\sum_{s\in S}p_s=1\).
\(A:H\to K\) is linear, \(N=\ker A\), and \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{The scenario interface consists of }\operatorname{prox}_{F/\rho},\ \Pi_N,\ \text{and the scaled multiplier update.}\]

notation.meaning: Product space of scenario decision blocks with a declared product inner product.
Orthogonal projection onto N in the declared product inner product.
Scaled multiplier for the consensus equality.

children.title: Delegated General Splitting Theory

knowledge_statements.title: Delegated General Splitting Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary contract importing general Douglas–Rachford fixed-point theory without redeveloping it in this chapter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P,Q\) be maximal monotone operators on a real Hilbert space and \(\gamma>0\). With resolvents \(J_{\gamma P}=(I+\gamma P)^{-1}\) and \(J_{\gamma Q}=(I+\gamma Q)^{-1}\), define
\[T_{\rm DR}=I-J_{\gamma Q}+J_{\gamma P}(2J_{\gamma Q}-I).\]
The general splitting interface supplies the equivalence
\[z\in\operatorname{Fix}(T_{\rm DR})\quad\Longrightarrow\quad J_{\gamma Q}z\in\operatorname{zer}(P+Q),\]
with the converse fixed-point construction when \(\operatorname{zer}(P+Q)\ne\varnothing\). Scenario decomposition identifies its local and coupling operators with \(P\) and \(Q\); maximality, averagedness, fixed-point convergence, and general primal-dual variants remain delegated to the general splitting theory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The chapter imports the resolvent fixed-point contract, while general monotone-operator convergence theory remains outside its decomposition-specific scope.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[J_{\gamma Q}\bigl(\operatorname{Fix}(T_{\rm DR})\bigr)=\operatorname{zer}(P+Q)\]
whenever the zero set is nonempty.

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the scaled operator gamma P.
